kuWcVe9WV4.key_idea: Compute a safe-versus-unsafe direction in a source LLM, map it into the target text-encoder space with a benign-only learned alignment, and add it as an inference-time steering vector.
kuWcVe9WV4.evidence: Three source LLMs and five text-to-image and text-to-video targets with SVD, ridge and MLP alignment maps, measured by detector-based attack success rate and CLIP-Sim utility over 45 main configurations.
kuWcVe9WV4.claimed_gains: Transferred directions reduce unsafe outputs in all 45 configurations of the main evaluation, with steering strength selectable from benign data alone (no percentages in the abstract).
kuWcVe9WV4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that transferring safety directions without target-side unsafe data is a practically relevant setting and that the evaluation is broad across source models, image generators and a video generator.
kuWcVe9WV4.main_concern: The method combines established components (difference-of-means steering, linear alignment, additive text-encoder intervention), and the evidence does not establish truly shared safety-specific representations versus general semantic features.

5BTp3W89Ok.one_liner: Parameter-free approximate rejection sampler that returns the sample with the largest importance weight divided by an independent uniform variable.
5BTp3W89Ok.problem: The best error bound for approximate rejection sampling depends on a threshold M that is typically unknown from the observed sample.
5BTp3W89Ok.method: Given N proposal samples with importance weights, uniform race divides each weight by an independent uniform variable and returns the candidate with the largest score. The authors bound its total variation error against every fixed-threshold rejection sampler and characterize its output distribution.
5BTp3W89Ok.key_idea: Dividing each importance weight by an independent uniform and taking the argmax attains the best fixed-threshold rejection-sampling bound for all thresholds simultaneously, without tuning.
5BTp3W89Ok.evidence: Theory (total variation bounds for every budget N, minimax optimality for bounded weights, comparison with a budget-calibrated rejection sampler) plus experiments on a fixed finite response pool.
5BTp3W89Ok.claimed_gains: Total variation error satisfies the rejection-sampling upper bound for every fixed threshold M at once for every budget N, and the sampler is minimax optimal for bounded importance weights (no empirical numbers stated).
5BTp3W89Ok.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the algorithm is simple, removes threshold and normalizer tuning, and comes with clean, rigorous guarantees from several complementary perspectives.
5BTp3W89Ok.main_concern: Novelty is unclear because the selection rule is a special case of classical priority sampling (disclosed only in the appendix), and experiments on a fixed finite pool do not show practical value.

CEOXssiNEb.one_liner: Optimal stopping for detecting that a generator has produced at least one hit, calibrated with conformal p-values for false-alarm control.
CEOXssiNEb.problem: Deciding when generation has yielded at least one hit, and so when to stop before costly experimental validation, requires controlling the chance of stopping before any hit exists (a false alarm).
CEOXssiNEb.method: The task is posed as finite-horizon optimal stopping with a false-alarm constraint. A monotone family of stopping times from Lagrangian duality is applied to conformal p-values built from screening scores, and the multiplier is chosen by calibrating on simulated global-null trajectories.
CEOXssiNEb.key_idea: Apply a Lagrangian-dual monotone family of stopping rules to conformal p-values and pick the multiplier as a quantile over simulated global-null trajectories for exact finite-sample false-alarm control.
CEOXssiNEb.evidence: Theory (near-optimal expected reward and exact false-alarm control under assumptions) plus synthetic and real experiments on QED-HGraph and TargetDiff candidates against adapted baselines.
CEOXssiNEb.claimed_gains: Substantial improvements over competing methods with the same finite-sample false-alarm guarantees on QED-HGraph and TargetDiff candidates (no numbers stated).
CEOXssiNEb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated, the Lagrangian-duality and calibration approach is principled with clean theory, and the method attains higher reward than baselines at the same false-alarm level.
CEOXssiNEb.main_concern: Practical benefit is not demonstrated: experiments assume a labeled pool from the deployment distribution, baselines are the authors' own adaptations, and simple score-based validation strategies are not compared.

HutWB3IC6c.one_liner: Reweights flow-matching supervision by trajectory-derived precision demand and internalizes it in the VLM condition representation for VLA policies.
HutWB3IC6c.problem: Flow-matching action training averages errors across contexts and flow times (Flow-Time Starvation), giving little supervision to the few decisive moments that determine success in precise manipulation.
HutWB3IC6c.method: PRISM scores precision demand offline, strengthens flow supervision where errors are consequential and action signals are visible, and internalizes that demand in the VLM condition representation. It changes only training and leaves inference unchanged.
HutWB3IC6c.key_idea: Weight the flow-matching loss by an offline per-context precision-demand score and train the VLM condition representation to predict that demand.
HutWB3IC6c.evidence: Simulation (RLBench-10) and three real-robot tasks across VLA backbones, with ablations of the components and a proposition bounding endpoint sensitivity to flow-time error.
HutWB3IC6c.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before the results)
HutWB3IC6c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem practically important, the training-only change easy to deploy, and the gains consistent across simulation and real-robot tasks.
HutWB3IC6c.main_concern: The precision-demand score is a behavioral proxy (slow motion, gripper cues) not shown to track physical tolerance, and the weighting rule is not derived from the sensitivity bound.

88MPTBmYmL.one_liner: Learns a mask over sparse-autoencoder concepts to suppress spurious ones before a frozen classifier, using few group-annotated examples.
88MPTBmYmL.problem: ERM-trained networks rely on spurious correlations, and existing fixes need retraining or many group labels, or modify only the classifier head and leave spurious information in the latent space.
88MPTBmYmL.method: SPOCK maps dense latent representations into an overcomplete concept space with a Sparse Autoencoder and learns a mask that suppresses spurious concepts while preserving task-useful ones. Representations are reconstructed from the filtered concepts and the existing classifier stays fixed.
88MPTBmYmL.key_idea: Learn a mask over overcomplete SAE concepts from a small group-annotated validation set, filter concepts before reconstruction, and feed the result to the unchanged classifier.
88MPTBmYmL.evidence: Four synthetic and real-world datasets compared with ERM and DFR; reviews cite CelebA, MultiNLI, BAR, and Waterbirds with ResNet-18 and BERT backbones.
88MPTBmYmL.claimed_gains: Substantially improves worst-group accuracy over ERM while maintaining high accuracy (the abstract is cut off); no numbers stated.
88MPTBmYmL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like that it mitigates spurious correlations without retraining or modifying the classifier head, needs few group labels, and improves over DFR on CelebA and MultiNLI.
88MPTBmYmL.main_concern: It is unclear why SAE masking separates spurious from core concepts, a dense-autoencoder control is missing, worst-group trade-offs appear on BAR and Waterbirds, and only small base models are tested.

VN16j6Be2H.one_liner: Uses target-aware counterfactual intervention, approximated by gradients, to find visual tokens that drive transferable targeted attacks on MLLMs.
VN16j6Be2H.problem: Existing transferable targeted attacks optimize target-related features but overlook which visual components actually drive adversarial transfer toward the target semantics.
VN16j6Be2H.method: A causal-guided framework estimates the causal influence of visual components through target-aware counterfactual intervention with a gradient-based approximation. The identified target-relevant components enter a causal-guided feature optimization objective that aligns the adversarial example with the target representation.
VN16j6Be2H.key_idea: Score visual components with a first-order gradient approximation of target-aware counterfactual effects and emphasize the top-scoring ones in the feature-alignment attack loss.
VN16j6Be2H.evidence: Experiments across various open-source and proprietary MLLMs against existing attack methods, with ablations; reviewers note 8 target models and main experiments on 100 samples.
VN16j6Be2H.claimed_gains: Consistently enhances targeted transferability over existing attack methods across various MLLMs; no numbers stated.
VN16j6Be2H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method intuitive and well motivated, with ablations justifying the components and higher attack success than baselines across several MLLMs.
VN16j6Be2H.main_concern: Novelty is overstated relative to attribution-patching work, and the first-order approximation and small-sample evaluation lack validation, with no confidence intervals and ablations on one target model.

H6YrYT7zC4.one_liner: Navigates from an overhead RGB map via dual pose/goal grounding and one-step semantic foresight, with a new benchmark.
H6YrYT7zC4.problem: Existing navigation goal types need coordinates, reference images, or route descriptions users may not have, ObjectNav labels are ambiguous, and unfamiliar multi-room layouts require extensive exploration without a global spatial prior.
H6YrYT7zC4.method: OmniMapNavBench uses one overhead RGB map as goal interface and spatial prior, with map-selected points, hand-drawn route sketches, and language goals. OmniMapNav's Dual-Grounding Map Reader estimates an agent pose-heading belief and a goal anchor field to retrieve map tokens, and a Semantic Foresight Predictor estimates action-conditioned next-observation features that a scorer uses to refine action scores.
H6YrYT7zC4.key_idea: Retrieve map tokens using separate agent-pose and goal-anchor estimates, then rescore actions with predicted action-conditioned next-observation features.
H6YrYT7zC4.evidence: A benchmark of 50,241 episodes across 4,724 scenes with ablations, plus a real-robot comparison using 60 trials per method after adaptation on 45 human trajectories.
H6YrYT7zC4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the map-centric goal interface intuitive, the identical-episode comparison of goal cues meaningful, and the ablations supportive of the dual-grounding components.
H6YrYT7zC4.main_concern: The foresight predictor is supervised only on the demonstrated action, so its action-conditioned semantics are unvalidated, and novelty and the real-world protocol need more detail.

j5qZYQUnUx.one_liner: Adapts the teacher with a student-vocabulary head and parallel-tokenized input so cross-tokenizer on-policy distillation gets full-dimensional logits.
j5qZYQUnUx.problem: Different teacher and student tokenizers misalign input tokenization and output logits in on-policy distillation, and existing fixes lose token information or keep only shared logit dimensions.
j5qZYQUnUx.method: DVLM replaces the teacher's LM head with a student-vocabulary projection head and feeds a Parallel-Tokenized Sequence (the teacher-tokenized sequence plus each student token re-tokenized into a teacher-token group). Hybrid-Prefix Attention restricts each re-tokenized group to its teacher prefix and uses its last state as the student-token representation projected into the student vocabulary.
j5qZYQUnUx.key_idea: Concatenate teacher-tokenized and student-token-regrouped sequences, mask attention so each group sees only its teacher prefix, and project the group's last state through a new student-vocabulary head.
j5qZYQUnUx.evidence: On-policy distillation experiments with ablations on re-tokenization and the new head; reviews cite comparisons against GOLD and student results in Table 1.
j5qZYQUnUx.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before the results)
j5qZYQUnUx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that giving the teacher a token-for-token, full-vocabulary output space is an elegant idea that avoids heuristic truncation, is lightweight, and is clearly presented.
j5qZYQUnUx.main_concern: Empirical gains look modest (about 2.8 to 3.1 points) relative to the added overhead and teacher modification, a closely related cross-tokenizer method is missing, and samples with undecodable student tokens are discarded.

qfBg2OrstG.one_liner: Benchmark of biopsy-confirmed deep-seated brain tumor MRI plus a VLM-and-MLP two-stage spatial-prior annotation pipeline.
qfBg2OrstG.problem: Existing brain tumor datasets focus on superficial tumors, and no public benchmark with biopsy-confirmed labels exists for deep-seated tumors in the thalamus, basal ganglia, and brainstem.
qfBg2OrstG.method: DeepSite-MRI has 249 biopsy-confirmed cases across four subtypes (Glioma, PCNSL, Germinoma, Rare). Its Two-Stage spatial Prior pipeline (TSP) combines VLM-guided coarse localization with MLP-based refinement to cut annotation time.
qfBg2OrstG.key_idea: Generate lesion spatial priors by VLM-guided coarse localization followed by MLP refinement, and supply them to classifiers as auxiliary input.
qfBg2OrstG.evidence: Ten CNN and Transformer architectures evaluated without priors, with coarse priors, and with refined priors using five-fold cross-validation, plus expert validation of the generated priors.
qfBg2OrstG.claimed_gains: Per-case annotation time (excluding spot-check review) drops from approximately 90 minutes to 3 minutes with a 96% clinical acceptance rate, and the best accuracy of mainstream architectures on the benchmark is 78.90%.
qfBg2OrstG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the biopsy-confirmed dataset for an underrepresented clinical problem and the broad evaluation of ten architectures under three prior conditions.
qfBg2OrstG.main_concern: The TSP refinement is questionable (the final prior is a union with the coarse prior, so false positives remain), and the annotation-speed claim, four-class grouping, and public release are weakly justified.

k1oht7VRA8.one_liner: Bayesian latent variable model with Gaussian-process spatial priors and sparse variational inference for spatial multi-omics domain detection.
k1oht7VRA8.problem: Integrating heterogeneous nonlinear spatial multi-omics measurements with complex spatial dependencies is challenging.
k1oht7VRA8.method: SpaLVM is a Bayesian latent variable model that captures cross-modality variation and spatial dependence through Gaussian process priors for nonlinear dimension reduction. A sparse, structured variational inference scheme with inducing points makes computation scalable.
k1oht7VRA8.key_idea: Place Gaussian process priors on latent states shared across modalities and use inducing-point sparse variational inference to scale the nonlinear spatial model.
k1oht7VRA8.evidence: Simulated and real datasets across diverse technologies and tissue structures, compared with spatial and non-spatial, single-modal and multimodal methods (nine baselines per a reviewer) on dimensionality reduction and spatial domain detection.
k1oht7VRA8.claimed_gains: About a 10-fold speedup over the original SpaLVM implementation, and consistently outperforms existing spatial, non-spatial, single-modal, and multimodal methods; no other numbers stated.
k1oht7VRA8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the model well motivated and clearly described, the sparse spatial parameterization a fix for a computational bottleneck, and the results strong across data types and baselines.
k1oht7VRA8.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate which component explains the gains (such as nonlinear versus linear mappings), and novelty over existing spatial multimodal latent-variable and GP latent-space methods is unclear.

TIC814H7ni.one_liner: Replaces FID's Bures-Wasserstein covariance estimator with a random-matrix-theory estimator that converges with far fewer samples.
TIC814H7ni.problem: FID needs at least 50k real and generated samples to be accurate, stays biased even at n = 50k because of slow convergence, and is unsuitable for small-sample specialized domains.
TIC814H7ni.method: FxD is a closed-form, strictly compatible replacement for FID that swaps the classical estimator of the Bures-Wasserstein distance between two population covariance matrices for a variant from random matrix theory.
TIC814H7ni.key_idea: Estimate the Bures-Wasserstein distance between population covariances with a random-matrix-theory estimator instead of plugging in classical sample covariances.
TIC814H7ni.evidence: Synthetic datasets and real datasets at various scales: ImageNet-1k, CUB200, Oxford102, and two specialized medical imaging and remote sensing datasets.
TIC814H7ni.claimed_gains: FxD converges with sample sizes as low as a few thousand images, up to ten times fewer samples than FID, while classical FID is still biased at n = 50k.
TIC814H7ni.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the sample-size dependence of FID an important problem that the paper measures concretely, and FxD a low-friction closed-form drop-in tested from synthetic to large-scale datasets.
TIC814H7ni.main_concern: Novelty is mainly adapting an existing random-matrix Wasserstein estimator, and the plateau FxD converges to is not shown to equal the true Fréchet distance, with theory and comparisons centered on n_r = n_g.

y3MUYpH9Ak.one_liner: Asymmetric recurrent cost regularizer conditions a forward encoder-decoder on compressed reverse-depth context for high-resolution aerial MVS.
y3MUYpH9Ak.problem: Memory-efficient slice-wise recurrent regularizers for aerial MVS either update state from one direction only or lack deep context integration across independent bidirectional passes.
y3MUYpH9Ak.method: RCCR uses a lightweight reverse encoder to extract compressed context that conditions a multi-scale forward recurrent encoder-decoder through a cell with an evidence-state discrepancy gating mechanism, run as two-pass inference that caches compressed reverse contexts and scalar depth logits. RCCR-MVS adds Coverage-risk-guided Range Expansion (CRE) and Spatial Evidence Support (SES) to cascaded deployments.
y3MUYpH9Ak.key_idea: Run a cheap reverse pass to compress future-depth context, then condition the forward recurrent regularizer on it with evidence-state discrepancy gating, without storing the full cost volume.
y3MUYpH9Ak.evidence: Experiments on high-resolution aerial MVS datasets with single-stage and coarse-to-fine variants, including component ablations such as RCCR alone.
y3MUYpH9Ak.claimed_gains: Reports the best performance among high-resolution aerial MVS methods (the abstract is cut off); no numbers stated.
y3MUYpH9Ak.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the asymmetric reverse-context design a practical accuracy-memory trade-off and the experimental validation strong, with RCCR alone improving over the baseline.
y3MUYpH9Ak.main_concern: The effect of reverse conditioning is not isolated from the evidence-state discrepancy mechanism, there is no comparison to symmetric bidirectional RNNs, and CRE and SES look like engineering extensions.

BXcipK4Lms.one_liner: Benchmark of procedurally generated sequential social dilemmas with hidden rules for testing LLM rule discovery and social adaptation.
BXcipK4Lms.problem: Sequential social dilemma benchmarks rarely test whether agents can infer hidden environmental rules through repeated interaction while adapting to other agents.
BXcipK4Lms.method: OpenSocialJax extends Clean Up and Commons Harvest with procedurally generated layouts and hidden rules governing tool effects, rewards, and resource dynamics. Each episode samples one configuration from tens of millions of possibilities and holds it fixed across five trials.
BXcipK4Lms.key_idea: Randomize layouts and hidden tool, reward, and resource rules per episode, then hold the configuration fixed over repeated trials so agents must infer the rules and adapt to teammates.
BXcipK4Lms.evidence: Eight LLMs (three closed source, five open source) evaluated in homogeneous teams and a mixed arena on the OpenCleanup and OpenHarvest environments.
BXcipK4Lms.claimed_gains: not stated (benchmark paper; it reports that rule discovery often improves performance but does not reliably sustain cooperation)
BXcipK4Lms.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see the procedurally varied hidden-rule environments as a useful, challenging benchmark that goes beyond fixed-dynamics social dilemmas and allows fast simulation.
BXcipK4Lms.main_concern: The setup's validity is doubtful: generated layouts lack stated playability validation, the rule-learning mechanism is hard-coded into the prompt so LLMs may not infer dynamics themselves, and the evaluation scope is narrow.

ZqoUV0nMb0.one_liner: Fuses fragment-peak, neutral-loss, and peak-difference evidence with reliability weighting and disagreement discounting for fingerprint prediction.
ZqoUV0nMb0.problem: MS/MS fingerprint prediction suffers from incomplete fragmentation and similar spectra from distinct structures, single-view methods miss complementary cues, and bit probabilities hide how strong the supporting evidence is.
ZqoUV0nMb0.method: UncertFP infers per-bit positive and negative evidence from three spectral views, adjusts each view by bit reliability, uses a learnable coefficient interpolating between direct accumulation and weighted averaging, and discounts evidence when strongly supported views disagree. The fused evidence and a shared prior yield a probabilistic fingerprint and an uncertainty mass, supervised by the ranking of whole-fingerprint prediction errors.
ZqoUV0nMb0.key_idea: Fuse per-bit evidence from multiple spectral views with a learnable accumulate-versus-average coefficient and disagreement discounting, yielding both a fingerprint and an evidence-insufficiency mass.
ZqoUV0nMb0.evidence: Three datasets, two spectral encoders, and multiple fingerprint sizes, with ablations on spectral views, fusion strategies, training objectives, and uncertainty mechanisms.
ZqoUV0nMb0.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before the results; the TL;DR claims better fingerprint prediction and candidate-structure ranking)
ZqoUV0nMb0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evidence-versus-probability framing is useful and that improvements are consistent across three datasets, two encoders, and fingerprint sizes, with extensive ablations.
ZqoUV0nMb0.main_concern: Baseline comparisons may be unfair because UncertFP gets additional training from pretrained checkpoints and a different checkpoint-selection metric, and its learned evidence and reliability are not directly validated.

6ISCyimm6T.one_liner: Driving world-action model that forecasts future scenes in a 16-token-per-frame register space and conditions planning on them.
6ISCyimm6T.problem: World Action Models on video generators incur prohibitive latency from dense future videos, efficient variants drop the world branch at deployment, and patch-level features still give long sequences with decision-irrelevant content.
6ISCyimm6T.method: SparseWAM compresses frozen DINOv2 features into 16 register tokens per frame, shaped by joint planning-and-scoring pretraining. A modality-decoupled Mixture-of-Transformers with a causal attention mask lets action tokens condition on imagined future registers, and the compact space enables low-cost multimodal sampling.
6ISCyimm6T.key_idea: Forecast in a sparse 16-register space trained with planning and scoring objectives so action tokens can condition on imagined future registers at deployment.
6ISCyimm6T.evidence: Evaluated on NAVSIM v1, NAVSIM v2, and NavHard against video-based world-action models such as DriveVA, with latency measurements and a counterfactual scene-editing analysis of the representation.
6ISCyimm6T.claimed_gains: 92.1 PDMS on NAVSIM v1, 89.8 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2, and 40.1 on NavHard at 260 ms latency, roughly 1/3 that of DriveVA.
6ISCyimm6T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the efficiency of keeping a future-prediction branch with far fewer parameters and low latency, and the task-oriented planning-and-scoring representation learning.
6ISCyimm6T.main_concern: The evidence does not isolate the value of predicted futures: the 92.1 headline uses 64 samples with scorer selection and lacks a matched action-only baseline, and there are no ablations over register count or planning and scoring objectives.

27eKWCdSy4.one_liner: Loops one transformer block over cell and row streams as a tabular in-context learner, with a learned exit gate.
27eKWCdSy4.problem: Tabular foundation models using in-context learning are largely parameter-redundant according to recent mechanistic insights, and they cannot trade inference cost against performance.
27eKWCdSy4.method: LoopICL is a single block processing a cell stream of per-cell feature representations and a row stream of in-context example representations, jointly refined through within-column and cross-column attention. Pre-training varies loop counts so the block can be unrolled a variable number of times at test time, with a learned exit gate.
27eKWCdSy4.key_idea: Reuse one weight-shared block across a variable number of loop iterations over coupled cell and row streams, decoupling parameter count from computational depth.
27eKWCdSy4.evidence: TabArena and TALENT benchmarks against TabICLv2 at the same FLOPs, with loop-count and residual-scaling experiments.
27eKWCdSy4.claimed_gains: Performs competitively with TabICLv2 on TabArena and TALENT at the same computational cost (FLOPs) while using nearly 90% fewer parameters.
27eKWCdSy4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the competitive results with far fewer parameters convincing and the loop-count experiments informative, with the inference-cost trade-off a practical benefit.
27eKWCdSy4.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the recurrent cell-stream update or weight sharing is what helps, whether parameter count is a real bottleneck, and what the full inference cost is, and they note modest novelty.

jZES6PB14x.one_liner: Multi-agent framework that picks initial designs from history and evolves the optimizer from execution feedback for scientific design.
jZES6PB14x.problem: Scientific design optimization faces costly evaluations, sparse feasible solutions, coupled parameters, and strict physical constraints, and general-purpose AI-for-AI methods ignore scientific priors, constraints, and limited evaluation budgets.
jZES6PB14x.method: ADAPT treats scientific optimization as two coupled decisions, where to search and how to search. It uses historical designs to identify promising, diverse initial conditions, progressively concentrates computation on favorable search directions, and evolves the optimization procedure from execution feedback.
jZES6PB14x.key_idea: Retrieve initial conditions from historical designs, stage the compute budget toward favorable directions, and evolve the optimizer code from execution feedback.
jZES6PB14x.evidence: Gravitational wave detector design with a differentiable physics simulator on eight unseen detector topologies, under matched evaluation budgets across 10 random seeds, against classical optimizers and a general-purpose agentic evolution baseline.
jZES6PB14x.claimed_gains: Mean loss of 0.208 ± 0.098, a 59.8% reduction relative to the best classical optimizer and 63.2% relative to the best general purpose agentic evolution baseline, over 10 random seeds.
jZES6PB14x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the where/how decomposition clean and practically relevant, with gains across all eight held-out topologies and concrete retrieval and parameter-transfer rules.
jZES6PB14x.main_concern: Evidence covers only eight gravitational-wave detector topologies, so the broad scientific claim is unsupported, and the boundary between policy development and held-out evaluation and the missing baselines such as Bayesian optimization and CMA-ES are unclear.

qambg0oh7u.one_liner: Second-order guidance for diffusion and bridge models that contrasts adjacent reference predictions along a degradation trajectory.
qambg0oh7u.problem: A single reference contrast gives only a first-order estimate of the desired sampling direction in diffusion and bridge guidance and may leave residual bias.
qambg0oh7u.method: C2G extends existing guidance with multi-level reference predictions along the degradation trajectory and contrasts adjacent reference differences to capture how the first-order steering direction varies. ProjC2G keeps the tuned first-order scale and splits the second-order correction into components parallel and orthogonal to the first-order direction, modulating them dynamically during sampling.
qambg0oh7u.key_idea: Contrast adjacent reference differences along the degradation trajectory to recover residual guidance, and decompose that correction into parts parallel and orthogonal to the first-order guidance.
qambg0oh7u.evidence: Experiments across four guidance mechanisms (CFG, AG, SG, PG), both diffusion and bridge models, and diverse generation tasks, using frozen pretrained models.
qambg0oh7u.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before the results)
qambg0oh7u.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the framework simple and broadly applicable across guidance mechanisms and both model families, with a projection design that stabilizes the correction while preserving the tuned first-order scale.
qambg0oh7u.main_concern: Novelty over ICFG's second-order extension and APG's parallel-orthogonal decomposition is not shown by direct comparison, the second-order term costs an extra forward pass per step, and its design relies on manual heuristics.

3g7Myiqb8i.one_liner: Benchmark of 200 dyadic conventions testing whether agents compress, accept, and produce partner-specific shorthand, plus a Pact-Mem memory fix.
3g7Myiqb8i.problem: Long-term memory benchmarks test facts stated in dialogue rather than conventions that emerge across sessions, so it is unknown whether agents can take part in forming and later using them.
3g7Myiqb8i.method: PactBench has 200 dyadic conventions spanning inversion, anchoring, adoption, and erosion, with user-compression and agent-compression histories, evaluated per capability by withholding the agent turn and scored conjunctively with a meaning question plus capability-specific checks. Pact-Mem is the proposed memory system (the abstract is cut off after saying it preserves convention-level information).
3g7Myiqb8i.key_idea: Store each convention as a joint form-meaning record, consolidate it across sessions, and retrieve it by situation so the agent can later produce the established form.
3g7Myiqb8i.evidence: Four backbone LLMs and six existing memory systems on PactBench, with a condition giving the full reference formation history to separate retrieval failures from generation failures.
3g7Myiqb8i.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before Pact-Mem's results)
3g7Myiqb8i.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the dyadic-convention topic novel and practically relevant, and the benchmark carefully built, with a task decomposition that separates compression, acceptance, and production.
3g7Myiqb8i.main_concern: Pact-Mem is evaluated only on PactBench with limited methodological novelty, and the fully synthetic conventions and fixed top-5 retrieval budget leave validity and baseline fairness unestablished.

iACIkoiBEl.one_liner: Gives MARL agents primary and auxiliary roles over semantic slots, shaped by contrastive learning and a performance-guided slot memory.
iACIkoiBEl.problem: Role-based MARL needs persistent role structures that capture inter-role associations and can be reused across episodes, rather than only current role assignments.
iACIkoiBEl.method: SPAR builds a role prototype space from semantic slots and represents each agent by a dual assignment of a primary and an auxiliary role. Relation-preserving contrastive learning shapes the role-space geometry, and a performance-guided slot memory reuses high-quality collaboration patterns.
iACIkoiBEl.key_idea: Represent each agent as a primary-plus-auxiliary soft assignment over semantic role slots, and store high-performing slot states in memory for reuse across episodes.
iACIkoiBEl.evidence: Experiments on SMAC and SMACv2 with five seeds and learning curves, compared with baselines such as ACORM.
iACIkoiBEl.claimed_gains: Achieves competitive performance across multiple test scenarios on SMAC and SMACv2; no numbers stated in the abstract.
iACIkoiBEl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see the primary-auxiliary soft role assignment with prototype reuse as a coherent, clearly motivated extension that improves over ACORM on most tasks.
iACIkoiBEl.main_concern: The experiments do not show that auxiliary roles capture cooperative relations rather than assignment ambiguity, the slot module's training objectives are unclear, and the contribution over established techniques is not well separated.

2hVZWyqA49.one_liner: Treats projected 3D actions as pixel classes on camera images, predicting whole action chunks in one forward pass.
2hVZWyqA49.problem: Robot action spaces are high-dimensional, span long horizons, and admit multi-modal solutions, and naively discretizing them for classification explodes the token vocabulary.
2hVZWyqA49.method: AMP projects 3D actions onto camera image planes and treats each pixel location as a discrete class, trained with cross-entropy on keypoint heatmaps, and recovers 3D end-effector poses by triangulation. It predicts the entire action chunk in a single forward pass without iterative denoising.
2hVZWyqA49.key_idea: Represent actions as per-pixel class heatmaps on calibrated camera views and triangulate the 3D pose, replacing a huge discrete vocabulary with image-space classification.
2hVZWyqA49.evidence: Six simulated and five real-world manipulation tasks against strong baselines, including Diffusion Policy for inference latency.
2hVZWyqA49.claimed_gains: Improves the completion rate by 50%--70% on long-horizon tasks (the abstract text is cut off there), with millimeter-level precision and substantially faster inference.
2hVZWyqA49.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the heatmap action representation well motivated, strong in real-world experiments, and faster at inference than Diffusion Policy.
2hVZWyqA49.main_concern: It depends on at least two calibrated cameras with shared workspace coverage, and the evidence (20 real-world runs per task, no confidence intervals, truncated training actions) may favor AMP.

fvCLbniPPr.one_liner: Taxonomy-guided, visually diverse multimodal reasoning benchmark with manually written questions that frontier MLLMs fail.
fvCLbniPPr.problem: Many multimodal benchmarks expand task types without capturing the visual diversity needed for open-ended real-world visual inputs.
fvCLbniPPr.method: The authors build a taxonomy of thousands of visual concepts across domains, curate images from search engines and existing datasets to cover it, and manually design challenging questions through structured trial-and-error until frontier MLLMs fail them.
fvCLbniPPr.key_idea: Select images from a taxonomy of thousands of visual concepts and write questions adversarially against frontier MLLMs through structured trial-and-error.
fvCLbniPPr.evidence: Evaluation of 15 MLLMs, quantitative and human diversity evaluations, and reasoning-budget analysis.
fvCLbniPPr.claimed_gains: Even the strongest of 15 evaluated MLLMs reaches only 64.0% accuracy, and some models perform marginally above chance.
fvCLbniPPr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find that taxonomy-guided curation and multi-round human review give useful visual coverage, with extensive evaluation across 15 models and diversity metrics.
fvCLbniPPr.main_concern: The benefit of taxonomy-driven diversity is not isolated from adversarial question selection, and human solvability and residual annotation error are not quantified.

EIGTuB0ze9.one_liner: Averaged mirror descent and a fixed-step dual gradient method with convergence guarantees for entropic Gromov-Wasserstein under arbitrary costs.
EIGTuB0ze9.problem: Mirror descent for entropic Gromov-Wasserstein is proven to converge only for restricted cost classes, and the dual gradient method for general costs needs a step size that depends on the regularization parameter.
EIGTuB0ze9.method: Averaged Mirror Descent (AMD) averages consecutive mirror descent steps and is proved to converge for arbitrary costs, and the dual gradient method is shown to converge with a fixed step size at the cost of a more complicated iteration. Both analyses account for inexact iterations.
EIGTuB0ze9.key_idea: Average consecutive mirror-descent steps to restore convergence for general costs, and prove the dual gradient method converges with a fixed step size.
EIGTuB0ze9.evidence: Convergence theorems for arbitrary costs that include inexact inner solves, plus numerical comparisons on three examples with non-CNT costs according to reviewers (the abstract's comparison text is cut off).
EIGTuB0ze9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the convergence guarantees beyond CNT costs that account for inexact inner solvers, and the clear progress on non-CNT examples where mirror descent stalls or oscillates.
EIGTuB0ze9.main_concern: Theoretically justified step sizes are far smaller than those that work in practice, experiments are limited to a few examples with one cost family, and novelty and focus are questioned.

T3sNV7G24U.one_liner: Learns coordinate-rank rules on post-projector LVLM features to label visual tokens contributive or residual before decoding.
T3sNV7G24U.problem: Visual-token function in vision-language models is typically analyzed only after decoder processing begins, leaving unclear whether representations entering the decoder already carry structure predictive of functional sensitivity.
T3sNV7G24U.method: PRISM builds label-free structural calibration anchors from paired pre/post-interface responses and learns compact, inspectable coordinate-rank rules over post-interface representations. The rules recover image-level contributive and residual token roles directly from post-interface features, before query-conditioned decoder processing.
T3sNV7G24U.key_idea: A restricted set of coordinates dominates visual-token activations after the interface, so rank rules over those coordinates, calibrated on pre/post-interface response pairs, separate contributive from residual tokens.
T3sNV7G24U.evidence: Controlled token-removal interventions across four projector- and merger-based LVLM backbones, with attention-matched controls and reuse of the role map across questions for token selection.
T3sNV7G24U.claimed_gains: Removing contributive tokens consistently causes greater downstream degradation than removing residual tokens across four LVLM backbones; no numbers stated.
T3sNV7G24U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the intervention-based validation across several LVLM architectures and the lightweight, label-free, reusable pre-decoder role map.
T3sNV7G24U.main_concern: Novelty over prior pre-decoder visual-token role analyses is not established by direct comparison, and the spectral analysis and attention controls support only narrower conclusions.

5dWjXQoyPp.one_liner: Wild-NVS dataset and benchmark plus a feed-forward latent-space NVS model with appearance conditioning and transient-feature suppression.
5dWjXQoyPp.problem: Feed-forward novel view synthesis from unconstrained photo collections lacks training setups covering real appearance variation, transient occlusion, and diverse source-view configurations, and inconsistent evaluation protocols complicate comparison.
5dWjXQoyPp.method: The Wild-NVS benchmark builds source-target view sets from internet photo collections using bidirectional covisibility, joint target coverage, and viewpoint diversity, with scene-level splits and fixed protocols across several source-view counts. The Wild-NVS model synthesizes target views from latent representations using bottlenecked appearance conditioning and a learned transient prediction head that guides source-feature suppression before decoding.
5dWjXQoyPp.key_idea: Predict transient content from source features and suppress it before decoding, while conditioning on a bottlenecked appearance code, in a latent-representation feed-forward NVS model.
5dWjXQoyPp.evidence: Experiments on the Wild-NVS benchmark and PhotoTourism against deterministic feed-forward methods, with component ablations.
5dWjXQoyPp.claimed_gains: Consistent improvements over existing deterministic feed-forward methods for in-the-wild NVS, with improved appearance modeling and reduced transient artifacts; no numbers stated.
5dWjXQoyPp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see the dataset and benchmark, with covisibility-checked views and a unified protocol, as the strongest contribution, and the NVS results as promising in a realistic setting.
5dWjXQoyPp.main_concern: The model is an incremental extension of LagerNVS with limited study of transient suppression, since most gains come from appearance conditioning, and baseline fairness and target-appearance conditioning in evaluation are unclear.

W3jcTOFu5O.one_liner: Measures discrete-diffusion train-inference mismatch as the Mirror Gap and reduces it via representation steering and gap-based resampling.
W3jcTOFu5O.problem: Discrete diffusion denoisers train on corrupted data but at inference see states produced by their own samples, creating a train-inference mismatch that has not been measured.
W3jcTOFu5O.method: The Mirror Gap is measured with three discrepancy measures: discriminability of training versus inference states, distance between representation centroids, and divergence between quantized representation distributions. Two strategies reduce it without denoiser retraining: steering generations in representation space and resampling states based on the measured gap.
W3jcTOFu5O.key_idea: Quantify the gap between training and inference state distributions in representation space, then use it to steer activations and to resample states during sampling.
W3jcTOFu5O.evidence: Measurements and interventions on text and image discrete diffusion across noise families, samplers, and model scales, with quality measured by MAUVE or FID.
W3jcTOFu5O.claimed_gains: At the same quality (MAUVE or FID), the methods show sampling-efficiency gains exceeding 8x over strong baselines (the abstract is cut off after this).
W3jcTOFu5O.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem important, the analysis clean and carefully executed across modalities, and the steering fix simple, nearly free at inference, and consistently effective.
W3jcTOFu5O.main_concern: Novelty is limited because the mismatch is the known exposure bias and the steering method is essentially activation steering, and the efficiency gains appear inflated by low-quality baselines.

zm8rhu1kzf.one_liner: Empirical study of how diversity and complexity of synthetic prior data shape prior-data fitted network generalization.
zm8rhu1kzf.problem: Synthetic data design for prior-data fitted networks is largely heuristic and trial-and-error, without a principled account of how data properties relate to downstream performance.
zm8rhu1kzf.method: The authors use PFNs to study how data-generation procedures shape training dynamics and inductive biases, identify diversity and complexity as key prior properties, and introduce practical proxies that are predictive of real-world downstream performance.
zm8rhu1kzf.key_idea: Vary prior diversity and complexity (graph connectivity, node retention, noise) and show that increasing either improves generalization even as the prior moves away from the target task.
zm8rhu1kzf.evidence: Controlled experiments varying synthetic prior properties, replicated across model capacities, on mostly 1D tasks plus one 2D experiment according to reviewers, with proxies correlated to downstream performance.
zm8rhu1kzf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the argument clear and the finding that more diverse priors generalize better despite distribution mismatch interesting, with good ablations replicated across model capacities.
zm8rhu1kzf.main_concern: Experiments are mostly 1D tasks, the proxies depend on the trained model, and the recommendations (more diverse data and capacity) may be well known, with 'complexity' bundling mechanisms that are not disentangled.

pwW2Wdfbsl.one_liner: Returns the user's hint only if its logit margin in an opinion-free VLM pass passes a calibrated threshold.
pwW2Wdfbsl.problem: Anti-sycophancy interventions for VLMs suppress wrong user hints but also discard correct ones; Leading-Query Contrastive Decoding keeps none of the 159 corrections the model had accepted from the user.
pwW2Wdfbsl.method: Accept-or-answer has the model answer the neutral question in an opinion-free pass and returns the user's answer instead when its logit margin in that pass reaches a threshold calibrated on labelled queries. It needs one opinion-free pass, does not depend on how hard the user pushes, and can take its margin from another model.
pwW2Wdfbsl.key_idea: Decide whether to trust a hint by how close it ranks to the model's own answer in a pass that never shows the hint.
pwW2Wdfbsl.evidence: 17 settings (seven benchmarks, three backbones, four phrasings, and hints written by people and by another model), compared with the best fixed policy of each setting chosen after the fact.
pwW2Wdfbsl.claimed_gains: Averages 72.2% accuracy pooled over wrong and correct hints against 70.2% for the best fixed policy of each setting, and scores above the best fixed policy in 16 of 17 settings (per the TL;DR).
pwW2Wdfbsl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the evaluation comprehensive and the method a light, clear inference-time rule that improves pooled accuracy and is stable across phrasings and scoring models.
pwW2Wdfbsl.main_concern: The rule needs labelled calibration data and logit access, reads only the first answer token, and relies on constructed wrong hints and correctly parsed inputs.

mgffGRI0Yj.one_liner: Twelve-strategy, four-level LLM data-rewriting framework for SFT knowledge injection emphasizing contextual diversity over repetition.
mgffGRI0Yj.problem: Model editing suffers parameter interference under sequential edits and continual pre-training is costly for sparse factual updates, while naive or semantically flat SFT rewrites yield only spurious memorization of co-occurring tokens.
mgffGRI0Yj.method: KnowContext organizes 12 structured rewriting strategies into an atom-to-interactive four-level taxonomy, applied to counterfactual data from seven domains for SFT. It is evaluated with a six-task protocol spanning direct recall to scenario simulation.
mgffGRI0Yj.key_idea: Rewrite each fact into structured, contextually varied training text, including contrastive reasoning and anchor-knowledge bridging, so SFT internalizes knowledge instead of memorizing token co-occurrence.
mgffGRI0Yj.evidence: Experiments on three LLMs with different sets of rewriting strategies across seven domains and a six-task evaluation; reviewers note comparison against DeepKI at matched sample counts.
mgffGRI0Yj.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports three qualitative findings: sufficient exposure is necessary, diversity dominates quantity, and contrastive reasoning with anchor bridging drives the deepest internalization)
mgffGRI0Yj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the evaluation protocol careful, separating direct recall from anchored reasoning, and the gains over DeepKI large and consistent across models and domains.
mgffGRI0Yj.main_concern: Novelty over DeepKI is limited and the comparison is confounded by different data-generation models, with single-run results, no measurement of unrelated-fact preservation, and a synthetic, partly LLM-judged evaluation.

YZZxYmav2u.one_liner: Modulates node-to-slice routing in a MeshGraphNet-Transolver model with impact-relative and bounding-box-relative geometry for impact response prediction.
YZZxYmav2u.problem: Predicting localized impact responses on complex structures needs representations of loading position, boundaries, and local mesh geometry, since responses have high gradients near the impact and long-range structural coupling.
YZZxYmav2u.method: GeoSlice-MGN uses impact-relative geometry and bounding-box-relative position to modulate content-driven node-to-slice assignment, keeps local MeshGraphNet propagation before and after global interaction, and augments slice states with relative soft occupancy. The authors also release AutoPanelImpact, a benchmark of 1,500 parameterized nonlinear impact cases on three automotive floor panels.
YZZxYmav2u.key_idea: Bias latent node-to-slice assignment with impact-relative and structure-relative geometry motivated by finite-plate mechanics, so load-structure geometry reaches global routing.
YZZxYmav2u.evidence: The AutoPanelImpact benchmark on three automotive floor panels plus further experiments on BumperBeam (the abstract is cut off), with ablations and baselines including Transolver, GINO, and Geo-FNO.
YZZxYmav2u.claimed_gains: Lowest average error on all six displacement-stress test metrics across the three panels; no numeric error values stated.
YZZxYmav2u.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the mechanics-motivated geometric routing design clear and effective, the released benchmark valuable, and the ablations informative.
YZZxYmav2u.main_concern: Baselines omit recent related methods such as GeoTransolver, Transolver++, and GAOT, the contribution beyond MeshGraphNet plus slice attention is not clearly stated, and comparison to classical finite element cost is missing.

pb11VFa5Tf.one_liner: Trains LLMs with SFT then role-aware RL to emit a structured reflection and resume from problem plus reflection only.
pb11VFa5Tf.problem: Reflective phrases like "wait, let me reconsider" in RL-trained reasoners are largely spurious, and existing self-reflection methods keep the faulty chain in context so the model must overcome its own errors.
pb11VFa5Tf.method: Under Clean-Slate Reflection, the model emits a structured <reflection> block summarizing verified sub-conclusions, diagnosed mistakes, and corrected directions, then continues from the problem and the reflection alone. REFLECT+ trains this with a supervised cold-start followed by role-aware reinforcement learning to decide when to reflect, what to retain, and how to resume.
pb11VFa5Tf.key_idea: Replace the faulty reasoning prefix with a model-written structured reflection as the new context, and optimize when to trigger it with role-aware RL.
pb11VFa5Tf.evidence: Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B, Qwen3-0.6B-Base, and Qwen3-4B-Base on MATH500, AMC23, GSM8K, LogiQA, GPQA, MMLU-Pro, BBH, CLUTRR, and DROP, measuring self-correction quality and accuracy against Base, SFT, and GRPO.
pb11VFa5Tf.claimed_gains: Outperforms GRPO on accuracy with selective reflection; no numbers stated.
pb11VFa5Tf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the clean-slate state-replacement mechanism clear and practical, with encouraging gains on the 1.5B model and a useful comparison of retaining versus discarding the faulty prefix.
pb11VFa5Tf.main_concern: The paper does not separate corrective state replacement from simply restarting afresh, lacks comparisons with reflection-aware methods such as REA-RL, and does not directly evaluate the accuracy of the reflections.

EH025bmUlj.one_liner: Proves tight oracle complexity and PLS-completeness for finding stationary points of higher-order smooth nonconvex functions in fixed dimension.
EH025bmUlj.problem: The paper targets the tight oracle complexity and computational hardness of finding approximate stationary points of nonconvex functions with prescribed higher-order Lipschitz derivatives in fixed dimension.
EH025bmUlj.method: For every fixed dimension d and order p, it establishes a tight oracle bound for finding epsilon-stationary points with deterministic exact gradient-only oracles. It also shows that stationary-point search is PLS-complete for every fixed finite p and d at least 2, for bounded functions with bounded derivatives.
EH025bmUlj.key_idea: Upper bound by regularized Taylor-model steps built from finite-difference gradient queries, a lower bound independent of dimension, and PLS-hardness via a kernel extension of known hard instances.
EH025bmUlj.evidence: Theoretical results only as described: matching oracle upper and lower bounds and a PLS-completeness proof.
EH025bmUlj.claimed_gains: Tight oracle bound Θ(ε^{-(p+1)/p}) for every fixed dimension d and fixed order p, and PLS-completeness for every fixed finite p ≥ 1 and fixed d ≥ 2.
EH025bmUlj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the matching lower bound that holds uniformly across smoothness parameters and the extension of PLS-hardness to every fixed finite order.
EH025bmUlj.main_concern: Dimension dependence is unresolved (the upper bound uses (2q+1)^d gradient queries per step), the subproblem solve acts as an extra oracle, and the PLS-completeness result is seen as incremental over prior work.

dY63wiBv2x.one_liner: Training-free cross-query reuse of document K/V in BERT rerankers using Taylor position correction and score-anchored selective updates.
dY63wiBv2x.problem: BERT rerankers re-encode unchanged documents for every query, but document states depend on query interactions and query-dependent positions, which prevents exact reuse across queries.
dY63wiBv2x.method: ReState separates full-document reading from document-state updating: query and score tokens attend to every document position while only selected document states are updated under the current query. A Taylor-based position approximation compensates positional changes with precomputed correction components, and Score-anchored restoration selects which positions to update.
dY63wiBv2x.key_idea: Reuse cached document K/V, correct query-dependent position shifts with precomputed Taylor terms, and recompute only the states chosen by score-anchored restoration.
dY63wiBv2x.evidence: Frozen BERT-based (MiniLM) rerankers evaluated with quality-latency curves and ablations separating position error, update selection, and candidate routing, against baselines such as SEE and PRISM.
dY63wiBv2x.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before the results)
dY63wiBv2x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find it a substantive training-free fix that separates position shift from missing query interaction, with sensible ablations isolating each component.
dY63wiBv2x.main_concern: Speedups are measured against an eager-attention full baseline and exclude cache storage and retrieval costs, and baseline comparisons are not at matched quality.

eUBvytr0mV.one_liner: Generates molecules from cellular phenotypes by aligning phenotype features to target-conditioned priors and distilling target behavior.
eUBvytr0mV.problem: Phenotype-driven molecular generation faces an underdetermined inverse mapping from cellular response to molecular structure when no predefined target is given.
eUBvytr0mV.method: PhenTTP uses a state-transition phenotype encoder and three stages: aligning phenotype-derived representations with target-conditioned priors, learning phenotype-conditioned generation from phenotype-molecule pairs, and transferring target-conditioned behavior through dual-route distillation. It supports both phenotype-only and phenotype-plus-target generation.
eUBvytr0mV.key_idea: Transfer a target-conditioned generator's behavior into a phenotype-conditioned generator through representation alignment and dual-route distillation, so no target is needed at inference.
eUBvytr0mV.evidence: Chemical, scaffold, cell-line, and target out-of-distribution settings, scored with Vina and Boltz-2 binding estimates, phenotype correlation, validity, uniqueness, and novelty against phenotype-only baselines.
eUBvytr0mV.claimed_gains: The phenotype-only route lowers Vina scores by 0.28-0.75 kcal/mol over the best phenotype-only baseline, and the target-informed route raises Boltz-2 binder probability by 18.2-28.3 percentage points over the same baselines.
eUBvytr0mV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem practically relevant and the idea of using target-conditioned knowledge as a prior for phenotype-only generation well designed, with encouraging phenotype-only results.
eUBvytr0mV.main_concern: The method lacks a clear probabilistic formulation (the stage-3 mixture target could collapse), the value of adding the target over a target-only generator is unclear, and design choices are weakly ablated.

FaZW437QoI.one_liner: Replaces electrostatic field matching's single capacitor with an infinite periodic chain of plates and a single-sample training objective.
FaZW437QoI.problem: Electrostatic Field Matching's single-capacitor geometry yields backward-oriented and exterior field lines, requiring stochastic branching for exact transport and complicating ODE-based inference.
FaZW437QoI.method: C2FM places source and target distributions on an infinite periodic chain of alternating plates whose symmetry confines field lines between adjacent plates, and proves the ideal construction transports source to target along forward-oriented field lines. It also derives a training objective with single-sample targets and theoretically grounded perturbation kernels.
FaZW437QoI.key_idea: Alternate source and target plates periodically so reflection symmetry confines field lines forward, and learn the field from single-sample targets with principled perturbation kernels.
FaZW437QoI.evidence: Proofs of forward transport and finite-chain truncation analysis, plus experiments on 2D toy data and 16x16 colored MNIST compared with EFM and flow matching according to reviewers.
FaZW437QoI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the periodic-chain geometric idea simple and intuitive with clean theory, and an improvement over the baseline EFM.
FaZW437QoI.main_concern: Experiments are limited to toy data and low-resolution MNIST, the method is expensive at large chain sizes, and the writing leans heavily on the appendix.

zPzEu7Qe7O.one_liner: Plug-and-play adapter steers frozen time-series foundation model patch features toward an SVD-based normality subspace for anomaly detection.
zPzEu7Qe7O.problem: Time series foundation models can reconstruct or forecast rare anomalies as well as normal patterns, which shrinks reconstruction and forecasting error-based anomaly scores.
zPzEu7Qe7O.method: NCL builds a compact normality subspace from a few normal patch features and adaptively steers each patch feature toward normality within it, guided by contrastive constraints, without modifying pretrained parameters. The calibrated features are aggregated and fused with the original TSFM output to amplify the discrepancy between normal and abnormal patterns.
zPzEu7Qe7O.key_idea: Constrain each patch feature to a normality subspace built from a few normal patches, with contrastive constraints, then fuse the result with the frozen TSFM output.
zPzEu7Qe7O.evidence: Paired comparisons across eight TSFM backbones (reconstruction- and forecasting-based) and ten datasets according to reviewers, with extra backbones, statistical baselines, and anomaly-detection foundation models in the appendices.
zPzEu7Qe7O.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before the results)
zPzEu7Qe7O.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem relevant, adaptation from a few normal subsequences attractive, and the SVD/PCA-based normality subspace usable across reconstruction and forecasting TSFMs with broad empirical coverage.
zPzEu7Qe7O.main_concern: The error-amplification proof does not analyze the implemented architecture, and sensitivity to PCA feature scaling and hyperparameters is unclear.

jtmxp8OoFS.one_liner: Sends sparse compressed feature patches that the receiver reuses to estimate pose correction and reliability-guided fusion.
jtmxp8OoFS.problem: Collaborative perception is limited by communication cost and pose noise, and under a small budget the features useful for detection may be hard to match across agents.
jtmxp8OoFS.method: Each sender transmits a few compressed local feature patches, and the receiver matches them against ego features to estimate a shared translation and yaw correction per sender, accounting for matching uncertainty and geometric consistency. An adaptive gate controls how much correction is applied to the whole message, while pose reliability guides local fusion.
jtmxp8OoFS.key_idea: Use the same sparse patch messages for both uncertainty-aware pose correction and reliability-weighted fusion, with a gate scaling the applied correction.
jtmxp8OoFS.evidence: OPV2V, V2XSet, and DAIR-V2X-C, with component ablations and pose diagnostics, compared with feature-level collaborative perception methods under pose noise.
jtmxp8OoFS.claimed_gains: On OPV2V, 86.98% BEV AP70 under strong pose noise at only 0.393 Mbps per sender, at the lowest communication rates among the evaluated feature-level methods.
jtmxp8OoFS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the joint design that reuses sparse patches for alignment and detection well motivated, and strong under pose noise at much lower communication than feature-level baselines across three datasets.
jtmxp8OoFS.main_concern: Main comparisons are at very different communication rates and omit CPPC, novelty over ERMVP and CPPC is unclear, and the adaptive gate hurts under strong pose noise with evaluation mostly on synthetic noise.

UiLIbJ9scW.one_liner: Prior-data fitted network trained on synthetic graphs infers link-predictive structural patterns from labeled context without parameter updates.
UiLIbJ9scW.problem: Structural patterns that predict links vary across graphs, so link predictors transfer poorly, and recent universal link predictors still learn how to use context from real graphs.
UiLIbJ9scW.method: LPLP follows the prior-data fitted network paradigm and is trained only on synthetic graphs from a prior in which the structural patterns that predict links vary across tasks. Given an unseen graph with labeled context links, it infers the graph's structural pattern and scores query links without parameter updates.
UiLIbJ9scW.key_idea: Train a PFN on synthetic graphs whose link-formation rule varies per task, so it learns to infer the link-predictive pattern in-context.
UiLIbJ9scW.evidence: Seven benchmarks with random and HeaRT hard negatives on shared splits, with ablations and a node-classification extension noted by reviewers.
UiLIbJ9scW.claimed_gains: Best average rank among methods evaluated on shared splits under random and HeaRT hard negatives, improving average Hits@50 over the strongest baseline by 4.33 and 4.04 points, respectively.
UiLIbJ9scW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find it convincing that training only on synthetic graphs beats baselines trained on the real graphs, with strong evidence that the model uses context patterns, across two negative-sampling protocols.
UiLIbJ9scW.main_concern: Removing the link-formation rule changes results only slightly, so gains may come from the PFN and synthetic graph structure, and baseline fairness and generality beyond homogeneous, undirected, attribute-free graphs are questioned.

6sXuOpNNU6.one_liner: Shares outcomes along policy-tree edges via couplings, cutting A/B test queries while keeping each policy's exact trajectory law.
6sXuOpNNU6.problem: A direct A/B/n test runs each of J candidate policies independently over T rounds and uses JT outcomes, which is costly or risky when each reward-bearing interaction is expensive.
6sXuOpNNU6.method: TCAB associates policies with a tree, executes them in a topological order, and shares the observed outcome along an edge when the two policies on it can be coupled. Every policy keeps exactly its standalone finite-horizon trajectory law, the outcome count satisfies N(T) = T plus the sum of edge mismatches and is at most JT, and a heuristic searches for the optimal tree.
6sXuOpNNU6.key_idea: Glue pairwise maximal couplings of policies along a tree so one observed outcome serves coupled policies without changing any policy's marginal trajectory.
6sXuOpNNU6.evidence: Finite-sample proofs (conditional optimality of cost for the selected tree, variance bounds for pairwise contrasts, E[N(T)] = T + o(T) under sublinear pseudo-regret) and experiments on language-model evaluation (MMLU-Pro, RewardBench per reviewers) and adaptive bandit policies.
6sXuOpNNU6.claimed_gains: Saves 20-50% query costs while preserving the exact marginal distribution of the policy trajectories (per the TL;DR; the abstract's results sentence is cut off).
6sXuOpNNU6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the tree-gluing coupling elegant with sound finite-sample proofs, and an exact, unbiased design that treats policies as black boxes.
6sXuOpNNU6.main_concern: The design adds latency and does not bound worst-case proposal overhead compared with running policies independently and simultaneously, and the theory is seen as built on standard coupling techniques.

4ZrneBPcHe.one_liner: Station-based verification of twelve AI and physical forecast systems against ECMWF IFS finds extreme-weather deficits are model-specific.
4ZrneBPcHe.problem: AI weather models are often reported to underpredict extremes, but most evidence comes from deterministic regression systems verified against reanalysis rather than station observations.
4ZrneBPcHe.method: The study compares twelve physical and AI forecast systems with ECMWF IFS on European station observations over ten months for 10 m wind, 2 m temperature, solar radiation, and precipitation, with regimes defined from a fixed ERA5 1991-2020 climatology and models compared on matched samples.
4ZrneBPcHe.key_idea: Verify against independent station observations with fixed ERA5-climatology regimes on matched samples, instead of against reanalysis, to compare tail skill across models.
4ZrneBPcHe.evidence: Ten months of European station observations across four variables and multiple forecast ranges, with matched-sample comparison and uncertainty estimates.
4ZrneBPcHe.claimed_gains: not stated (qualitative finding: no uniform AI-specific loss of relative skill in the tails, with several AI systems more accurate than IFS in extreme regimes and others deteriorating markedly)
4ZrneBPcHe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study is comprehensive, using independent station observations across many AI and numerical systems, variables, and horizons, with uncertainty estimates.
4ZrneBPcHe.main_concern: Extremes are defined by climatological quantiles such as the 95th percentile rather than formal extreme-value analysis or real hazardous events, and the analysis lacks higher-order moment and spatial evaluation.

z4bzVxEI0L.one_liner: Synthesizes 3D pseudo-anomalies by amplifying natural variations among aligned normal instances and trains a paired scorer to detect them.
z4bzVxEI0L.problem: 3D point cloud anomaly synthesis relies on hand-crafted deformation operators or predefined anomaly morphologies, which limits the diversity of synthesized anomalies.
z4bzVxEI0L.method: NOVA uses local surface differences among aligned normal instances as deformation patterns and strengthens them beyond normal variation to create pseudo-anomalies. A normal-geometry branch first learns how much and in which directions normal surfaces vary and is then frozen, and an anomaly-scoring branch uses its features and reference-matching statistics to assign higher scores to the same points after deformation.
z4bzVxEI0L.key_idea: Amplify normal-instance surface variations beyond their normal range to make pseudo-anomalies, then train a scorer to rank points higher after deformation than before.
z4bzVxEI0L.evidence: Real3D-AD and Anomaly-ShapeNet, comparing synthesis strategies and detection with and without pseudo-anomaly supervision of 32 pseudo-anomalies per category.
z4bzVxEI0L.claimed_gains: The normal-geometry branch alone surpasses the best published O-AUROC and P-AUROC on both datasets, and 32 pseudo-anomalies per category raise P-AUROC on Real3D-AD from 92.68% to 95.99% (the second dataset's figure is cut off).
z4bzVxEI0L.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find using natural normal variation to drive pseudo-anomaly patterns well motivated and effective, with a strong normal-only baseline that synthetic supervision improves.
z4bzVxEI0L.main_concern: Novelty is limited and the design is not disentangled: deformation pattern versus strength calibration is not isolated, a baseline synthesis (CASL) beats NOVA's on Anomaly-ShapeNet, and the insight may not hold where normal samples are identical.

J99AInECr2.one_liner: Structured narrative memory with world-fact, character-belief, development, and hypothetical views over one graph, retrieved by planned reconstruction.
J99AInECr2.problem: LLM agents writing long-form fiction need explicit memory of the evolving storyworld that keeps heterogeneous narrative information distinct, integrates developments across granularities, and recovers dependencies a writing request leaves implicit.
J99AInECr2.method: NarraWorld derives four connected views (world facts, per-character beliefs, open developments, hypothetical branches) from a shared evidence-grounded graph, and uses hierarchical aggregation with atomic closure to consolidate events into scenes, plotlines, and plots traceable to source spans. At retrieval, planned reconstruction infers a query's dependencies from the narrative situation and a memory preview, then assembles relevant records within a token budget.
J99AInECr2.key_idea: Build memory as world creation, separating shared facts from per-character beliefs over one graph, and retrieve by planning a query's implicit dependencies against a memory preview.
J99AInECr2.evidence: Three long-form writing benchmarks plus situated role-playing and a general-purpose long-term memory benchmark, with ablations and human evaluation.
J99AInECr2.claimed_gains: Achieves the strongest aggregate results across three writing benchmarks and largely preserves recall on a general-purpose long-term memory benchmark; no numbers stated.
J99AInECr2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the separation of shared world facts from character beliefs well matched to long-form fiction, the evaluation broad with ablations and human assessment, and performance strong overall.
J99AInECr2.main_concern: Architectural novelty is limited since graph-based, typed, hierarchical memory and retrieval planning already exist, and the practical gain over the Full Context baseline is small given the extra inference cost.

UMOUS68i5Z.one_liner: Unlearns by editing only embedding rows of a small anchored token set selected from forget-versus-retain token distribution differences.
UMOUS68i5Z.problem: Gradient Ascent unlearning has high training cost and inconsistent retained utility, and LoRA-based approaches struggle to forget strongly without sacrificing retained utility.
UMOUS68i5Z.method: TASE exploits token distribution differences between the forget and retain sets to build a small anchored token set that maximizes forget-sample coverage while minimizing retain-side interference. Embedding-only surgical editing then updates only the corresponding embedding rows.
UMOUS68i5Z.key_idea: Select tokens that cover forget samples but interfere little with retain data, and update only those tokens' embedding rows.
UMOUS68i5Z.evidence: BERT, Phi-1.5B, and Llama-2-7B on classification, TOFU, and MUSE, with GPU memory and GPU-hour comparisons against baselines.
UMOUS68i5Z.claimed_gains: Competitive forgetting and retained utility across encoder and decoder architectures; the abstract says TASE modifies 2-5 orders of ... before it is cut off.
UMOUS68i5Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear, the method highly parameter- and compute-efficient, and the evaluation broad across architectures and unlearning benchmarks.
UMOUS68i5Z.main_concern: Novelty over prior token-embedding editing for unlearning is unclear, and the premise that editing input embeddings removes knowledge, rather than blocking entity recognition, is questioned.

RNr07fsXyz.one_liner: Flow-matching velocity field for inverse problems that applies the forward operator inside the field via alternating data-consistency and learned steps.
RNr07fsXyz.problem: Flow matching methods for inverse problems add measurements through network conditioning or sampling-time guidance, and neither explicitly applies the forward operator within the learned conditional velocity field.
RNr07fsXyz.method: FIRM expresses the optimal velocity for a linear interpolation path through the posterior mean E[x1|xt,y], shown to be the unique minimizer of a variational objective with an explicit data-consistency term. The resulting forward-operator-aware velocity field alternates data-consistency steps with learned updates, is trained end-to-end, and needs no separate guidance during sampling.
RNr07fsXyz.key_idea: Parameterize the velocity through a posterior-mean estimator unrolled as alternating data-consistency and learned updates, so the forward operator is applied in every velocity evaluation.
RNr07fsXyz.evidence: Five imaging tasks against competitive flow-based methods, with a 2D Gaussian-mixture posterior check, an ablation against A^T y conditioning, and an analysis of sampling steps versus the distortion-perception trade-off.
RNr07fsXyz.claimed_gains: Leading reconstruction quality with up to 50x fewer network evaluations than competitive flow-based methods across five imaging tasks, and the number of sampling steps controls the distortion-perception trade-off without retraining.
RNr07fsXyz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea well motivated, with a coherent link between theory and a model-based architecture, simple to implement, and consistent PSNR/SSIM results on established benchmarks.
RNr07fsXyz.main_concern: Experiments do not establish posterior sampling fidelity at image scale or that the design beats a plain conditional flow, with weak baselines and mismatched compute conditions in the comparisons.

mHZsxbr72j.one_liner: Speeds test-time depth completion with a function-space harmonic residual propagation and a spectral warm start for LoRA adaptation.
mHZsxbr72j.problem: Test-time LoRA optimization for depth completion is fragile and slow because its minimizers leave at least 95% of parameter dimensions free, so choosing a minimizer is the difficulty, and its zero initialization is degenerate.
mHZsxbr72j.method: Semiparametric residual propagation (SRP) chooses the minimizer explicitly in function space, splitting the correction into a parametric term in the predicted depth and a field harmonic on a bandwidth-free affinity graph with the measurements as constraints. A spectral warm start (SWS) replaces the degenerate initialization with the best rank-r descent step, whose amplitude is computed rather than searched.
mHZsxbr72j.key_idea: Pick the minimizer explicitly with a harmonic residual field on an affinity graph, and initialize the low-rank adapter with the best rank-r descent step instead of zeros.
mHZsxbr72j.evidence: Five benchmarks (all 6,479 evaluation images according to a reviewer) comparing against the 40-step LoRA-TTO baseline and TestPromptDC.
mHZsxbr72j.claimed_gains: 10 adaptation steps match or beat the full 40-step baseline on every metric while lowering MAE by 27% on KITTI and 31% on DDAD; SRP alone needs no backward pass, runs 30-40x faster, and lowers MAE by 22% on KITTI and 26% on DDAD.
mHZsxbr72j.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the analysis of why test-time adaptation is slow and unstable precise and well motivated, with extensive, reproducible experiments and substantial speed gains.
mHZsxbr72j.main_concern: Novelty of SRP is seen as small since harmonic interpolation on graphs is decades old, comparisons omit diffusion-based and supervised methods such as Marigold-dc, and results are weaker on sparse VOID measurements and RMSE.

sBUHukPWyS.one_liner: Transfers diffusion-classifier noise-level aggregation to a single-pass classifier via noise sampling and label smoothing derived from per-level KL contributions.
sBUHukPWyS.problem: Diffusion classifiers show robustness and human alignment but need about 10^5 forward passes per prediction, and it is unclear where their alignment comes from or whether an ordinary single-pass classifier can have it.
sBUHukPWyS.method: The authors decompose the human-alignment gap into training data, resolution, evidence aggregation across noise levels, and training objective, and find aggregation the main contributor. They measure each noise level's contribution as the reduction in KL divergence to the diffusion classifier's final prediction; the normalized contributions give a noise-sampling distribution w_gen and their cumulative sum gives a label-smoothing schedule rho for training an ordinary classifier such as ResNet-50.
sBUHukPWyS.key_idea: Use each noise level's KL contribution to a diffusion classifier's final prediction as the noise-sampling distribution and label-smoothing schedule when training a standard classifier.
sBUHukPWyS.evidence: Analysis from a toy 2D case to 64p and 224p ImageNet, training a ResNet-50 classifier and evaluating accuracy under distribution shifts, human alignment, and guidance.
sBUHukPWyS.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before the results)
sBUHukPWyS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the staged, scientific analysis insightful and the transfer of diffusion-classifier properties to a cheap single-pass classifier practical, with the noise-level information curve a useful finding.
sBUHukPWyS.main_concern: The need for and sensitivity to the expensive w_gen are unclear since a cheaper alternative gives similar gains, KL contribution is not equivalent to label reliability, and experiments stay within ImageNet-1k.

c8jn4gtPxK.one_liner: Feed-forward dynamic 3D Gaussian splatting that moves Gaussians along slot-level trajectories plus per-Gaussian residuals for urban driving scenes.
c8jn4gtPxK.problem: Feed-forward dynamic 3DGS for driving scenes suffers temporal inaccuracies and under-constrained entity-level correspondence from local or low-order motion approximations and no explicit entity constraint under self-supervision.
c8jn4gtPxK.method: TrajForward introduces learnable motion-bearing slots as latent proxies that bind dynamically related Gaussians without object annotations. A hierarchical trajectory representation decomposes motion into slot-level macroscopic trajectories and Gaussian-specific local residuals to derive target-time Gaussian centers.
c8jn4gtPxK.key_idea: Bind Gaussians to learnable motion slots and place target-time centers on slot-level trajectories plus local residuals, giving entity-level temporal correspondence without annotations.
c8jn4gtPxK.evidence: Rendering-quality and motion-accuracy comparisons in Tables 1-4 plus a speed comparison according to reviewers (the abstract is cut off before experimental details).
c8jn4gtPxK.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before the results)
c8jn4gtPxK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the hierarchical slot-plus-residual trajectory design well motivated, a sensible balance of shared motion and local flexibility, with competitive rendering and motion results.
