c8jn4gtPxK.main_concern: The provenance of baseline numbers (reproduced versus reported) and the novelty scope are unclear, and the paper lacks re-rendered videos, motion-field visualizations, and a limitations discussion.

R6IWF6WKFW.one_liner: Prioritizes high flow-matching-residual trajectory moments in continued VLA training, with importance weights preserving the original objective.
R6IWF6WKFW.problem: Uncorrected non-uniform temporal sampling in continued VLA adaptation shifts the baseline training objective, with uncertain effects under limited update budgets.
R6IWF6WKFW.method: ReTime scores trajectory moments with Flow-Matching residuals from a frozen starting policy and samples high-error moments more often. Importance correction (weights p/q) keeps the baseline continuation objective and its expected raw gradient unchanged.
R6IWF6WKFW.key_idea: Sample moments in proportion to a frozen policy's flow-matching residuals, then reweight each sample by p/q so the expected gradient matches the baseline objective.
R6IWF6WKFW.evidence: Six simulation and real-world settings with Florence and Qwen backbones, including Florence-SimplerEnv, a same-proposal controlled comparison, and a longer-horizon Florence-Phone study.
R6IWF6WKFW.claimed_gains: On Florence-SimplerEnv, 500 additional updates raise success by 24.91 points over the starting policy and 12.76 points over the strongest continuation baseline; importance correction adds 4.69 points under an identical proposal.
R6IWF6WKFW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question clear and the separation of temporal allocation from objective reweighting clean and simple, with controlled analysis and no added inference cost.
R6IWF6WKFW.main_concern: Limited statistical strength: most settings use a single continuation run and the real-world tests use only ten fixed configurations per task.

GzXi1dSKqd.one_liner: Tree-based Gromov-Wasserstein using co-depth (shared root-path length), solved exactly over leaf clusters for scalable cross-space alignment.
GzXi1dSKqd.problem: Gromov-Wasserstein is quadratic and non-convex at scale, and tree-based speedups that use only root-to-node path lengths discard pairwise tree geometry.
GzXi1dSKqd.method: T-GROW builds a hierarchy over samples and defines a GW discrepancy using co-depth, the length of the root path two samples share before diverging. It solves GW over leaf clusters, which the authors prove equals GW over the original samples under the induced tree metric.
GzXi1dSKqd.key_idea: Use co-depth as the tree similarity so that GW over compressed leaf clusters exactly equals GW over all samples under the induced tree metric.
GzXi1dSKqd.evidence: Equivalence proof for any fixed hierarchy plus a gap bound; experiments on SNARE-seq and CIFAR-100 blind matching against EGW, FlowAlign, DepthAlign, and GW (per reviews; abstract is cut off).
GzXi1dSKqd.claimed_gains: Not stated in the available abstract; reviews cite about 200x lower runtime than EGW at similar quality on SNARE-seq and 65.6% versus 30.0% for GW on CIFAR-100.
GzXi1dSKqd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit co-depth for restoring shared-ancestry information that root-only methods miss, and the exact leaf aggregation gives a practical fixed-resolution speedup.
GzXi1dSKqd.main_concern: The blind-matching results are hard to attribute: T-GROW beats full GW by a wide margin on CIFAR-100 without explanation, the matching procedure is underspecified, and no experiment isolates the tree metric's contribution.

2xzNyVFbTl.one_liner: Stores each cached token's attention output in place of its Value so later video blocks read finalized earlier outputs.
2xzNyVFbTl.problem: In autoregressive video diffusion, a token's same-layer attention output reaches later blocks only through the next layer, and a later block's loss reaches that attention only through deeper layers.
2xzNyVFbTl.method: CausalFold keeps each cached Key but replaces the cached Value with the token's attention output, so a token reads Values of its own block plus outputs of earlier, already-final blocks. This forms a finite recursion over blocks, adds no parameters, and keeps each backbone's masks, sampler, and cache schedule.
2xzNyVFbTl.key_idea: Cache attention outputs instead of Values, so each output is a convex combination of Values that recursively includes earlier blocks' outputs and passes gradient to earlier attention logits.
2xzNyVFbTl.evidence: Matched comparison against Standard-KV controls with identical training on five backbones, plus a paired human study; means over three training seeds.
2xzNyVFbTl.claimed_gains: Raises transition completion by 2.3 to 4.9 points in all six comparisons against Standard-KV controls.
2xzNyVFbTl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple and parameter-free with a clear mechanism, and the matched Standard-KV comparison across five backbones controlled and broad.
2xzNyVFbTl.main_concern: Extra cost is not offset: generation is 5.4-18.0% slower, MAGI-1's cache doubles, and training cost is unreported, so gains are not shown against Standard-KV at equal latency or memory.

mHrdi0iHY7.one_liner: Learns fixed-length discrete image tokens by updating a token message crop by crop, then decoding with flow matching.
mHrdi0iHY7.problem: Discrete image tokenizers optimized for reconstruction or compression encode local appearance rather than object-level structure.
mHrdi0iHY7.method: A single transformer processes one localized crop at a time and updates, refines, and reorganizes a fixed-length token message; after several steps the message conditions a flow-matching decoder that reconstructs the full image. Training combines flow-matching reconstruction with semantic representation-alignment objectives (SREPA).
mHrdi0iHY7.key_idea: Build the token message by iteratively rewriting it from local crops inside one shared encoder-decoder transformer, pushing tokens toward object-centric structure.
mHrdi0iHY7.evidence: Probing, compositional generalization, and relational reasoning evaluations (including Visual Genome triplets) against prior tokenizers such as FlexTok, with ablations removing SREPA and local crops.
mHrdi0iHY7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the approach simple and coherent, with clear ablations showing semantic alignment mainly helps recognition while local crops drive token-object localization.
mHrdi0iHY7.main_concern: The benefit of sequential communication is not isolated, since removing local crops also removes recurrence and extra views, and DINOv2 distillation confounds the source of the semantic structure.

7wCUWzic5B.one_liner: Estimates SDE drift from noisy trajectories by alternating Kalman smoothing with neural drift regression, gated by a variational objective.
7wCUWzic5B.problem: Regression on noisy increments amplifies measurement error, while regression on smoothed trajectories treated as exact ignores state uncertainty and dependence between consecutive latent states.
7wCUWzic5B.method: VEST alternates Gaussian Markov smoothing with neural drift learning: an iterated extended Kalman smoother proposes updates to the Gaussian approximation, and the drift regresses on conditional targets from adjacent-state moments. An acceptance rule based on a shared variational objective decides whether each proposed update is kept.
7wCUWzic5B.key_idea: Treat the smoother as a proposal and accept or reject smoother and drift updates by one shared variational objective, with drift targets using marginal and lag-one covariance moments.
7wCUWzic5B.evidence: Theory on discretization error of the variational objective and convergence of the algorithm, plus experiments against related methods such as SING and SDE Matching and a without-safeguards ablation.
7wCUWzic5B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper clear and the diagnosis of why increment regression and smoothed-mean regression fail convincing, with a sensible safeguarded design and thorough theory.
7wCUWzic5B.main_concern: The guarantees do not cover the cubature-approximated objective actually implemented, novelty over SING and standard smoothing components is unclear, and the diffusion is assumed known.

sEwLB21Bgz.one_liner: Selects salient weights for binary LLM quantization by balancing high- and low-variance activation directions via covariance-balanced alignment.
sEwLB21Bgz.problem: Reconstruction-based 1-bit post-training quantization preserves high-variance calibration directions but suppresses low-variance ones that can matter more on unseen domains.
sEwLB21Bgz.method: The paper defines a directional survivor rate comparing each principal direction's share of activation variance before and after quantization. It then proposes Covariance-Balanced Alignment (CBA), a salient-mask selection criterion that balances high- and low-variance directions when comparing full-precision and quantized representations.
sEwLB21Bgz.key_idea: Normalize full-precision and quantized activations by their covariances before comparing them, so low-variance directions weigh as much as high-variance ones in salient-mask selection.
sEwLB21Bgz.evidence: Cross-domain analysis of calibration versus unseen-domain activation spectra, and experiments across several model families on language-modeling and downstream tasks.
sEwLB21Bgz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the spectral diagnosis of calibration bias and the survivor-rate metric, and find CBA a coherent translation of that diagnosis into mask selection.
sEwLB21Bgz.main_concern: The theory (Proposition 1, FP-covariance normalization) does not match the implemented CBA, which normalizes each branch by its own covariance, so a small CBA loss need not imply high direction survival.

Hn9Rz0S8Y3.one_liner: Pretrains an EHR world model on learned state and action vectors, forced through a forecast-driven bottleneck.
Hn9Rz0S8Y3.problem: Incorporating longitudinal patient records into foundation models through next-token prediction has achieved limited success.
Hn9Rz0S8Y3.method: Local encoders map health-observation tokens to state vectors and treatment tokens to action vectors, and the model autoregressively predicts future events in that space. Local decoders generate the next state or action tokens rather than reconstructing current ones, and see prior history only through these vectors.
Hn9Rz0S8Y3.key_idea: Decoders predict the next block from history accessible only through compressed state-action vectors, so those vectors must encode patient health rather than trivial token patterns.
Hn9Rz0S8Y3.evidence: Pretraining on about 19 million patients and 28 billion record tokens with scaling laws, evaluated on disease-risk and treatment-outcome tasks including health systems unseen in pretraining, against EHR foundation model baselines at matched 1B scale.
Hn9Rz0S8Y3.claimed_gains: Not stated numerically in the available abstract (superior disease-risk and treatment-outcome performance); a review cites SS-EHR AUPRC 0.496 for HealthSAW versus 0.464 for a raw-history-access variant.
Hn9Rz0S8Y3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the forecast-driven bottleneck well isolated, since a raw-history variant reaches lower pretraining loss but worse downstream performance under matched corpus and scale.
Hn9Rz0S8Y3.main_concern: The unseen-health-system and treatment-simulation claims look overstated: the largest gain is on a same-nation system, external gains are smaller, no seeds or intervals are reported, and four of five datasets are private.

lkZqOpAEr4.one_liner: Agentic tutoring and practice-generation pipelines that share course retrieval and a learner profile revised from interaction traces.
lkZqOpAEr4.problem: Tutoring a learner and choosing what to practice next are different operations that depend on the same course material and evidence of learner difficulties.
lkZqOpAEr4.method: DeepTutor separates problem tutoring (investigate, solve with tools, write an evidence-backed explanation) from practice generation (select a learning target, then generate and validate question-answer-explanation items), sharing course retrieval and an evolving learner profile. TutorBench evaluates both outputs in multi-turn dialogue with a student simulator.
lkZqOpAEr4.key_idea: Share course-grounded retrieval and a learner profile revised from interaction traces across two distinct pipelines, tutoring and practice generation.
lkZqOpAEr4.evidence: TutorBench with 270 tasks across five disciplines and 90 learner specifications, ablations of course grounding and the learner profile, and a blind human and LLM-judge comparison with an agentic tutoring baseline.
lkZqOpAEr4.claimed_gains: Highest average scores for both tutoring and generated practice on TutorBench, and human raters and the LLM judge favor DeepTutor across all ten evaluation dimensions; no effect sizes in the abstract.
lkZqOpAEr4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the framework coherent and well written, with a broad evaluation including matched-backbone comparisons, ablations, cross-domain tests, and blind human evaluation.
lkZqOpAEr4.main_concern: The learner-profile ablation removes the profile, its updates, and traces together, so the benefit of an evolving profile is not separated from simply having memory or extra context.

mzuHSEMM3U.one_liner: A 0.6M-parameter predictor learns per-layer, per-KV-head, per-step block thresholds for sparse attention in long reasoning decoding.
mzuHSEMM3U.problem: Sparse-attention methods rank KV tokens well but budget with a fixed top-k or fixed attention-mass top-p shared across layers, heads, and queries, rather than learning budgets from output quality.
mzuHSEMM3U.method: Given a block ranking distilled from dense attention, a small predictor sets a threshold for each layer, KV head, and decoding step, and blocks whose normalized ranker scores exceed it are attended. The predictor is trained end-to-end by output-level distillation under a relaxed token budget, with the backbone and ranker frozen.
mzuHSEMM3U.key_idea: Learn the sparse-attention budget as thresholds on ranker scores, predicted per layer, KV head, and decoding step and trained by output-level distillation.
mzuHSEMM3U.evidence: Four reasoning models and six benchmarks, same-ranker comparisons, a layer-head-bias ablation, and end-to-end decoding timing mostly on Qwen3-8B on H20.
mzuHSEMM3U.claimed_gains: Up to 4.1x end-to-end decoding speedup while preserving near-full-attention reasoning accuracy.
mzuHSEMM3U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find separating KV ranking from budgeting well motivated, the method simple and practical, and the accuracy-density results across reasoning models promising.
mzuHSEMM3U.main_concern: Limited novelty: SeerAttention-R already supports threshold-based adaptive block selection, output distillation is common, and related learned-budget baselines are missing.

U8ylf6hukk.one_liner: Learns pairwise contact energy and dissipation from two-object collisions, summed over a contact graph for multi-object dynamics.
U8ylf6hukk.problem: Learned simulators of 3D deformable-object collisions usually need training on large multi-object scenes and generalize poorly to unseen object counts.
U8ylf6hukk.method: PNEO models each contacting pair's conservative energy exchange with a scalar potential and Rayleigh dissipation terms learned from two-object interactions. These pair terms are summed over the contact graph to recover multi-object dynamics.
U8ylf6hukk.key_idea: Make the interaction law pair-local, a learned scalar potential plus Rayleigh dissipation per contacting pair, so it is independent of scene cardinality.
U8ylf6hukk.evidence: A single model trained only on two-object collisions is tested zero-shot across object count (up to 50), point-cloud resolution, and mechanical properties against baselines, with spring-mass simulated ground truth.
U8ylf6hukk.claimed_gains: Zero-shot transfer from two-object training to scenes of up to 50 objects without retraining, outperforming baselines across the main multi-object settings; no error values in the abstract.
U8ylf6hukk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the zero-shot transfer from two-object training to scenes with up to 50 objects strong and the compositional pairwise inductive bias well motivated.
U8ylf6hukk.main_concern: There is no comparison with the closely related NEXUS and no runtime numbers against the numerical simulator, so the efficiency and practical advantage over generating larger training scenes are unproven.

BYc0nnzEwy.one_liner: PRM-guided test-time search that revisits a persistent pool of past prefixes via random subpools and power-weighted SMC resampling.
BYc0nnzEwy.problem: Frontier-only PRM-guided search irreversibly prunes prefixes using noisy PRM scores, causing premature commitment, diversity collapse, and loss of prefixes that still admit correct continuations.
BYc0nnzEwy.method: The search keeps a persistent pool of generated prefixes. Subpool Selection applies Top-N selection within random subpools, and Power Backtrack Sequential Monte Carlo extends SMC resampling to the pool using powered PRM scores and mixture-corrected weights.
BYc0nnzEwy.key_idea: Let search draw parents from the whole history of prefixes, not just the current frontier, via random subpool selection or power-weighted, mixture-corrected SMC resampling.
BYc0nnzEwy.evidence: Comparisons with many PRM-guided and backtracking baselines under matched token and runtime budgets, component ablations, and multiple seeds for Qwen2.5 and Phi-4 (Qwen3 reported as point estimates).
BYc0nnzEwy.claimed_gains: Not stated numerically in the available abstract; a review cites Backtrack SMC raising average accuracy from 50.88 to 52.43.
BYc0nnzEwy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear, the methods simple (Subpool Selection needs no extra training), and the experimental coverage broad, with matched-budget comparisons and ablations.
BYc0nnzEwy.main_concern: Insight beyond existing search ideas is limited, and the experiments do not fully separate the benefit of revisiting history from having a larger, more diverse candidate pool.

JfLtg8PPN2.one_liner: Shows RLVR collapses the uncertain middle class in ordinal classification; CURB recasts the middle as two one-sided cutoff decisions.
JfLtg8PPN2.problem: RLVR-trained LLM classifiers push answers toward common categories, so the rare 'cannot decide' middle category loses recall while overall accuracy rises.
JfLtg8PPN2.method: CURB (Cumulative-ray Reparameterization of the Bounded middle) rewrites the middle category as two one-sided cutoff decisions at the model's output. The authors attribute the collapse to class rarity and to the middle being a two-sided range.
JfLtg8PPN2.key_idea: Rewrite the bounded middle class as two cumulative one-sided cutoff decisions, removing the two-sided boundary that makes it collapse more than one-sided end classes.
JfLtg8PPN2.evidence: Experiments across every setting and three model families, including Biomedical QA and a pathogenicity scale (per reviews), with ablations on reward design and class difficulty.
JfLtg8PPN2.claimed_gains: CURB reduces the middle-class collapse in every setting and all three model families without making the middle dominant; no numbers in the abstract.
JfLtg8PPN2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the vanishing-middle phenomenon new and well investigated, the paper clear, and the proposed fix simple and effective.
JfLtg8PPN2.main_concern: The two-sided-boundary explanation is not directly shown, since other two-sided classes do not collapse as severely, and results focus on recall without accuracy or other-class trade-offs.

6AydDvNAPu.one_liner: A video diffusion transformer generates weights of a small executor network that carries the last latent frame through each segment.
6AydDvNAPu.problem: Video diffusion transformers spend compute on a full spatial token grid for every latent frame, although consecutive frames share most of their content.
6AydDvNAPu.method: The latent video is split into short segments; for each, the transformer generates 256 tokens forming channel-mixing matrices of a shared executor network, which applies them to the previous segment's last latent frame to produce the current segment's frames. A slot encoder is trained with the executor, then the transformer learns to generate the weights with flow matching.
6AydDvNAPu.key_idea: Generate compact per-segment transition weights instead of dense frame tokens, and apply them to a carried boundary latent frame through a small executor network.
6AydDvNAPu.evidence: Comparison with Dense models on SANA-Video 2.0, LTX-Video, and CogVideoX, with a rank bound and an error recursion for boundary-frame error growth; reviews mention LTX-Video 13B, IRASim, and segment-length ablations.
6AydDvNAPu.claimed_gains: Generates 129-frame videos 2.81-4.07x faster than Dense across SANA-Video 2.0, LTX-Video, and CogVideoX; a review cites up to 7.76x on 961-frame videos.
6AydDvNAPu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the representation change, segment transition weights applied to a carried frame, interesting and the efficiency gains substantial under broad, controlled evaluation.
6AydDvNAPu.main_concern: Gains may come from fewer transformer tokens rather than the weight representation, since no token-matched Dense baseline with coarser patching is included, and segments are limited to short lengths.

gyRJizZwIb.one_liner: Trains a prompt-only surrogate that predicts a text-to-image model's gender and race distribution without generating images.
gyRJizZwIb.problem: Auditing demographic bias in text-to-image models requires generating and classifying large image batches for every evaluated prompt.
gyRJizZwIb.method: A surrogate predicts the demographic distribution of a model's generated images directly from the prompt, using either the target model's own text encoder or an external encoder that needs no weight access. It is trained on long and short prompts paired with measured gender and race distributions for three T2I models.
gyRJizZwIb.key_idea: Regress measured demographic distributions of generated images onto prompt embeddings, so each bias audit is a single forward pass.
gyRJizZwIb.evidence: A constructed prompt dataset for FLUX.2-klein, SDXL Turbo, and Z-Image Turbo, comparisons with text-embedding and diffusion-activation probes, a 9,396 object-activity analysis, and a debiasing-pipeline test.
gyRJizZwIb.claimed_gains: Improves gender bias-detection accuracy by 11-25% over the strongest text-based or diffusion-internal baseline and raises gender fairness from 0.62 to 0.74 in a debiasing pipeline without reducing image quality.
gyRJizZwIb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea simple, practical, and useful for cheap large-scale and cross-model bias audits, including API-only models.
gyRJizZwIb.main_concern: Gains may reflect supervision rather than method (baselines use pronoun-derived labels), test prompts include gendered words, label noise is unmeasured, and the large-scale analysis was checked against real generations for only 90 combinations.

9vVrNt0PtJ.one_liner: Benchmark scoring video LLMs on object-centric sub-question chains with Faithful Accuracy, plus a trajectory-based reasoning framework, STRAND-Track.
9vVrNt0PtJ.problem: Single final-answer video benchmarks hide failures to track object identities, states, and relations over time, since queries can be solved with local cues or priors.
9vVrNt0PtJ.method: STRAND decomposes queries into human-verified sub-questions and scores Faithful Accuracy, crediting a prediction only when the target and every prerequisite sub-question are correct. STRAND-Track builds structured object trajectories via chunk-wise state extraction and temporal aggregation, then reasons over them.
9vVrNt0PtJ.key_idea: Count a video answer as correct only if all prerequisite sub-questions are also correct, and reason over explicitly extracted per-chunk object trajectories.
9vVrNt0PtJ.evidence: A benchmark of 88 videos and 977 target questions with annotation agreement kappa 0.88 (per reviews), with controls for prompts, compute budgets, scaffolding, identity linking, and oracle trajectories.
9vVrNt0PtJ.claimed_gains: Not stated in the available abstract; a review notes a gain of only 2.1 points under the strictest control, close to the paper's 2.0-point tie threshold.
9vVrNt0PtJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the benchmark a useful diagnostic of tracking failures, built on human-annotated object-centric facts with high annotation agreement and extensive experimental controls.
9vVrNt0PtJ.main_concern: The benchmark is small (88 videos, mostly yes/no questions), and under the strictest control STRAND-Track's gain is only 2.1 points, with prompting alone recovering much of the improvement.

iKBnrAng6H.one_liner: Recovers optical fields through turbulence by estimating VAE latents from unitary coded probes using turbulence-invariant Gram geometry.
iKBnrAng6H.problem: Recovering complex optical fields through atmospheric turbulence is a challenging inverse problem, and end-to-end baselines degrade under strong turbulence and small apertures.
iKBnrAng6H.method: Recovery is cast as parameter estimation: a fixed VAE compresses the field into a latent, and trainable unitary coded probes are combined with Gram geometry, which is independent of the turbulence channel under lossless reception. Finite-aperture truncation is modeled by an explicit effective metric R.
iKBnrAng6H.key_idea: Exploit the channel-invariant Gram geometry of unitary propagation, with an explicit effective metric for aperture truncation, and train only the probes while the VAE stays frozen.
iKBnrAng6H.evidence: A 2-km distributed-turbulence channel spanning 42 turbulence-aperture conditions, compared with end-to-end baselines (U-Net, NAFNet) and with fixed-probe ablations.
iKBnrAng6H.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says only that it is substantially more accurate than end-to-end baselines under strong turbulence and small apertures)
iKBnrAng6H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the physical basis sound, using Gram invariance under unitary propagation and a finite-aperture effective metric, and see measurable benefit from learned over fixed probes.
iKBnrAng6H.main_concern: The comparisons do not isolate the Gram-based design: GSCP-Net uses 12 or 15 coded probes while baselines use a different measurement protocol, so matched measurement budgets are needed.

1pcXCy4igE.one_liner: Audits LaTeX normalizers for rendering changes and builds TeXForm, a knowledge-base-driven normalizer that preserves rendering.
1pcXCy4igE.problem: Formula-recognition data pipelines and benchmark scoring silently rely on LaTeX normalizers that state nothing about what they preserve, causing false rejections and false accepts.
1pcXCy4igE.method: The paper formalizes LaTeX normalization with four properties (safety, canonicity, idempotence, coverage) and builds TeXForm, a normalizer driven by an explicit knowledge base of command argument structure and rewrite rules.
1pcXCy4igE.key_idea: Apply rewrite rules from an explicit knowledge base of command argument structure through a symbolic parser, with the knowledge built offline using LLMs.
1pcXCy4igE.evidence: Audits of dataset construction and three benchmarks (UniMER-Test, OCRBench v2, OmniDocBench) and of the CDM metric, with TeXForm compared against other normalizers using cross-renderer checks and ablations.
1pcXCy4igE.claimed_gains: Official scoring pipelines falsely reject 19-26% of render-equivalent pairs, CDM's normalizer alters rendering for 14% of inputs, and TeXForm alone preserves the rendering of over 97% of inputs while folding 37-47% of (text cut off in the available abstract).
1pcXCy4igE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem real and well formalized, and the evaluation thorough, with ablations, cross-renderer validation, and sensitivity analyses showing normalization choices can change scores.
1pcXCy4igE.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited (a parse-rewrite-serialize pipeline), and score or ranking changes alone do not show more accurate evaluation, with no comparison to existing tools after their errors are fixed.

luwUb88GQq.one_liner: Builds chain-of-thought supervision for multi-view spatial reasoning by first drawing auxiliary images, then adds confidence-guided policy optimization.
luwUb88GQq.problem: Textual chain-of-thought for multi-view spatial reasoning serializes the global spatial state into local relational statements and leaves cross-step spatial consistency implicit.
luwUb88GQq.method: View-AID externalizes task-relevant spatial hypotheses as auxiliary images before translating them into textual CoT used as training supervision, while inference uses only the original views and question. CGPO adds trace-conditioned answer confidence to binary outcome rewards.
luwUb88GQq.key_idea: Generate auxiliary diagrams of spatial hypotheses first, derive the text CoT from them, and reward traces by answer confidence conditioned on the trace.
luwUb88GQq.evidence: Qwen3-VL-4B experiments on MindCube-Tiny and MMSI-Bench, transfer to disjoint spatial reasoning tasks, and a larger backbone.
luwUb88GQq.claimed_gains: On Qwen3-VL-4B, improves MindCube-Tiny and MMSI-Bench by 48.4 and 9.4 percentage points and exceeds the strongest listed spatial baseline by 4.2 points in Overall accuracy.
luwUb88GQq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the visual-first idea intuitive and the paper clearly presented, with large gains on several spatial benchmarks and no image generation at inference.
luwUb88GQq.main_concern: The contribution of auxiliary images is not isolated, since there is no matched comparison against directly generated text CoT with the same teachers, samples, and training budget, and diagram correctness is unvalidated.

ygJLUKxykG.one_liner: Analyzes a multi-objective optimizer combining norm-constrained LMO steps with entropic task-weight updates, with rates for general norms.
ygJLUKxykG.problem: Multiple-gradient descent is usually formulated in Euclidean geometry, whereas matrix-aware optimizers use directions induced by other norms.
ygJLUKxykG.method: A single-loop method takes a norm-constrained linear-minimization-oracle step on a blended gradient while updating task weights with entropic (mirror-descent) updates. The paper proves ergodic stationarity rates, static regret for the inner weighting problem, and iteration-wise inner-gap control.
ygJLUKxykG.key_idea: Blend task gradients with entropic weights and step along a norm-constrained LMO direction, using one persistent blended-gradient momentum buffer.
ygJLUKxykG.evidence: Convergence theory for any finite-dimensional norm pair, plus experiments comparing with existing multi-task optimizers and examining oracle, weighting, and momentum choices.
ygJLUKxykG.claimed_gains: An O(T^{-1/2}) ergodic stationarity rate in the deterministic setting and O(T^{-1/4}) with stochastic gradients, with the leading term having no explicit dependence on the number of tasks.
ygJLUKxykG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the general-norm framework a useful extension that links multi-objective optimization to Signum and Muon, backed by substantial theory including the nonunique blended-gradient analysis.
ygJLUKxykG.main_concern: Novelty is unclear: the method combines known pieces (entropic task weighting, LMO descent) and overlaps substantially with the concurrent MOON in the spectral-norm case.

SaFnheCUjW.one_liner: Proves SignGD beats GD on softmax unigram learning with heavy-tailed class imbalance because GD updates rare-token logits slowly.
SaFnheCUjW.problem: Existing explanations for why adaptive and non-Euclidean optimizers beat SGD in language modeling assume smoothness or noise structure tailored to each optimizer.
SaFnheCUjW.method: The authors reduce a realistic language-modeling optimizer gap to a minimal softmax unigram model with heavy-tailed class imbalance, then prove upper and lower convergence bounds for GD and upper bounds for SignGD, including stochastic mini-batch settings.
SaFnheCUjW.key_idea: GD's logit updates shrink with token frequency so rare tokens move slowly, while SignGD removes the magnitude dependence and moves rare and common coordinates at comparable scale.
SaFnheCUjW.evidence: Experiments tracing the optimizer gap from language modeling down to a unigram model, plus deterministic and stochastic convergence bounds, including momentum variants.
SaFnheCUjW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the minimal model well motivated, the path from observation to theory convincing, and the convergence results across algorithm variants technically sound.
SaFnheCUjW.main_concern: The model is highly simplified and the stochastic result needs large batches, so how far the SignGD advantage extends to practical settings and finite batch sizes is unclear.

caB774AxZP.one_liner: Shows JEPA point prediction smooths away unpredictable CT pathology, using a 3D ViT-B JEPA trained on 113,611 CT volumes.
caB774AxZP.problem: JEPA point prediction summarizes the conditional target distribution and cannot reproduce variation the context does not resolve, which matters for sporadic pathology in CT.
caB774AxZP.method: TAP-JEPA (ViT-B/3D) is trained on 113,611 CT volumes, then the predictive pathway is audited by replaying the exact masking, teacher, and predictor computations and comparing pathology with anatomy and with matched control regions in the same organ.
caB774AxZP.key_idea: Define predictability bias as point prediction regressing toward the conditional mean, then measure it by comparing prediction skill and teacher-direction shifts for pathology versus anatomy.
caB774AxZP.evidence: Masking-replay audits and feature-space interventions on ATLAS and ReX, plus scan-level classification compared with COLIPRI, Merlin, and VoxelFM.
caB774AxZP.claimed_gains: Prediction lowers mean Skill from 0.388 to 0.271 for pathology but only from 0.921 to 0.873 for anatomy, and moves pathology 34.7% toward matched controls versus 13.6% for controls toward pathology.
caB774AxZP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question relevant and the audit strong, with a consistent pathology-versus-anatomy shortfall across two datasets and matched-region controls and feature-space interventions.
caB774AxZP.main_concern: Conceptual novelty is limited: predictability bias restates the known regression-to-conditional-mean property, which applies equally to MAE-style methods that are not audited.

SVxtUWAwAX.one_liner: Discovers complementary MILP solver-configuration portfolios using an LLM initializer and refiner that guide a model-based configurator.
SVxtUWAwAX.problem: Portfolio discovery for instance-aware MILP configuration needs expensive solver evaluations, and conventional configurators ignore parameter semantics and problem-family knowledge.
SVxtUWAwAX.method: An LLM Initializer proposes starting configurations from problem descriptions and parameter semantics, and an LLM Refiner uses portfolio performance and search feedback to focus or expand a working subspace that guides an existing model-based configurator. At deployment, a lightweight GNN selector picks a configuration with no LLM calls or search.
SVxtUWAwAX.key_idea: Inject LLM knowledge of parameter semantics into numerical configurator search by proposing initial configurations and adaptively narrowing or widening the search subspace from portfolio feedback.
SVxtUWAwAX.evidence: SCIP and Gurobi on 12 datasets, with component ablations and a transfer test to larger instances of the same problem family.
SVxtUWAwAX.claimed_gains: Not stated numerically in the available abstract; reviews report consistent improvements over default configurations on 12 datasets with SCIP and Gurobi.
SVxtUWAwAX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the integration of semantic LLM guidance with measured solver performance practical, with offline discovery, a lightweight deployment selector, and ablations supporting each component.
SVxtUWAwAX.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited since the framework mainly combines existing components, and comparisons do not fully count initialization and portfolio-evaluation costs.

lnMqah89Ay.one_liner: Streaming-video memory of activity trees under a fixed token budget, using exception-based routing and similarity-weighted token merging.
lnMqah89Ay.problem: Streaming VLM memories either grow tokens without bound or merge adjacent events, losing interleaved activity threads when tasks are interrupted and resumed.
lnMqah89Ay.method: ConcurTree organizes events into distinct activity-thread trees with an exception-based routing mechanism (a Qwen-VL judge compares events with candidate threads). It compresses history in place by similarity-weighted token merging rather than evicting or flattening it.
lnMqah89Ay.key_idea: Keep a separate tree per activity thread, link returning events to their thread by exception-based routing, and compress each tree by similarity-weighted token merging.
lnMqah89Ay.evidence: Three held-out long-video benchmarks (pooled n=1,054) including EgoLifeQA and Ego-R1, against matched fixed-budget streaming baselines.
lnMqah89Ay.claimed_gains: Reaches 50.4% pooled accuracy versus 43.1% for the strongest matched fixed-budget baseline, and 48.6% on EgoLifeQA and 39.5% on Ego-R1 under a condition cut off in the available abstract.
lnMqah89Ay.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the activity-tree memory with exception-based routing logical and well explained, a reasonable response to interrupted and resumed activities, with substantial gains on long-horizon video QA.
lnMqah89Ay.main_concern: The multi-tree structure is not shown to matter, since a single-tree memory reaches the same 50.4% pooled accuracy, and routing correctness is not directly validated.

yAx4MJmgnk.one_liner: Feed-forward novel view synthesis transformer that iterates one weight-tied block with a per-patch halting gate for adaptive depth.
yAx4MJmgnk.problem: Feed-forward novel view synthesis transformers apply a fixed amount of computation per target view although scene complexity varies, which freezes the quality-compute trade-off.
yAx4MJmgnk.method: UVSM grounds the scene once, then recursively refines each image-patch token in parallel with a single weight-tied block until a halting probability gate says to stop. The gate acts as an inference-time dial between a fast preview and a converged render.
yAx4MJmgnk.key_idea: Iterate one weight-tied transformer block per patch token until a learned halting gate fires, replacing stacked layers with adaptive recurrent depth.
yAx4MJmgnk.evidence: Seven benchmarks under the same training protocol, including out-of-distribution ScanNet and DL3DV zero-shot transfer, with architectural ablations and baselines retrained at a small budget (per reviews).
yAx4MJmgnk.claimed_gains: Beats every baseline on all seven benchmarks with the highest margins out of distribution; a review cites ScanNet +3.29 dB and DL3DV-even +1.65 dB over the best baseline.
yAx4MJmgnk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem well motivated and the architecture simple, with strong zero-shot results and broad benchmark and ablation coverage.
yAx4MJmgnk.main_concern: Novelty over existing recurrent and adaptive-computation work (Universal Transformers, PonderNet) is limited, baselines retrained at a small budget may be weak, and per-patch compute savings are not measured.

OuFCDydWCF.one_liner: Chinese logic benchmark where multi-agent hardening of human seeds and two solver-executed formalizations produce audited answers.
OuFCDydWCF.problem: Logic benchmarks either measure direct answering or generate text from formal structures that fix the formalization before the problem is written, while forward construction makes difficulty and answer reliability hard to control.
OuFCDydWCF.method: A forward-construction pipeline separates authoring from answer generation: a multi-agent workflow hardens human-authored Chinese seeds without solving them, and two independent formalizations executed by logic solvers are adjudicated under human-expert oversight. HyperLogic-Base has 195 items and 922 sub-questions, and HyperLogic-Hard has 100 items with larger, coupled search spaces.
OuFCDydWCF.key_idea: Decouple problem authoring from answer generation by deriving answers from two independent formalizations executed by logic solvers and adjudicated by human experts.
OuFCDydWCF.evidence: Seven frontier models on Base with controlled ablations on feasible worlds and cases, and tool-assisted agent evaluation on Hard comparing a code sandbox alone with one that adds a logic modeling library.
OuFCDydWCF.claimed_gains: Separates seven frontier models by 33.0 percentage points in strict item accuracy (44.6-77.6%), no model exceeds 16% on Hard in direct answering, and the sandbox improves every model by 16.7-40.1 points.
OuFCDydWCF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is difficult and discriminates between frontier models, and that separating authoring, formalization, solver execution and expert adjudication gives an auditable, low-error answer process.
OuFCDydWCF.main_concern: The pipeline design choices (four-role workflow, forward construction, two formalizations) are not validated by ablation against simpler alternatives, and LLM-based grading of long answers and residual errors are not independently assessed.

foVuCqQqvX.one_liner: Adds Subjective Logic evidence to categorical latent transitions so world models estimate doubt and propagate trust through imagined rollouts.
foVuCqQqvX.problem: World-model predictions beyond experience become unreliable, and prediction-derived uncertainty estimates can stay overconfident on unfamiliar state-action pairs.
foVuCqQqvX.method: LucidWM integrates Subjective Logic into categorical latent transitions to separate predicted outcomes from their evidential support, giving each transition a doubt value. Trust, the complement of doubt, multiplies along imagined trajectories to reweight policy-learning returns and guide action selection, with no extra parameters or forward passes.
foVuCqQqvX.key_idea: Read per-transition evidence from categorical latent heads via Subjective Logic and multiply transition trust along imagined trajectories to reweight returns.
foVuCqQqvX.evidence: Four base world models against seventeen uncertainty readouts on environment-change detection and action-corrupted rollouts, plus a controlled navigation case study.
foVuCqQqvX.claimed_gains: Acting on trust reduces the steps needed to reach the goal from 362 to 190 in a controlled navigation case study.
foVuCqQqvX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the evidence-based separation of unfamiliar transitions from spread-out predictions sound, tested against many baselines and world models, and clearly presented.
foVuCqQqvX.main_concern: The headline numbers come from single sequences or seeds (e.g., 190 versus 362 steps) while multi-seed gains are modest, and the before-decision test uses unrealistic random actions.

M4fNHbh9ma.one_liner: Learns when to disclose support information to humans via a threshold rule on estimated Value of Information under a budget.
M4fNHbh9ma.problem: Acquiring support information is costly and disclosure may fail to improve or even impair human decisions, so it is unclear when to reveal it.
M4fNHbh9ma.method: They show the optimal policy thresholds the Value of Information (the expected reduction in human decision risk), estimate regime-specific human risks, and bound the plug-in policy's degradation relative to no disclosure and its regret relative to the optimal policy.
M4fNHbh9ma.key_idea: Estimate human decision risk with and without disclosure and reveal information only where the estimated Value of Information exceeds a budget-set threshold.
M4fNHbh9ma.evidence: Benchmark datasets, two user studies, and a counterfactual benchmark that replaces participants' predictions with ML predictions when disclosure occurs.
M4fNHbh9ma.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports qualitative gains over no disclosure, full disclosure, and human-selected disclosure without numbers.
M4fNHbh9ma.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated, the formulation is natural, and the evaluation is broad, combining synthetic data, existing human-response datasets, and two user studies.
M4fNHbh9ma.main_concern: The user studies do not isolate better selection from more assistance, benefits are inconsistent across tasks (no significant gain in the email study), and the theory is seen as marginal.

xmO1vMVcQv.one_liner: HerKry reconstructs sparse-view CT with a Hermite-Gaussian hierarchy, linear-coefficient data consistency, and a Krylov-trajectory GRU.
xmO1vMVcQv.problem: Sparse-view CT relies on learned priors that are fragile under distribution shift, and coarse-to-fine hierarchies are hard to combine with data consistency because image and sinogram downsampling do not commute with fan-beam projection.
xmO1vMVcQv.method: Images are modeled by a continuous Hermite-Gaussian hierarchy moving from sparse high-order primitives to dense lower-order ones, decoupling representation resolution from measurement scale so data consistency uses native sinograms. Data consistency freezes nonlinear parameters and optimizes only linear coefficients (HC-CGLS), and a Krylov-Trajectory GRU encodes intermediate solver iterates to propagate optimization dynamics across stages.
xmO1vMVcQv.key_idea: Higher-order Hermite modes absorb spatial deformation through linear coefficients, so data consistency can freeze nonlinear parameters and solve only a linear least-squares problem with CGLS.
xmO1vMVcQv.evidence: Evaluations across cross-organ transfer, varying noise and extreme sparsity against competing methods.
xmO1vMVcQv.claimed_gains: Data-consistency latency is cut by over 90% with better fidelity, and the method outperforms competing methods by up to an amount that is cut off in the abstract.
xmO1vMVcQv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem (non-commuting downsampling and projection) well identified and the Hermite basis solution clear, with extensive comparisons and clear reconstruction improvements.
xmO1vMVcQv.main_concern: The method is hard to follow, and it is unclear how Hermite-Gaussian measurement fitting combines with supervised learning and how CGLS gradients interact with the neural branch.

fTscnIoaJx.one_liner: EMDU unlearns masked diffusion language models with anchor-first KL toward a frozen anchor whose full answer span is masked.
fTscnIoaJx.problem: The prior MDU method has two failure modes: random answer masking can leave key forget tokens visible to the anchor, and at near-one-hot predictions the anchor-last KL logit gradient vanishes, stalling training on the tokens most needing removal.
fTscnIoaJx.method: EMDU replaces MDU's anchor-last KL with the anchor-first KL toward a frozen anchor in which the entire answer span is masked, backed by theoretical and empirical analyses.
fTscnIoaJx.key_idea: Reverse the KL direction so the logit gradient stays nonzero at memorized one-hot predictions, and fully mask the answer span in the anchor to prevent leakage.
fTscnIoaJx.evidence: TOFU and RWKU (a subset of TOFU per reviews) on two model families including LLaDA, with ablations on KL direction and full answer masking.
fTscnIoaJx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the explanation of why anchor-last KL has vanishing gradients on confident predictions convincing, supported by reasonable experimental coverage and ablations.
fTscnIoaJx.main_concern: Evaluation is limited (subset of TOFU and RWKU, no MUSE or WMDP, no forget-quality metric), and EMDU often outputs empty completions, which does not show the knowledge is removed.

I90KA7L0dd.one_liner: Learns set-level uplift for agent memory retrieval, using an EVSI criterion to choose which memory sets to probe.
I90KA7L0dd.problem: Choosing which memories to retrieve together needs outcome feedback on memory sets, but evaluating each untested alternative costs an extra rollout.
I90KA7L0dd.method: UpliftMem learns set-level execution uplift relative to the same executor without memory. Under a correlated Gaussian surrogate it derives a closed-form expected value of sample information (EVSI) criterion to prioritize probes, trains a shared scorer on the feedback with the executor frozen, and needs no probing at inference.
I90KA7L0dd.key_idea: Pick memory-set probes by closed-form expected value of sample information under a correlated Gaussian surrogate, and train a shared scorer on the resulting uplift feedback.
I90KA7L0dd.evidence: ALFWorld, WebShop, BigCodeBench, and fixed-store MemSyco-Bench evaluations with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, plus matched-probe-budget comparisons against random probing.
I90KA7L0dd.claimed_gains: On fixed-store MemSyco-Bench, decision accuracy rises from 41.7% to 66.5% with Qwen3-4B and from 44.4% to 68.8% with Qwen3-8B, and EVSI beats random probing by 10.6 and 13.9 percentage points at matched probe budgets.
I90KA7L0dd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the fixed-store evaluation gives compelling evidence of retrieval improvement and that coupling set-level uplift learning with decision-aware probing is well motivated.
I90KA7L0dd.main_concern: Key comparisons are missing (set-level versus independent memory scoring, baselines suited to experiential memory), and results cover only Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B with single training runs.

f3IuZ7rXVD.one_liner: Closed-form concept erasure for diffusion models using a rectified half-space preservation constraint, a shared selector, and analytic readouts.
f3IuZ7rXVD.problem: Strict equality-based preservation constraints in closed-form editing excessively restrict the available edit space when erasing concepts from text-to-image diffusion models.
f3IuZ7rXVD.method: They formulate editing-based erasure as constrained optimization and replace equality constraints with a rectified half-space relaxation that makes retained representations inactive without forcing their preactivations to vanish. SHARE pairs a shared, residual-supervised rectified selector with analytic layer-specific closed-form readouts, avoiding joint optimization of selector and readouts.
f3IuZ7rXVD.key_idea: Retained representations only need to be inactive under a rectified selector rather than zero, which enlarges the feasible edit space, and analytic per-layer readouts apply it in closed form.
f3IuZ7rXVD.evidence: Experiments across multiple concept scales (for example 50 and 100 erased celebrities), prompt types, and model architectures, with ablations on loss components and retained-set coverage.
f3IuZ7rXVD.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims favorable trade-offs between target erasure and non-target retention, without figures).
f3IuZ7rXVD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the geometric argument for half-space preservation is clear and that retention gains over baselines are large and competitive across celebrity, implicit, and style erasure settings.
f3IuZ7rXVD.main_concern: Training, validation, and evaluation prompt splits are not specified and results lack run-to-run uncertainty, and the method is seen as an incremental combination of gated editing and analytic regression.

PTSO2gNTin.one_liner: Derives a sufficient condition for unique logit fixed points using only choice-relevant payoff changes, with a sharp universal constant.
PTSO2gNTin.problem: Stability bounds for entropy-regularized multi-agent learning that use the full payoff change count changes that leave choices unchanged, demanding more regularization than needed.
PTSO2gNTin.method: They derive a sufficient stability condition for logit responses that counts only changes altering relative action payoffs and specifies how much regularization suffices, under which responses converge to the same fixed point from every initial state. A two-action example shows the constant is sharp, and the analysis is applied to independent natural policy gradient.
PTSO2gNTin.key_idea: Bound logit-response sensitivity by the payoff change after removing components that do not alter relative action payoffs, instead of the full payoff matrix norm.
PTSO2gNTin.evidence: Theorems, a two-action example showing sharpness of the universal constant, synthetic experiments against full-payoff-matrix bounds, and natural policy gradient learning experiments.
PTSO2gNTin.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims weaker regularization requirements and sharper sampling-error bounds than full-payoff bounds, without numbers)
PTSO2gNTin.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear, the condition is intuitive and checkable, and the sharpness example gives a clean boundary for the main theorem.
PTSO2gNTin.main_concern: Theoretical novelty over existing softmax sensitivity bounds is limited, and experiments are mostly synthetic with independent natural policy gradient not directly evaluated.

TFsYuNqlg6.one_liner: Fine-tunes pathology foundation models on cross-domain distance preferences derived from multimodal LLM judgments of tile biological similarity, without labels.
TFsYuNqlg6.problem: Pathology foundation model embeddings encode institution, scanner, and stain, so tiles group by domain rather than biology, and existing mitigation needs labeled data or struggles to preserve biological signal.
TFsYuNqlg6.method: ROPAL asks a multimodal LLM to compare tile similarity (rather than label tiles) in a role-blind way, converts the judgments into cross-domain distance preferences, and fine-tunes the foundation model on them without tissue labels or paired scanner data.
TFsYuNqlg6.key_idea: Ask an MLLM which tiles are biologically more similar, not what each tile is, and train the encoder to follow those relative preferences across domains.
TFsYuNqlg6.evidence: Benchmark on eleven datasets, three foundation models, and six robustification baselines.
TFsYuNqlg6.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract reports benchmarking on eleven datasets, three foundation models and six baselines.
TFsYuNqlg6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the label-free use of MLLM similarity preferences a well-motivated, parameter-efficient approach to cross-institution robustness, evaluated across several models and datasets.
TFsYuNqlg6.main_concern: The MLLM similarity supervision (about 79% accuracy) lacks expert pathologist validation and some baselines are imperfectly optimized, so the comparison is weakened.

2Hf2YKc6K5.one_liner: Audits relation-conditioned evaluators separately for reading and verifying a declared requirement, then tests effects on best-of-n selection and guidance.
2Hf2YKc6K5.problem: A score can use a declared requirement without enforcing it, so a measurement can reveal that an output is wrong yet supply no signal to correct it, which affects selection and guidance.
2Hf2YKc6K5.method: The paper audits relation sensitivity (reading) and relation completeness (verifying) separately and proves the gap is reachable. For diffusion inverse problems the abstract describes an observation-conditioned straight-through update in which a local probe locates flat measurement coordinates and the observed residual selects where to restore a backward path, and a molecular case traces the distinction through scoring, selection and guidance.
2Hf2YKc6K5.key_idea: Test the evaluator on both sides separately: whether its score responds to the declared requirement, and whether it checks that the output satisfies it.
2Hf2YKc6K5.evidence: Diffusion inverse-problem experiments (two-bit quantization on 16 images with DAPS and JAPS), a molecular structure case with preregistered single-generator selection, and reward-model cross-tabulations cited by reviewers.
2Hf2YKc6K5.claimed_gains: Selective DAPS improves PSNR, LPIPS and SSIM on all 16 images versus uniform straight-through (+5.85 dB, -0.466, +0.354 on average), improves PSNR and LPIPS over projected smoothing (+2.74 dB, -0.190), and gains 0.55 dB in JAPS.
2Hf2YKc6K5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that an evaluator reading a requirement without verifying it is an important and often overlooked problem worth separating into two properties.
2Hf2YKc6K5.main_concern: Poor clarity and limited methodological novelty: the problem formulation is hard to follow, and the audit uses straightforward interventions while correcting the gap needs task-specific fixes.

MC3exEYUch.one_liner: Composes 3D Gaussians trained at different budgets, keeping low-budget ones unless rendered depth shows gain, to extract compact meshes.
MC3exEYUch.problem: Gaussian placement and density are driven by photometric supervision and may not match the geometry needed for compact mesh reconstruction, so denser Gaussians yield denser triangulation regardless of geometric need.
MC3exEYUch.method: Starting from the lowest-budget Gaussian set, it keeps those Gaussians where they capture the geometry and replaces them with higher-budget Gaussians only where rendered depth indicates sufficient geometric gain. The composite is then meshed with the underlying reconstruction method's own extraction procedure.
MC3exEYUch.key_idea: Allocate Gaussian density by region: start from the lowest budget and swap in higher-budget Gaussians only where rendered-depth improvement exceeds a gain threshold.
MC3exEYUch.evidence: Tests across multiple Gaussian-based surface reconstruction methods (Gaussian Wrapping, MILo and GGGS per reviews) on DeMapGS, NeRF Synthetic, Mip-NeRF 360, DTU and Tanks and Temples, reporting mesh size, Chamfer distance, F1 and mesh rendering.
MC3exEYUch.claimed_gains: Yields more compact meshes while preserving geometric quality; no numbers in the abstract.
MC3exEYUch.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the rendering-versus-meshing question is relevant and the method gives mesh-size reductions with comparable geometry across several extractors and is easy to integrate.
MC3exEYUch.main_concern: The independent value of multi-budget composition is not convincingly isolated: gains over mesh simplification are conditional, and simply selecting a mid-budget set and optimizing it keeps most of the benefit.

UEOi8APfL4.one_liner: ALPS pairs LLM-proposed structure mutations with gradient-based parameter fitting to synthesize probabilistic programs from data.
UEOi8APfL4.problem: Constructing probabilistic programs from data alone is hard because the space of structures is combinatorially large and parameter optimization requires a fixed structure.
UEOi8APfL4.method: An LLM proposes and mutates program structures, and each candidate's continuous parameters are refined by gradient-based optimization. Reviews note it builds on DeGAS's closed-form likelihood and gradients.
UEOi8APfL4.key_idea: Separate structure search from parameter fitting: an LLM proposes and mutates program structures, and gradient descent fits each candidate's continuous parameters.
UEOi8APfL4.evidence: Nine benchmarks common in the probabilistic-program literature against four baselines, averaged over 5 seeds with significance tests per reviews, plus ablations on gradient refinement, mutation, LLM feedback and LLM backend.
UEOi8APfL4.claimed_gains: Attains the best likelihood fit on average on all nine benchmarks and remains competitive in distributional distance to the ground-truth program; no numeric values stated.
UEOi8APfL4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is well written with a clear, simple pipeline and well-designed ablations, addressing the important goal of recovering human-readable generative models.
UEOi8APfL4.main_concern: The benefit of the search strategy is confounded with the stronger LLM backend (a 120B model for ALPS versus 7B for the LLM baselines), and novelty over FunSearch and LLM-SR style loops is limited.

ywkbERYvpx.one_liner: Co-evolves an indirect-prompt-injection defender with a prober that mines deferred injections still penetrating the current defender.
ywkbERYvpx.problem: Training-based defenses against indirect prompt injection are optimized on a static distribution of explicit injections, learn surface cues, and fail when malicious intent is folded into a plausible workflow and deferred for several turns.
ywkbERYvpx.method: The defender is updated each round via LoRA-based GDPO under a decoupled reward over safety, task progress, and format compliance. A co-evolving prober searches over injection rounds, methods, and payloads, guided by attack success and attack latency, to find breaches the defender notices late.
ywkbERYvpx.key_idea: Alternate defender training with a prober that mines injections the current defender misses or detects late, so each update shifts the attack distribution to a new frontier.
ywkbERYvpx.evidence: Per reviews, comparison against nine baselines and a new long-horizon benchmark (LatentDojo) judged by an LLM; the abstract text is cut off before results.
ywkbERYvpx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that delayed, workflow-embedded attacks are a useful motivation and that CoDeL reaches low attack success while keeping task utility, supported by a new long-horizon benchmark.
ywkbERYvpx.main_concern: There is no direct comparison with the closest co-evolutionary defenses (CoER and COPA), so the added benefit over them is unclear.

BGoOVJ2n1T.one_liner: Radiology report decoding that periodically scores the generated prefix against image-grounded latent semantics and injects a corrective signal.
BGoOVJ2n1T.problem: Most radiology report generation is open-loop autoregressive, with the evolving report rarely re-evaluated against image-grounded semantics during decoding, which risks inconsistent findings.
BGoOVJ2n1T.method: LCC condenses visual and textual representations into compact semantic prototypes and runs iterative latent cross-modal reasoning to obtain a unified representation. During decoding it periodically evaluates the generated prefix against image-grounded semantics and conditionally injects a lightweight corrective signal when inconsistency is detected.
BGoOVJ2n1T.key_idea: Use a shared image-text latent space as an in-decoding consistency check, converting detected prefix-image discrepancy into a corrective control signal.
BGoOVJ2n1T.evidence: Benchmark radiology report datasets (IU X-Ray per reviews) evaluated on language generation quality and clinical factual correctness against representative methods.
BGoOVJ2n1T.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says consistent improvements in language quality and clinical factuality over representative methods on most metrics, without numbers).
BGoOVJ2n1T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using a shared representation space to assess the evolving report and feed back a control signal is a meaningful design that targets hallucination in report generation.
BGoOVJ2n1T.main_concern: The decoding-time correction claim is weakly supported: ablations suggest most of the gain comes from extra training losses, the consistency signal is not validated against clinical errors, and baseline numbers are copied and omit R2GenGPT.

5NwjSNncks.one_liner: Tests whether state probes on Qwen and Gemma survive irrelevant file-history changes in controlled agent file workflows.
5NwjSNncks.problem: Probes trained to predict task state from activations are candidate monitors before destructive or out-of-scope agent actions, but their reuse when the context changes is untested.
5NwjSNncks.method: In execution-checked file histories with an exact tracker, the authors append an unrelated-file TEST and compare a fixed linear probe, model output scores, a same-site alternative, and MLP probes on pairwise accuracy and fixed-threshold accuracy. They also test feedback training and a live workflow check.
5NwjSNncks.key_idea: Evaluate probe reuse by changing irrelevant history while keeping the correct answer fixed, separating pairwise ranking from threshold accuracy and workflow completion.
5NwjSNncks.evidence: Qwen3.8-27B and Gemma-4-31B-IT on controlled file histories (32 new families), plus a live check with validation-selected MLPs that completes every case.
5NwjSNncks.claimed_gains: An unrelated-file TEST lowers a fixed Qwen linear probe's pairwise accuracy from 0.984 to 0.428 on 32 new families, while output scores retain 0.988.
5NwjSNncks.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled design (changing irrelevant history with exact labels) makes the central comparison clear and that separating ranking, threshold accuracy, and workflow completion reveals failures a single metric would hide.
5NwjSNncks.main_concern: Narrow scope and relevance: one language template, mainly one Qwen model and a simple probe, and no real agent shown to act on probe scores, so practical implications are limited.

bZEADlVnL1.one_liner: Training-free GUI grounding that turns coordinate-token perplexity into a spatial probability field guiding zoom-in proposals, triggered by a verifier.
bZEADlVnL1.problem: GUI grounding degrades on high-resolution interfaces where dense layouts and small elements exceed model input resolution, and existing refinement relies on hand-designed crops, sample consensus, or extra RL.
bZEADlVnL1.method: AutoFocus converts token-level coordinate perplexity into an anisotropic spatial probability field that guides global-local region proposals. An error-triggered verifier activates refinement only when the initial prediction is uncertain.
bZEADlVnL1.key_idea: Use the VLM's own autoregressive coordinate perplexity as an anisotropic spatial probability field to place zoom-in regions at test time.
bZEADlVnL1.evidence: ScreenSpot-Pro, ScreenSpot-V2, and OSWorld-G across general-purpose and GUI-specialized models.
bZEADlVnL1.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says consistent improvements across general-purpose and GUI-specialized models, without numbers).
bZEADlVnL1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method gives consistent gains across backbones and three benchmarks as a training-free inference enhancement, with a useful link between generation uncertainty and spatial search.
bZEADlVnL1.main_concern: Gains are not isolated from extra compute and prior refinement pipelines: latency rises about 4.6 times (3.26s to 14.91s per example), comparisons match only sampling budget, and RegionFocus and UI-Zoomer overlap.

nau33qzRKX.one_liner: Structured image annotations support controlled comparisons of JSON versus prose conditioning and pixel versus latent generation.
nau33qzRKX.problem: Unreleased large-scale JSON-annotated image corpora limit reproducible studies of annotation content, serialization, and generator design.
nau33qzRKX.method: JIG introduces 13.7M images with structured scene, style, and spatial annotations, then compares JSON and prose versions against dense captions. Four models cross pixel and latent spaces with decoupled diffusion and Transfusion-style architectures.
nau33qzRKX.key_idea: Hold structured annotation content fixed while changing its textual format, and compare generator designs across pixel and latent spaces.
nau33qzRKX.evidence: JIG-14M supports controlled caption-format experiments, four-model comparisons, and reported GenEval2 and PRISM evaluations.
nau33qzRKX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the large annotated dataset and controlled experiments separating annotation format from content.
nau33qzRKX.main_concern: Annotation quality and coverage complicate attribution of generation improvements to particular supervision properties.

SYmRZugAVX.one_liner: Physics-guided mesh allocation and geometry-conditioned feature transport separate sampling choices from interactions in adaptive neural operators.
SYmRZugAVX.problem: Node relocation changes representation contexts, so direct aggregation can mix physical variation with discretization effects.
SYmRZugAVX.method: GA-AMNO uses physics-informed allocation to place spatial samples and geometry-conditioned low-rank transport to map source features into target contexts before aggregation. Separate computational pathways support interventions on allocation and interaction.
SYmRZugAVX.key_idea: Map source features into each target node's geometric representation context through low-rank transport before aggregating messages.
SYmRZugAVX.evidence: Reviewers report evaluations across five PDE benchmarks and interventions examining the roles of allocation and interaction.
SYmRZugAVX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate explicitly separating mesh allocation from feature interaction and evaluating their roles.
SYmRZugAVX.main_concern: The evidence does not isolate a distinctive benefit of gauge-inspired transport beyond existing edge-conditioned kernels or added architectural capacity.

3Txu9VXQZj.one_liner: Independent positional clocks decouple speech and internal reasoning streams so full-duplex models tolerate changing decoding speeds.
3Txu9VXQZj.problem: Shared positional clocks make changes in internal reasoning speed alter audio-token distances and disrupt full-duplex speech models.
3Txu9VXQZj.method: RUBATO assigns independent clocks through multistream positional encoding, decoupling audio timing from thinking-token progress. Training at two extreme decoding speeds supports interpolation to intermediate inference rates.
3Txu9VXQZj.key_idea: Encode each stream with an independent positional clock so thinking-token progress does not change audio-stream timing relationships.
3Txu9VXQZj.evidence: Evaluation covers five spoken reasoning tasks, fixed and varying thinking budgets, single-turn reasoning, and synthetic overlapping conversations.
3Txu9VXQZj.claimed_gains: At interpolated speeds on Spoken GSM8K, the abstract reports 1.7% baseline accuracy and a RUBATO-Full accuracy range beginning at 48.7%.
3Txu9VXQZj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the positional-mismatch diagnosis and independent-clock mechanism clear and empirically supported.
3Txu9VXQZj.main_concern: Missing intermediate-budget training baselines leave the advantage over broader speed augmentation unestablished.

pGsviSLDzU.one_liner: Jointly evolving evidence interfaces and reading procedures improves frozen multimodal agents through failure-guided skill revision.
pGsviSLDzU.problem: Reusable multimodal skills depend on both which evidence an agent receives and how it interprets that evidence.
pGsviSLDzU.method: ViewCraft evolves executable observation selection, transformation, and arrangement together with reading instructions. Failure traces propose revisions, replay and paired evaluation select changes, and interface projection salvages visual edits from eligible rejected joint proposals.
pGsviSLDzU.key_idea: Co-optimize an executable visual-evidence interface and its reader using paired evaluations of failure-driven revisions.
pGsviSLDzU.evidence: Eight benchmarks include token-matched controls, restricted and alternative search strategies, component ablations, and transfer across executors.
pGsviSLDzU.claimed_gains: ViewCraft improves average task score by 6.1 points over direct execution and uses 8–15% fewer input tokens than Initial skill on all five multi-source tasks.
pGsviSLDzU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the joint evidence-and-reading design well motivated and the controlled experiments supportive of the gains.
pGsviSLDzU.main_concern: Comparative and statistical claims need clearer accounting because adapted baselines restrict scope and some reported scores and uncertainty calculations require reconciliation.

AVnMPAMcKx.one_liner: Certified probabilistic bracketing restricts sorting to threshold-adjacent scores for scalable exact-budget differentiable soft top-k.
AVnMPAMcKx.problem: Hard top-k is nondifferentiable, while soft alternatives become expensive at very large coordinate counts.
AVnMPAMcKx.method: Fast LapSum uses kernel-noised sampling and order-statistic bracketing to localize the threshold, aggregating outside-tail contributions. A linear certification pass verifies localization, with full sorting as a fallback.
AVnMPAMcKx.key_idea: Sort only the ambiguous threshold band while retaining exact tail contributions and certifying the resulting selection mass.
AVnMPAMcKx.evidence: GPU timing tests reach 10^8 scores, with gradient checks and applications to megapixel sparse adversarial examples and 3D Gaussian splatting.
AVnMPAMcKx.claimed_gains: The certified implementation processes 10^6, 10^7, and 10^8 scores in median times of 0.92, 1.39, and 7.24 ms, respectively, and reports an order-of-magnitude speedup for sparse adversarial examples.
AVnMPAMcKx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value localized solving with exact tail contributions, certification, and demonstrations at large application scales.
AVnMPAMcKx.main_concern: The paper insufficiently distinguishes inherited LapSum algorithms and measures speedups against weak reference implementations rather than stronger optimized solvers.

k8FG3HZdQa.one_liner: Value-norm and output-rank diagnostics distinguish attention sinks that suppress updates from sinks that distribute shared information.
k8FG3HZdQa.problem: Visually similar attention sinks can conceal different computations, making attention concentration alone difficult to interpret.
k8FG3HZdQa.method: The study formalizes adaptive NOP and broadcast mechanisms on synthetic tasks and tests their signatures in pretrained vision transformers. Causal and architectural interventions examine gating, register tokens, and a position-free global pathway.
k8FG3HZdQa.key_idea: Separate sink mechanisms by near-null value norms for suppression and low-rank shared outputs for broadcast.
k8FG3HZdQa.evidence: Synthetic tasks, pretrained vision-transformer diagnostics, causal interventions, and gating/register/global-pathway experiments test the proposed mechanisms.
k8FG3HZdQa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the mechanistic distinction and controlled interventions connecting toy tasks to vision-transformer behavior.
k8FG3HZdQa.main_concern: Broadcast-like signatures do not yet clearly establish input-specific information transfer or generalize across models and architectural interventions.

rrZiabt0DH.one_liner: A separate explorer seeks uncertain states that imagined main-policy rollouts predict are recoverable toward expert behavior.
rrZiabt0DH.problem: Conservative imitation policies undersample uncertain useful regions, while unrestricted uncertainty exploration can collect task-irrelevant dynamics.
rrZiabt0DH.method: RECON separates the conservative task policy from a real-environment exploration policy. The explorer rewards epistemic uncertainty conditioned on recoverability estimated through multi-step main-policy imagination.
rrZiabt0DH.key_idea: Gate uncertainty-driven exploration by whether the main policy can return from a state toward expert behavior.
rrZiabt0DH.evidence: Locomotion, navigation, and manipulation experiments measure interaction efficiency, imitation performance, model errors, and robustness to unseen perturbations.
rrZiabt0DH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find recoverability-guided data collection well motivated and the robustness and world-model results promising.
rrZiabt0DH.main_concern: Gains over broader prior methods are modest or insufficiently demonstrated beyond the detailed CMIL comparisons.

JD3XLNNlwi.one_liner: Executable image-examination code and decision-level reinforcement learning teach a medical agent to inspect and correct diagnostic evidence.
JD3XLNNlwi.problem: Medical VLMs can answer correctly from population priors while failing to perform the measurements or localized examinations a diagnosis requires.
JD3XLNNlwi.method: CodeLancet trains a 4B agent on skill-guided, rubric-audited demonstrations and outcome-based GRPO to examine images through code. Focal-PPO uses local outcome-change credit to target decisions within examination trajectories.
JD3XLNNlwi.key_idea: Represent examinations as executable image operations and train individual decisions using their estimated effect on expected outcomes.
JD3XLNNlwi.evidence: Three medical imaging tasks include retinopathy grading and ejection-fraction assessment, with matched fixed-tool comparisons, training-stage ablations, and physician reviews.
JD3XLNNlwi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value executable medical examination and the ablations examining tool interfaces and training stages.
JD3XLNNlwi.main_concern: Process-quality improvements rely mainly on the same model judge used during training, without independent comparisons across training stages.

MwK3UtexbN.one_liner: Sharp heterogeneity thresholds and coordinate-dependent counterexamples characterize when Adam converges or diverges.
MwK3UtexbN.problem: Aggregate gradient heterogeneity alone may not explain Adam convergence under fixed memory parameters and changing coordinate geometry.
MwK3UtexbN.method: The paper derives scalar inequalities and convergence thresholds, then constructs positive-definite quadratic counterexamples with a shared minimizer. It analyzes how coordinate normalization, conditioning, and dimension affect divergence despite low aggregate heterogeneity.
MwK3UtexbN.key_idea: Show how coordinatewise normalization amplifies tiny conflicting gradients that barely affect aggregate heterogeneity.
MwK3UtexbN.evidence: One-dimensional convergence proofs, restricted trajectory analyses, and high-dimensional counterexamples cover cyclic, reshuffled, and IID sampling.
MwK3UtexbN.claimed_gains: In one dimension convergence holds for C<2 and examples diverge at C=2+O(log n/n), while high-dimensional divergence can occur as C tends to one and every C<1+1/p is safe in dimension p.
MwK3UtexbN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the sharp scalar analysis and counterexamples separating aggregate heterogeneity from coordinate geometry.
MwK3UtexbN.main_concern: The sharp multidimensional characterization remains restricted to special trajectories or memoryless settings, limiting conclusions for general Adam runs.

vrFV5ixfnb.one_liner: Geometry-aware orbit generation and cross-stage regional source access condition coarse-to-fine single-image 3D reconstruction.
vrFV5ixfnb.problem: A fixed keyframe subset can omit views needed to recover particular self-occluded regions in single-image 3D generation.
vrFV5ixfnb.method: V23D adapts Wan2.2 with noise-decoupled LoRA and an orbit adapter to generate turntable priors. Its Regional Source Adapter records coarse-stage source-frame indices and attention masses, then lets shape-stage queries reread those patches.
vrFV5ixfnb.key_idea: Carry regional source references across stages while allowing refinement queries to reread their original visual details.
vrFV5ixfnb.evidence: HY3D-Bench-test and Toys4K evaluations include full-orbit controls for all-frame aggregation, current-state routing, and fixed-feature transfer.
vrFV5ixfnb.claimed_gains: V23D lowers FVD from 205.8 to 176.8, reaches 0.2418 ULIP-I and 0.3827 Uni3D-I, and improves F-score@1% from 57.4% to 61.1%, with 62.7% on Toys4K.
vrFV5ixfnb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate separating source selection from detail reading and the ablations comparing cross-stage alternatives.
vrFV5ixfnb.main_concern: The RSA training schedule and rendered-versus-generated view setup need clarification to assess reproducibility and the training-inference gap.

MyRfVzMNI4.one_liner: Alternating task-specific budget adaptation and likelihood-guided policy optimization trains agents across varying execution budgets.
MyRfVzMNI4.problem: Agents trained for fixed or predefined budgets may perform poorly across the resource limits encountered in deployment.
