yoVbNsRK03.method: PFedMA tracks agent capability and reliability, evaluates responses before aggregation, and refines subsequent queries using collaboration feedback. Clients generalize local privacy rules and selectively adopt global rules through bidirectional rule evolution.
yoVbNsRK03.key_idea: Couple feedback-driven multi-round orchestration with selective local-to-global and global-to-local privacy-rule updates.
yoVbNsRK03.evidence: Experiments span reasoning, privacy-sensitive, and adversarial settings with routing, query-refinement, reliability, and rule-update ablations.
yoVbNsRK03.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see value in jointly adapting collaboration quality and reusable privacy rules while keeping client data decentralized.
yoVbNsRK03.main_concern: Output-leakage measurements do not establish protection against server inference or cumulative disclosure under genuinely distinct client requirements.

2owqx5bgiB.one_liner: Shares a contact-energy bottleneck between antibody binding-site prediction and affinity ranking using alternation over separately annotated datasets.
2owqx5bgiB.problem: Residue-level binding-site and complex-level affinity tasks have complementary signals but scarce joint annotations.
2owqx5bgiB.method: CoBALT forms partner-conditioned residue representations and factorizes pairwise interactions into contact and energy-like fields. Alternating multitask training uses separate binding-site pairs and affinity candidate sets to train the shared bottleneck.
2owqx5bgiB.key_idea: Factor shared pairwise interactions into interface contacts and affinity contributions so disjoint task labels can train a common representation.
2owqx5bgiB.evidence: Five-fold evaluations include random and homology-aware splits, task-specific baselines, predicted-contact analysis, and single-fold component ablations.
2owqx5bgiB.claimed_gains: CoBALT reports epitope/paratope AUPRCs of 65.60%/88.58%, BAR Spearman improvement from 0.64 to 0.70, and Precision@1 from 50.77% to 56.99%.
2owqx5bgiB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value connecting interface prediction and affinity ranking through a shared representation trained without dual annotations.
2owqx5bgiB.main_concern: Single-fold component ablations and incomplete uncertainty reporting do not establish consistent, statistically reliable bottleneck gains.

hyoaz4AE7X.one_liner: Chains adjacent-frame matches with learned stopping and per-channel retention to replace quadratic temporal attention in video diffusion.
hyoaz4AE7X.problem: Endpoint-based sparse attention can break motion tracks, while unrestricted propagation can harm temporal coherence.
hyoaz4AE7X.method: PathSpan scores local neighboring-frame windows plus a no-match option and composes matches through two linear-time scans. Per-channel retention sets temporal reach, and within-frame attention selects carried content.
hyoaz4AE7X.key_idea: Construct long-range temporal connections by composing local motion routes with channel-specific reach and an explicit stopping option.
hyoaz4AE7X.evidence: Wan2.2, LTX-Video, and Cosmos-Predict2.5 experiments compare matched dense fine-tuning and ablate routes, propagation, retention, stopping, and spatial attention.
hyoaz4AE7X.claimed_gains: Complete generation is 1.52–4.03× faster than matched dense fine-tuning with VBench totals within 0.05 points.
hyoaz4AE7X.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the motion-route motivation, component ablations, and evaluation across several pretrained video models.
hyoaz4AE7X.main_concern: Missing factorized space-time attention comparisons leave the specific benefit of route-following temporal attention unclear.

eAngnY8TPN.one_liner: Adapts video segments and sampled-frame counts to visual dynamics for open-vocabulary relationship detection.
eAngnY8TPN.problem: Uniform temporal segmentation and frame budgets under-sample dynamic relations and waste observations on stable ones.
eAngnY8TPN.method: The method segments videos using changes in optical flow and bounding-box layouts, then predicts frame counts from appearance and motion. MLLM-derived pseudo-supervision trains observation budgets, and selected evidence is fused with whole-segment context.
eAngnY8TPN.key_idea: Predict pair-segment observation budgets from temporal dynamics rather than assigning every segment the same number of frames.
eAngnY8TPN.evidence: Two benchmark evaluations cover novel and all-category settings with supervision, segmentation, and observation-budget ablations.
eAngnY8TPN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find adaptive evidence allocation sensible and the experiments supportive of its accuracy-computation trade-off.
eAngnY8TPN.main_concern: The comparative evaluation needs clarification because baseline provenance and inconsistent reported baseline mAP values weaken interpretability.

Tlffy1vOZ2.one_liner: Routes edit gradients through selected sparse-autoencoder features while optimizing preservation with separate unmasked gradients.
Tlffy1vOZ2.problem: Low-rank knowledge edits can alter broad internal directions and disrupt unrelated model behavior.
Tlffy1vOZ2.method: SAE-Locked LoRA uses normalized edit-loss attribution to choose a bounded sparse-feature set covering a target mass. It routes edit gradients through that fixed set while applying preservation gradients through an independent unmasked pass.
Tlffy1vOZ2.key_idea: Restrict only the edit-loss gradient to edit-specific SAE coordinates while leaving preservation gradients unrestricted.
Tlffy1vOZ2.evidence: CounterFact, matched ReCoE, and 100 sequential edits accompany objective-matched coordinate controls, regularizer factorials, cross-backbone tests, and bypass-path analysis.
Tlffy1vOZ2.claimed_gains: CounterFact success is 99.6% versus 99.8%, locality 89.5% versus 63.7%, and KL drift 0.16 versus 0.65; gains over PCA are 7.5 locality points (95% CI [6.7, 8.3]), ReCoE scores are 49.8% exact match and 28.5% micro correct_flip, and 100-edit retention is 91.8% versus 18.2% for MEMIT and 8.4% for vanilla LoRA.
Tlffy1vOZ2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the precise gradient-routing mechanism and controls beyond comparisons with unregularized LoRA.
Tlffy1vOZ2.main_concern: Headline comparisons confound routing with preservation regularization, while sequential-editing evaluations omit stronger preservation-oriented baselines.

9SxsrLIsLR.one_liner: Fits cross-domain persona elicitation relationships and varies fine-tuned layer depth to control trait transfer.
9SxsrLIsLR.problem: Narrow fine-tuning can induce undesirable traits in unrelated domains, with transfer difficult to predict from data alone.
9SxsrLIsLR.method: The study measures relationships between in-domain and out-of-domain persona elicitation across models and fine-tuning settings. It tests whether moving updates to later layers reduces transfer while retaining trained behavior.
9SxsrLIsLR.key_idea: Predict cross-domain trait rates from in-domain elicitation and control their relationship through the depth of updated layers.
9SxsrLIsLR.evidence: Experiments cover five models, two personas, varied tuning configurations, held-out-model/family prediction, alternative judges, and matched in-domain comparisons.
9SxsrLIsLR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the safety-relevant question and broad experimental examination of persona transfer and its control.
9SxsrLIsLR.main_concern: Uneven held-out prediction and sizable errors do not establish reliable predeployment prediction despite strong fitted relationships.

Qk6ZCxL1aW.one_liner: Diagnoses failures across visual evidence acquisition, reading, and grounding to guide teachers and reweight on-policy distillation.
Qk6ZCxL1aW.problem: Visual-agent errors propagate through actions, resulting observations, and reasoning without stage-specific correction in existing distillation approaches.
Qk6ZCxL1aW.method: ReVuE compares multiple student trajectories for a query, summarizes visual evidence, and diagnoses the first failed stage. These reflections guide teacher feedback and token-level distillation grouping and weighting.
Qk6ZCxL1aW.key_idea: Condition teacher supervision on cross-trajectory diagnoses of where the visual evidence chain first fails.
Qk6ZCxL1aW.evidence: Experiments cover two model families and 11 benchmarks, with reflection/reweighting ablations, grouping controls, and human checks of critic diagnoses.
Qk6ZCxL1aW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the acquisition-reading-grounding distinction and its conversion into targeted training supervision.
Qk6ZCxL1aW.main_concern: Comparisons do not isolate stage-specific diagnosis from the critic's richer information, reference answers, and extra training compute.

eGl0SCqeRA.one_liner: Applies doubly robust post-hoc isotonic regression to calibrate right-censored survival curves from Deep Cox models.
eGl0SCqeRA.problem: Deep Cox proportional-hazards models achieve strong risk discrimination on censored multimodal data but often output poorly calibrated survival probability distributions.
eGl0SCqeRA.method: The authors construct augmented inverse-probability-of-censoring weighted (AIPCW) pseudo-outcomes using a conditional censoring model and apply two-dimensional monotonic isotonic regression over Deep Cox risk scores and time horizons. This post-hoc recalibration refines survival probability curves while preserving risk-score ordering and enjoys asymptotic double-robustness and threshold-calibration guarantees.
eGl0SCqeRA.key_idea: Project doubly robust censoring-adjusted pseudo-outcomes onto a bivariate monotone surface over risk score and time via post-hoc isotonic regression.
eGl0SCqeRA.evidence: Asymptotic double-robustness and misspecified-score calibration theorems alongside empirical evaluations on synthetic survival simulations and real-world clinical time-to-event datasets.
eGl0SCqeRA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining AIPCW pseudo-outcomes with isotonic regression provides a mathematically grounded, doubly robust post-hoc framework for calibrating censored Deep Cox survival predictions.
eGl0SCqeRA.main_concern: Reviewers point out that full distribution consistency relies on a strong risk-score sufficiency assumption (ordering true conditional survival curves at all times) and sensitivity to finite-sample censoring-probability clipping.

7Hz8XOtleF.one_liner: Pairs queue-normalized inverse-gap exploration with discounted dual updates to decouple regret from violation in constrained bandits.
7Hz8XOtleF.problem: Prior primal-dual algorithms for constrained contextual bandits with general regression oracles couple regret bounds to dual-queue bounds, causing regret rates to degrade with constraint-violation difficulty and Slater margins.
7Hz8XOtleF.method: The proposed primal-dual algorithm scales inverse-gap exploration weights by (1 + q_t^2)^(-1) using the virtual constraint queue q_t and applies a discounted dual regulator update. This quadratic queue normalization prevents dual amplification of oracle prediction error while negative quadratic drift absorbs the extra exploration penalty, decoupling regret from dual-process bounds.
7Hz8XOtleF.key_idea: Normalize inverse-gap exploration by quadratic virtual-queue length and discount dual updates so oracle error does not scale with queue size.
7Hz8XOtleF.evidence: Regret and constraint-violation proofs under general feasibility and unknown-margin Slater feasibility, accompanied by contextual bandit simulations using XGBoost regression oracles.
7Hz8XOtleF.claimed_gains: For every theta in [1/2, 1] and cumulative oracle error bound U, achieves O-tilde(T^theta U^(1-theta)) regret and O-tilde(T^(1-theta/2) U^(theta/2)) violation under general feasibility, improving violation to O-tilde(min{sqrt(TU)/epsilon, T^(1-theta/2) U^(theta/2)}) under Slater margin epsilon > 0.
7Hz8XOtleF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining quadratic queue-normalized inverse-gap exploration with dual regularization cleanly decouples regret from the Slater margin and sharpens polynomial rates over prior oracle-based bounds.
7Hz8XOtleF.main_concern: Reviewers note incremental advancement over classical Lyapunov drift-plus-penalty analyses, omitted action-count dependence and matching lower bounds, and mismatched empirical comparisons using XGBoost oracles at a single theta=1/2 setting without ablations.

lMgjnXrWPA.one_liner: Distills tool-cropped forgery evidence into single-pass bounding-box chains of thought and refines localization with tag-level RLVR.
lMgjnXrWPA.problem: Smaller multimodal LLMs struggle at fine-grained image forgery detection and localization unless aided by slow multi-round external image-cropping tool calls at inference time.
lMgjnXrWPA.method: Region-to-Fake (R2F) cold-starts a student MLLM by distilling multi-round image-cropping trajectories and bounding-box coordinates from a teacher model into a single tool-free Chain-of-Thought pass with structured thinking and bounding-box tags. It then applies Perceptual-Aware RL with Verifiable Rewards (PA-RLVR) using tag-sequence-level importance sampling to refine forgery classification and localization.
lMgjnXrWPA.key_idea: Distill teacher multi-crop forensic trajectories into single-pass bounding-box reasoning traces and optimize them via verifiable RL with tag-sequence importance sampling.
lMgjnXrWPA.evidence: Evaluated across multiple fake image detection and localization benchmarks (including LOKI and RTM) against forensic detectors and MLLM baselines such as Qwen3-VL-8B and TruFor.
lMgjnXrWPA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that internalizing multi-crop regional forensic evidence into single-pass structured reasoning traces removes inference-time tool latency while producing inspectable bounding-box explanations.
lMgjnXrWPA.main_concern: Reviewers point to internal numerical contradictions in benchmark tables (such as overall accuracy falling below both class accuracies), unverified teacher-generated pseudo-boxes for fully synthetic images, and unclear localization evaluation protocols.

QjveSVx834.one_liner: Decomposes training SQL queries into an offline derivation graph and embeds natural-language questions for one-step structural example retrieval.
QjveSVx834.problem: Semantic Text-to-SQL retrievers miss SQL structural relationships, while structure-based retrievers require generating a preliminary draft SQL query online that increases token and latency costs.
QjveSVx834.method: Derivation-SQL decomposes training SQL queries into subqueries linked in an offline SQL derivation graph (DG) and trains a DG-based embedding network (DGE) that aligns natural-language questions with graph-structured SQL representations. At inference time, it embeds the input question directly to retrieve structurally relevant few-shot examples without a preliminary SQL generation pass.
QjveSVx834.key_idea: Encode subquery derivation graphs offline into a shared question-SQL embedding space to retrieve structurally relevant Text-to-SQL examples without draft SQL generation.
QjveSVx834.evidence: Evaluated on BIRD and Spider Text-to-SQL benchmarks (including GPT-4o on BIRD-Dev) with retriever comparisons against semantic, AST, and SQL-structure baselines.
QjveSVx834.claimed_gains: With GPT-4o, Derivation-SQL achieves 72.56% execution accuracy on BIRD-Dev with low token consumption.
QjveSVx834.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that shifting SQL structural modeling into offline graph construction and vector indexing avoids online preliminary SQL generation overhead while achieving competitive BIRD and Spider accuracy.
QjveSVx834.main_concern: Reviewers note that ablations conflate graph topology with subquery data augmentation and synthetic question pairs, alongside unfair cost comparisons and insufficient differentiation from prior structure-aware retrievers (DCG-SQL and ReFSQL).

WMS0ypYjwm.one_liner: Routes across CNN, Transformer, and state-space experts using cross-expert response interactions for generalizable deepfake detection.
WMS0ypYjwm.problem: Mixture-of-experts deepfake detectors typically restrict experts to a single architecture family and route solely from input features without comparing how heterogeneous experts actually respond to forensic cues.
WMS0ypYjwm.method: CAEIR evaluates convolutional, Transformer, and Mamba state-space experts in parallel, summarizes their candidate outputs as evidence nodes, and models cross-expert interactions to refine an input-conditioned Top-1 router. A separate bounded modulator scales only the winning expert's response before injecting it into the detection residual.
WMS0ypYjwm.key_idea: Execute heterogeneous CNN, Transformer, and state-space experts and model interactions among their summarized responses to refine Top-1 expert routing.
WMS0ypYjwm.evidence: Trained on FaceForensics++ real videos with online synthetic fake supervision across three seeds and evaluated cross-dataset on Celeb-DF v2, DFD, DFDC, and FFIW with expert-pool and routing ablations.
WMS0ypYjwm.claimed_gains: Trained on FF++ real videos with online synthetic fake supervision, CAEIR achieves three-seed video-level AUCs of 96.26 ± 0.38% on Celeb-DF v2, 95.22 ± 0.52% on DFD, 81.66 ± 0.49% on DFDC, and 90.46 ± 1.00% on a fourth benchmark.
WMS0ypYjwm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining CNN, Transformer, and Mamba experts with response-conditioned routing is well motivated for heterogeneous forensic artifacts and achieves strong cross-dataset generalization under single-source training.
WMS0ypYjwm.main_concern: Reviewers note that computing all four experts to inform Top-1 routing makes inference computationally dense (nearly doubling latency), while ablations do not fully separate cross-expert interaction from extra parameters and simpler response-conditioned routers.

qKZewFbAXh.one_liner: Jointly calibrates weight and activation clipping for analog in-memory computing via safeguarded Newton steps on coupled-error surrogates.
qKZewFbAXh.problem: Digital clipping methods ignore output-side analog-to-digital converter (ADC) quantization error in analog in-memory computing, while grid-search calibration is slow and suboptimal for coupled operand-and-ADC errors.
qKZewFbAXh.method: IMC-CLINIC formulates an analytical surrogate for analog IMC matrix-multiplication output error that couples activation and weight rounding, coherent clipping-induced bias, and rescaled ADC quantization noise. Using closed-form gradients and approximate curvature computed from compact calibration statistics, it optimizes weight and activation clipping thresholds via safeguarded Newton iterations.
qKZewFbAXh.key_idea: Minimize an analytical surrogate coupling operand rounding, coherent clipping bias, and ADC quantization error using safeguarded Newton iterations over calibration statistics.
qKZewFbAXh.evidence: Evaluated on four LLMs under simulated analog IMC quantization against digital W/A grid-search and ADC-aware alternating coordinate-search baselines, with surrogate-term ablations.
qKZewFbAXh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explicitly coupling operand clipping, clipping bias, and output-referred ADC quantization error captures a genuine hardware difference from digital quantization and accelerates calibration.
qKZewFbAXh.main_concern: Reviewers point out incomplete cross-model comparisons against matched ADC-aware empirical MSE optimization to isolate the surrogate and Newton benefit, as well as unmodeled analog circuit non-idealities such as device variation.

4WL15hFfNo.one_liner: Derives finite-noise random-feature learning curves showing diffusion score-matching bias rises at p~n while double-descent peaks at p~nm.
4WL15hFfNo.problem: Although denoising score matching minimizes a quadratic regression loss where overparameterization is classically benign, overparameterized diffusion models exhibit catastrophic memorization rather than generalization.
4WL15hFfNo.method: The authors derive closed-form test-loss and bias-variance decompositions for a random-features denoising score-matching model trained with n samples, p parameters, and m fixed noise realizations per sample, alongside experiments on U-Nets trained on CelebA. The analysis separates convergence toward the memorizing empirical score from generalization to the true population score.
4WL15hFfNo.key_idea: Solve a finite-noise random-features denoising score-matching model analytically to separate score-bias growth at p~n from variance double descent at p~nm.
4WL15hFfNo.evidence: Closed-form asymptotic learning curves and bias-variance decompositions in a random-features diffusion model paired with overparameterized U-Net training experiments on CelebA.
4WL15hFfNo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extending random-features diffusion theory to finite noise realizations per sample clarifies where double descent occurs (p~nm) versus when memorization bias sets in (p~n).
4WL15hFfNo.main_concern: Reviewers note that practical diffusion training operates far below the finite-m interpolation scale (making finite-m peaks unreachable at realistic model sizes) and critique unclear connections between Theorem 2.1 and the main text.

dbB7Ni8kVL.one_liner: Selects PTQ calibration coresets via corrected greedy price-weighted moment herding to preserve pairwise quantization configuration rankings.
dbB7Ni8kVL.problem: Diversity- and activation-coverage criteria for selecting post-training quantization calibration data do not directly control distortion in pairwise rankings among candidate quantization configurations.
dbB7Ni8kVL.method: Price-Preserving Calibration Coresets (PPCC) decomposes pairwise quantization price-gap distortion and formulates calibration selection as a price-weighted moment-matching problem. It selects samples using a greedy herding algorithm augmented with a finite-population correction term that minimizes expected terminal moment discrepancy.
dbB7Ni8kVL.key_idea: Match price-weighted activation moments using a greedy herding selector with a terminal-discrepancy correction term to preserve pairwise quantization configuration costs.
dbB7Ni8kVL.evidence: Finite-pool concentration and moment-discrepancy proofs alongside post-training quantization experiments on 1B–8B Llama and Qwen models (including Llama-3.2-1B) against Random, ZipCal, and CoverCal baselines.
dbB7Ni8kVL.claimed_gains: Recovers the full-pool quantization price minimizer at all three tested budgets on Llama-3.2-1B.
dbB7Ni8kVL.reviewer_consensus: Supportive reviewers appreciate the decision-oriented theoretical framing that ties calibration coreset selection directly to preserving quantization configuration preferences via bounded price-gap distortion.
dbB7Ni8kVL.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing component ablations isolating price weighting and the finite-pool correction from standard herding, heavy mathematical presentation omitting key implementation details, and evaluation limited to 1B–8B models with higher selection runtime.

KBvTQnVpIp.one_liner: Selects informative rows and features for black-box tabular foundation models via iterative KernelSHAP regression and multi-fidelity pruning.
KBvTQnVpIp.problem: Tabular foundation models suffer from context-length limits and performance degradation when inference datasets are large, noisy, or augmented beyond pretraining size distributions.
KBvTQnVpIp.method: VIP-COP performs black-box hard context compression for tabular foundation models by iteratively sampling candidate subsets, scoring validation predictions without model internals, and fitting an online KernelSHAP-based regression to estimate sample and feature importance. Value-guided context sampling and multi-fidelity pruning refine discrete subsets of high-value rows and features under an anytime compute budget.
KBvTQnVpIp.key_idea: Estimate per-sample and per-feature predictive importance via online KernelSHAP regression on black-box validation scores with value-guided sampling and multi-fidelity pruning.
KBvTQnVpIp.evidence: Evaluated on tabular classification tasks under standard, data-augmented, and noisy or contaminated settings across tabular in-context backbones including TabPFNv1.
KBvTQnVpIp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that black-box selection of informative samples and features without accessing model internals is intuitive and practical for scaling tabular foundation models to larger or noisy contexts.
KBvTQnVpIp.main_concern: Reviewers note potential validation-set overfitting and unfairness from optimizing directly against validation accuracy, restriction to classification on older backbones (TabPFNv1 rather than TabPFNv2 or v3.5), and insufficient budget-matched comparisons against established selectors.

mShsvnQnYt.one_liner: Gradient decomposition links target learning and learning rates to when RL or SFT retains capabilities.
mShsvnQnYt.problem: The common claim that RL post-training forgets less than SFT lacks an account of when that advantage reverses.
mShsvnQnYt.method: The authors decompose SFT gradients into capability and supervision components, relate binary-reward on-policy RL to the capability component, and analyze retention through first-order and nonlinear update effects.
mShsvnQnYt.key_idea: Initialization, supervision compatibility, and learning rate control target gains and non-target gradient interactions, determining relative retention.
mShsvnQnYt.evidence: Controlled experiments vary Qwen and Llama models, target tasks, and learning rates, supported by gradient and Taylor-expansion analyses of non-target cross-entropy.
mShsvnQnYt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the capability–supervision decomposition offers a useful explanation and that counterexamples challenge blanket retention claims for RL.
mShsvnQnYt.main_concern: Reviewers most often argue that proposed explanations are not systematically isolated across the broad experiments or matched checkpoint-selection procedures.

0tGiz42faO.one_liner: MAX-Cache corrects motion-misaligned activations and selectively recomputes mismatched tokens across video chunks.
0tGiz42faO.problem: Cross-chunk activation reuse accelerates video diffusion but fails under ego motion, moving objects, parallax, and occlusion.
0tGiz42faO.method: MAX-Cache gates whole-prefix reuse with a learned residual corrector and otherwise routes low-mismatch tokens to motion-aligned cached outputs while recomputing high-mismatch tokens.
0tGiz42faO.key_idea: Mismatch-guided token routing combines motion-aligned cache reuse with fresh updates only where cached features disagree.
0tGiz42faO.evidence: Four-seed experiments report end-to-end timing, short- and long-horizon generation quality, and component ablations on an autoregressive driving generator.
0tGiz42faO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that gated correction and selective recomputation form a reasonable acceleration method with a workable speed–quality tradeoff.
0tGiz42faO.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite narrow evaluation on one backbone, dataset, view, resolution, and GPU, alongside incomplete calibration-cost accounting.

1UcrS30WXL.one_liner: DoobImp conditions an unconditional diffusion backbone with Doob's h-transform and iterative incomplete-data fitting.
1UcrS30WXL.problem: Artificial masking during diffusion-imputation training couples learning to a mask distribution that may not match test missingness.
1UcrS30WXL.method: DoobCond approximates conditional reverse diffusion for observed entries, while DoobFit alternates imputation and unconditional-score refitting on incomplete training data.
1UcrS30WXL.key_idea: Doob's h-transform supplies inference-time conditioning without training the backbone under artificial masks.
1UcrS30WXL.evidence: Experiments compare 17 baselines on nine tabular datasets under three missingness mechanisms and evaluate four time-series datasets with pointwise and structured missingness.
1UcrS30WXL.claimed_gains: DoobImp attains an average MAE rank of 1.19 and the highest aggregate categorical accuracy across nine tabular datasets.
1UcrS30WXL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that mask-free conditioning is practical and supported by broad tabular and time-series experiments.
1UcrS30WXL.main_concern: Reviewers most often question methodological novelty and missing matched comparisons with posterior-guidance and earlier mask-free imputation methods.

ZYSU20zoD5.one_liner: Representation and intervention analyses show tool mediation raises and weakens effective refusal mechanisms.
ZYSU20zoD5.problem: Harmful requests receive fewer refusals in tool-mediated interactions than conversations, but the internal mechanism is unclear.
ZYSU20zoD5.method: Matched conversational and tool-mediated prompts are compared through representation geometry, neuron analyses, threshold measurements, and progressive refusal-computation interventions.
ZYSU20zoD5.key_idea: Tool mediation preserves harm representations but changes their conversion into refusal through higher thresholds and greater intervention brittleness.
ZYSU20zoD5.evidence: The study evaluates eight open-weight models from five families across matched intents, multiple tool framings, and causal ablations.
ZYSU20zoD5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that holding requests and weights fixed across eight models provides useful controlled evidence about channel-dependent refusal.
ZYSU20zoD5.main_concern: Reviewers most often argue that measurements confound perceived harm with refusal and use different refusal criteria for conversational and tool settings.

Q5X79cYBFQ.one_liner: SWE-Serve tests repository-scale inference features with hidden regression, serving, and performance checks.
Q5X79cYBFQ.problem: Existing coding benchmarks rarely evaluate production inference features spanning model support, runtime execution, and public APIs.
Q5X79cYBFQ.method: SWE-Serve derives 53 SGLang tasks across six engineering families and runs CPU or single-H100 evaluation with hidden tests, E2E serving checks, performance gates, and no-op and oracle controls.
Q5X79cYBFQ.key_idea: Executable production-serving tests evaluate full-stack patches rather than isolated kernels or local repository behavior.
Q5X79cYBFQ.evidence: The benchmark evaluates 11 models and 31 model–effort configurations with closed-book execution and adversarial verifier review.
Q5X79cYBFQ.claimed_gains: Across 11 models and 31 model–effort configurations, the best-performing configuration achieves 75% mean pass@1.
Q5X79cYBFQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that real checkpoints, serving paths, and careful task controls give the benchmark practical value for inference engineering.
Q5X79cYBFQ.main_concern: Reviewers most often question score validity and whether E2E gaps reflect cross-component serving behavior rather than test coverage or complexity.

SNSSqi18BW.one_liner: GyroFlow samples saturated 5D gyrokinetic states directly from operating parameters using latent flow matching.
SNSSqi18BW.problem: Gyrokinetic simulations must resolve costly transient dynamics before reaching the statistically steady states needed for analysis.
SNSSqi18BW.method: GyroFlow uses a Swin5D autoencoder and conditional latent flow matching to generate saturated phase-space snapshots from noise under an ergodicity assumption.
SNSSqi18BW.key_idea: Conditional distribution sampling replaces autoregressive time evolution by treating steady-state ensemble samples as time averages.
SNSSqi18BW.evidence: Experiments evaluate saturated 5D gyrokinetic snapshots and steady-state statistics against autoregressive surrogates and cold-start simulation.
SNSSqi18BW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that direct steady-state modeling addresses a major computational bottleneck and suits high-dimensional gyrokinetic data.
SNSSqi18BW.main_concern: Reviewers most often question limited methodological novelty and whether ergodic sampling remains valid with multiple attractors or metastability.

xBECSvN8L2.one_liner: STaRC cross-predicts spectral and temporal views, then calibrates few-shot activity features with Bayesian relations.
xBECSvN8L2.problem: Cross-dataset activity recognition must transfer heterogeneous motion representations while modeling uncertainty from scarce target labels.
xBECSvN8L2.method: STCP pretrains by bidirectionally predicting temporal and spectral views across ten harmonized IMU datasets, and BRC samples relational graphs and routes base-knowledge experts during adaptation.
xBECSvN8L2.key_idea: Bayesian relational graph sampling calibrates target features using multiple base-class experts under few-shot uncertainty.
xBECSvN8L2.evidence: Experiments evaluate several shot settings and self-supervised and few-shot baselines on cross-dataset wearable activity recognition, especially PAMAP2 and UCI HAR.
xBECSvN8L2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating transferable pretraining from few-shot relational adaptation is sensible and yields substantial PAMAP2 gains.
xBECSvN8L2.main_concern: Reviewers most often find BRC's uncertainty contribution unisolated and note mismatches between the described training procedure and supplied implementation.

W0wPiGw2VI.one_liner: Decouples hyperbolic vision-language training using angular alignment for semantics and radial-angular order cones for hierarchical entailment.
W0wPiGw2VI.problem: Hyperbolic vision-language objectives entangle semantic similarity and hierarchy in radial coordinates, creating conflicting geometric constraints.
W0wPiGw2VI.method: AURORA aligns image-text semantics purely via angular similarity while modeling partial-order entailment with Radial-Angular Order Cones (RAOC) whose apertures depend on relative parent-child radial gaps, stabilized by norm regularization.
W0wPiGw2VI.key_idea: Assigns semantic matching to hyperbolic angles and hierarchical entailment to radial-gap-conditioned order cones with norm regularization.
W0wPiGw2VI.evidence: Trains on millions of image-text pairs and evaluates zero-shot classification, retrieval, hierarchical reasoning, and compositional understanding.
W0wPiGw2VI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the geometric decoupling of angular semantics and radial hierarchy clean and mathematically well supported.
W0wPiGw2VI.main_concern: Baseline numbers for HyCoCLIP and PHyCLIP are substantially lower than published results, and WordNet hierarchy metrics are confounded by classification accuracy.

8dbA0S2cWG.one_liner: Steers frozen VLA policies at test time by adding optimized residuals to high-attention visual action-register tokens.
8dbA0S2cWG.problem: Test-time steering of VLA policies typically alters action samplers rather than visual backbone representations for zero-shot spatial control.
8dbA0S2cWG.method: RegiSteer identifies uninformative visual patches that receive concentrated action-token attention (action registers) and optimizes test-time residuals on those tokens to steer Cartesian motion without updating policy weights.
8dbA0S2cWG.key_idea: Applies test-time residual perturbations to high-attention visual action-register tokens to steer frozen VLA end-effector trajectories.
8dbA0S2cWG.evidence: Evaluates across generalist and specialist VLA policies in simulation (including LIBERO-PRO) and small-scale real-world demonstrations.
8dbA0S2cWG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the action-register phenomenon interesting and the training-free encoder-output intervention architecture-agnostic.
8dbA0S2cWG.main_concern: Steering is limited to free-space 3D waypoint reaching barely outperforming an IK baseline, and online gradient steering triples inference latency (57 ms to 177 ms).

4TcBqwETJL.one_liner: Autoformalizes stochastic optimization proofs in Lean using proof-obligation-driven construction, revision contracts, and an independent Judge.
4TcBqwETJL.problem: Revising Lean models during proof construction to restore provability risks silently weakening or altering the original mathematical theorem.
4TcBqwETJL.method: ProofLoom drives Lean formalization from open proof obligations, records model changes in source-linked signature contracts checked by an independent Judge, decomposes arguments via a Planner-Audit loop, and stores verified developments in SOptLib.
4TcBqwETJL.key_idea: Constrains iterative Lean formalization with proof-obligation selection and source-linked signature contracts policed by an independent Judge.
4TcBqwETJL.evidence: Evaluates on 15 textbook and research-paper stochastic optimization tasks against six baselines and builds 33 verified developments.
4TcBqwETJL.claimed_gains: Obtains mean human ratings of 6.3/7 and 6.4/7 versus 4.9/7 and 5.0/7 for the strongest of six baselines, producing 490,693 lines of verified Lean code across 33 developments.
4TcBqwETJL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the focus on preventing semantic drift during autoformalization and the substantial Lean implementation and evaluation.
4TcBqwETJL.main_concern: Main comparisons give ProofLoom accumulated SOptLib support unavailable to baselines, and individual components closely resemble prior agentic proving workflows.

wsELxUE6SR.one_liner: Prunes LLM-judged soft constraints to at most one per instruction during RLVR while retaining all code-verifiable hard constraints.
wsELxUE6SR.problem: Scaling instruction-following RL with multi-constraint LLM judges introduces severe false-positive reward noise that degrades policy learning.
wsELxUE6SR.method: H1S retains all code-verifiable hard constraints and prunes soft constraints to at most one per prompt, confining LLM-as-a-judge evaluation to its reliable single-constraint regime based on verifier-precision diagnostics.
wsELxUE6SR.key_idea: Retains all deterministic hard constraints while capping LLM-judged soft constraints at one per prompt to preserve RLVR reward precision.
wsELxUE6SR.evidence: Combines verifier audits and noise-injection studies with RLVR experiments across 7B and 32B models on five instruction-following benchmarks.
wsELxUE6SR.claimed_gains: Achieves average gains of 11.3% (7B) and 6.7% (32B) over base models across five benchmarks, beating mixed-constraint training by 5.5% at 7B.
wsELxUE6SR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find H1S simple, actionable, and effective, cutting 32B step latency from 19.63 to 8.23 minutes.
wsELxUE6SR.main_concern: The core insight that reward precision matters is incremental, overlap with TinyJudge results is under-clarified, and noise-injection/diversity controls are confounded.

oJ0ETOCP6A.one_liner: Prices shared-memory writer reputation by reader closed-book failure probability and adds forgetting to prevent stale or undeserved credit.
oJ0ETOCP6A.problem: In multi-agent shared memory, readers answering correctly from parametric knowledge reward writers of false facts, and old reputation persists after writers turn unreliable.
oJ0ETOCP6A.method: Priced Reputation Learning (PRL) weights writer credit on successful tasks by the probability the reader would fail without memory and incorporates a forgetting mechanism so reputation tracks changing writers.
oJ0ETOCP6A.key_idea: Scale shared-memory writer credit by the reader's counterfactual closed-book failure probability and decay past reputation to handle non-stationary writers.
oJ0ETOCP6A.evidence: Theoretical lock-in analysis and experiments across six memory conditions and twelve readers from five model families support PRL.
oJ0ETOCP6A.claimed_gains: Unpriced reputation returns a correct fact on only 20.4% of reads when writers turn false, whereas PRL reaches the writer oracle to within reader variation.
oJ0ETOCP6A.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating reader-knowledge leakage from stale reputation provides a sharp failure diagnosis and clean mechanism.
oJ0ETOCP6A.main_concern: Reviewers note that evaluation uses two slices rather than a full condition-by-reader grid without oracle confidence intervals, and task-level credit is heuristic rather than causal across co-served facts.

VzpCr9i3I7.one_liner: Learns discrete action codes from observational data and lifts code policies back to structured actions via the behavior system.
VzpCr9i3I7.problem: Off-policy improvement with structured actions like text or images suffers from weak action-level overlap and decoder approximation errors.
VzpCr9i3I7.method: PolicyLift learns discrete high-level action codes, optimizes a context-dependent policy over those codes, and deploys it by querying the historical behavior system conditioned on the selected code.
VzpCr9i3I7.key_idea: Eliminate deployment mismatch and decoder training by optimizing a policy over discrete action codes and generating actions via code-conditioned queries to the behavior policy.
VzpCr9i3I7.evidence: Theoretical value-improvement guarantees and synthetic plus real-world text generation experiments (including OfflinePrompts) support the framework.
VzpCr9i3I7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating code-level policy improvement from behavior-conditioned lifting cleanly addresses deployment mismatch without training a new decoder.
VzpCr9i3I7.main_concern: Reviewers note unclear presentation in Section 4, missing stage ablations and baselines, reliance on querying the behavior system at deployment, and limited semi-synthetic text validation.

nArH632i3v.one_liner: Proves non-monotonic algorithmic stability bounds showing privacy helps generalization at high noise but hurts it at low noise under Byzantine attacks.
nArH632i3v.problem: Prior trilemma results link Byzantine robustness, local differential privacy (LDP), and optimization error, leaving generalization error regimes uncharacterized.
nArH632i3v.method: Connecting Byzantine attack strength to membership inference attacks (MIA), the authors derive matching upper and lower bounds on algorithmic stability under LDP and Byzantine robustness across privacy regimes.
nArH632i3v.key_idea: Link Byzantine-induced instability to membership inference capability to prove opposing privacy effects on stability in high-noise versus low-noise regimes.
nArH632i3v.evidence: Theoretical stability bounds (Theorem 3.1) and numerical experiments on logistic regression and CNNs under Opt-IPM attacks support the characterization.
nArH632i3v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the non-monotonic privacy-robustness-generalization analysis and the connection to membership inference attacks theoretically interesting.
nArH632i3v.main_concern: Reviewers note that the theory bounds worst-case uniform stability rather than actual generalization error, lacks tightness in intermediate regimes, and relies on assumptions needing tighter proof justification.

eUcR9yXyYg.one_liner: Pools frozen omni audio features into one speaker token per segment and adapts the LLM via LoRA for memory routing.
eUcR9yXyYg.problem: Omni models can process speech and text but cannot natively link utterances to enrolled speaker identities for conversational memory routing.
eUcR9yXyYg.method: An attention-based speaker pooler over a frozen omni audio encoder produces one continuous exchangeable token per speaker or segment, without an external speaker encoder. The language model is lightly adapted with LoRA so its middle layers separate same-speaker from cross-speaker turns for routing and multi-party tracking.
eUcR9yXyYg.key_idea: Attention pooling over frozen omni audio features mints one continuous speaker token, and light LoRA adaptation teaches the LLM to route memory with it.
eUcR9yXyYg.evidence: Experiments evaluate speaker verification, memory routing, and multi-party benchmarks across LibriSpeech, VoxCeleb1-O, SpeakerBind, M3-SLU, and three non-Qwen backbones.
eUcR9yXyYg.claimed_gains: Lifts unseen LibriSpeech routing accuracy from 24.8% to over 97%, lowers VoxCeleb1-O EER from 42.13% to 11.87%, and beats CAM++ clustering by 6.0% on SpeakerBind (85.2% vs. 79.2%).
eUcR9yXyYg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers note the finding that speaker information in a token is insufficient without adapting the LLM to use it, along with promising routing and verification numbers.
eUcR9yXyYg.main_concern: Reviewers criticize presentation and missing details in the main body, limited LLM backend evaluations, and small novelty given that cosine matching alone outperforms the adapted LLM.

i2EdO6YkEj.one_liner: Combines Adam-ES zeroth-order search with cached reference routes to find adversarial coordinate perturbations for neural routing solvers.
i2EdO6YkEj.problem: Neural routing solvers achieve low average optimality gaps on standard benchmarks but suffer severe local vulnerabilities under small geometric perturbations.
i2EdO6YkEj.method: Reference-Route Reuse Attack (RRA) maximizes the optimality gap under bounded coordinate perturbations using Adam-ES, which merges evolution strategies with adaptive momentum. To avoid costly exact-solver calls per candidate, RRA scores perturbations against cached recent reference routes and refreshes the reference after each update.
i2EdO6YkEj.key_idea: Pairing Adam-ES zeroth-order optimization with cached reference-route reuse exposes adversarial coordinate perturbations in neural routing solvers at low solver cost.
i2EdO6YkEj.evidence: Experiments attack six TSP/CVRP solvers (24 TSP and 15 CVRP configurations) and test adversarial fine-tuning.
i2EdO6YkEj.claimed_gains: Greedy probing raises mean gaps 4-38x on 100-node TSP; RRA increases mean best-found gap over greedy by 18.3-39.5% and cuts search-time reference solves by 96.94%.
i2EdO6YkEj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exposing local perturbation vulnerabilities in neural routing solvers is a relevant angle and that reference-route reuse substantially improves attack efficiency.
i2EdO6YkEj.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological novelty in combining Adam-ES with route caching, single-seed evaluations, and weak evidence that adversarial fine-tuning generalizes beyond the attacked model.

RAXN0NrLQP.one_liner: Generalizes score matching to non-conservative vector fields via a projected Fisher objective admitting arbitrary stationary-distribution dynamics.
RAXN0NrLQP.problem: Score-based generative models are restricted to learning the unique conservative data score vector field, preventing direct imposition of structural or dynamical priors.
RAXN0NrLQP.method: Flux Matching relaxes the score-matching target using a projected Fisher divergence objective that admits infinitely many non-conservative vector fields sharing the data as their stationary distribution. This freedom lets practitioners shape sampling dynamics for speed, interpretability, or directed variable dependencies.
RAXN0NrLQP.key_idea: Minimizing a projected Fisher divergence admits non-conservative vector fields with the data stationary distribution, turning the generative dynamics into a design choice.
RAXN0NrLQP.evidence: Theoretical derivation of the projected Fisher objective paired with experiments on high-dimensional image datasets, faster sampling, and structured/directed dynamics.
RAXN0NrLQP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that generalizing score matching to non-conservative stationary-distribution vector fields is theoretically sound and an interesting conceptual direction.
RAXN0NrLQP.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical advantage over standard score matching and note missing comparisons against simpler baselines and prior non-conservative dynamics literature.

14Cp3A2kOi.one_liner: Broadcasts a validation-derived TKNN-Shapley valuation function built from LDP reports so providers estimate data value locally.
14Cp3A2kOi.problem: Data valuation in markets requires assessing a record's task-dependent value before purchase without forcing providers to disclose raw sensitive data.
14Cp3A2kOi.method: PIVOTS collects one locally differentially private (LDP) randomized report per provider and combines it with buyer validation data to broadcast a valuation function. Each provider evaluates this function on its retained raw record (and optional public features) to estimate its TKNN-Shapley contribution locally.
14Cp3A2kOi.key_idea: Broadcasting a valuation function built from single LDP reports and validation data lets providers compute their data value on retained raw records without disclosure.
14Cp3A2kOi.evidence: Establishes MSE upper bounds and matching minimax lower bounds, plus synthetic and real-world experiments under full and partial LDP.
14Cp3A2kOi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that enabling data valuation before raw-record disclosure under local differential privacy is a practical and well-motivated problem.
14Cp3A2kOi.main_concern: Reviewers question trust assumptions on seller-side self-evaluation, incremental novelty over existing LDP/KNN-Shapley methods, and unclear controlled gains over random selection.

uOnPLYpEi4.one_liner: Trains a contextual-bandit RL router over four complete LLM agent workflows to enforce clinical nutrition redline rules.
uOnPLYpEi4.problem: Applying a single fixed LLM agent workflow to all clinical nutrition queries wastes compute on simple cases and misses redline safety checks on complex ones.
uOnPLYpEi4.method: NutriAgent-RL trains a contextual-bandit router on frozen LLM outputs to select among Direct Answer, RAG, Multi-agent Reasoning, and Fixed Revision based on parsed patient context. Offline training uses rule-grounded critics scoring redline compliance alongside workflow cost.
uOnPLYpEi4.key_idea: A contextual-bandit router trained with rule-grounded critic rewards and cost penalties selects among four complete LLM workflows per patient context.
uOnPLYpEi4.evidence: Evaluations measure rule compliance, routing agreement (RouteMatch), and efficiency across clinical nutrition queries with redline rules.
uOnPLYpEi4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that routing between complete agent workflows for rule-grounded clinical nutrition advice is practical and well-framed.
uOnPLYpEi4.main_concern: Reviewers note missing adaptive-router baselines, unclear validation of the redline rule bank, and an unresolved numerical inconsistency in Qwen DCA scores (candidates summing to 32.9% vs. router 82.9%).

WwFl5oMZuN.one_liner: Adds epoch-wise periodic momentum resetting to zeroth-order SGDM to achieve optimal dimension dependence in nonsmooth nonconvex optimization.
WwFl5oMZuN.problem: Classical zeroth-order SGD methods suffer from extra smoothness or dimension dependencies in existing analyses for nonsmooth nonconvex objectives.
WwFl5oMZuN.method: The authors analyze a zeroth-order SGD with momentum (ZO-SGDM) variant that retains standard SGDM updates while adding an epoch-wise outer loop with periodic momentum resetting. They exploit the recursive averaging structure of momentum to bound the oracle complexity for Lipschitz-continuous objectives.
WwFl5oMZuN.key_idea: Periodic epoch-wise momentum resetting combined with recursive averaging isolates the dimensional penalty to zeroth-order gradient estimation rather than SGDM optimization dynamics.
WwFl5oMZuN.evidence: Theoretical complexity analysis for finding (delta, epsilon)-stationary points of Lipschitz-continuous nonsmooth nonconvex objectives.
WwFl5oMZuN.claimed_gains: Achieves an oracle complexity of O(d * delta^-1 * epsilon^-3), matching the best-known dependence on d, delta, and epsilon.
WwFl5oMZuN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses an interesting theoretical problem with clear motivation, presentation, and comparisons to prior work.
WwFl5oMZuN.main_concern: Reviewers note incremental novelty since the rate only matches prior best-known complexity, limited experimental validation, and insufficient discussion of optimality lower bounds and global Lipschitz assumptions.

WBLUYlTW3x.one_liner: Selects sparse, traceable neuron-time-scale coordinates using conditional mutual information followed by grouped out-of-fold residual scoring.
WBLUYlTW3x.problem: Latent-component neural decoders obscure individual neuron and spike-time traceability, while static information rankings ignore what the current readout already captures.
WBLUYlTW3x.method: The authors introduce Residual-Informed Sparse Decoding (RISD), which first selects an information core via conditional mutual information and then iteratively adds multiscale Haar coordinates using grouped out-of-fold cross-entropy residuals computed from training data only.
WBLUYlTW3x.key_idea: Pairing a conditional mutual information core with grouped out-of-fold residual scoring selects sparse, traceable neuron-time-scale features conditioned on the current decoder.
WBLUYlTW3x.evidence: Image-identity and semantic decoding experiments on neural recordings from marmoset retina, mouse visual pathway, and macaque visual cortex.
WBLUYlTW3x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the interpretable, traceable neuron-time-scale feature selection and the broad evaluation across three species and visual processing stages.
WBLUYlTW3x.main_concern: Reviewers note limited algorithmic novelty in combining WCMI with residual selection and missing comparisons against standard sparse decoders like L1 or group-lasso logistic regression.

w7vcAOHNNk.one_liner: Mitigates majority-concept feedback loops in abductive learning via progressive knowledge-base expansion and distribution-prior score rectification.
w7vcAOHNNk.problem: Under skewed concept distributions, abductive learning amplifies early majority-concept bias through pseudo-label feedback from logical abduction.
w7vcAOHNNk.method: The authors propose DPRP-ABL, which progressively expands nested knowledge sub-bases to limit ambiguous candidate competition early in training and rectifies candidate scoring using estimated concept distribution priors to counteract majority-favoring dilution.
w7vcAOHNNk.key_idea: Progressive expansion of nested knowledge sub-bases paired with distribution-prior score rectification prevents majority concepts from dominating early abductive pseudo-labels.
w7vcAOHNNk.evidence: Theoretical analysis of candidate selection and ground-truth feasibility preservation, plus experiments on two tasks (digit addition and judicial sentencing) under concept skewness.
w7vcAOHNNk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper clearly formulates how concept skewness creates a biased feedback loop in abductive learning.
w7vcAOHNNk.main_concern: Reviewers raise a major concern about potential ground-truth concept leakage in phase stratification metadata, limited novelty over curriculum ABL and prior adjustment, and missing comparison to C-ABL.

rVwheNHlum.one_liner: Designs polynomial-time linear contract algorithms using cost/outcome predictions with worst-case robustness and consistency guarantees.
rVwheNHlum.problem: Principals designing linear contracts lack algorithms that achieve near-optimal utility under accurate predictions while remaining robust to arbitrary prediction errors.
rVwheNHlum.method: The authors formulate linear contract design with predictions of action costs and outcome distributions and propose two algorithms—including a breakpoint-based polynomial-time method—that balance consistency and worst-case robustness.
rVwheNHlum.key_idea: Combines prediction-guided contract selection with pessimistic breakpoint buffering to guarantee both consistency and worst-case approximation bounds.
rVwheNHlum.evidence: Purely theoretical upper and lower approximation-ratio bounds.
rVwheNHlum.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear formulation and novelty of integrating machine-learned predictions into linear contract design.
rVwheNHlum.main_concern: Reviewers flag potential mathematical flaws in Theorems 1 and 4 (missing positivity conditions), triviality of some robustness bounds, and restrictive single-agent assumptions.

fiL9cazF0K.one_liner: Couples fast predictor updates with an LLM adaptation agent evolved via online field-weighted DPO from candidate plan outcomes.
fiL9cazF0K.problem: Continual spatiotemporal forecasting methods use prescribed rules for when, where, and how to adapt rather than learning adaptation decisions from evolving states.
fiL9cazF0K.method: CoEvoST uses an LLM agent that retrieves diagnostic evidence over multiple rounds to select an adaptation plan, executes candidate plans from the same checkpoint, and updates its policy via online field-weighted DPO.
fiL9cazF0K.key_idea: Co-evolves predictor adaptation with an LLM decision policy trained via online DPO on realized outcomes of candidate adaptation plans.
fiL9cazF0K.evidence: Forecasting experiments across multiple spatiotemporal domains including AIR and CAMELS-13.
fiL9cazF0K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that state-dependent adaptation strategy selection is well-motivated for evolving spatiotemporal streams.
fiL9cazF0K.main_concern: Reviewers question the added value of an LLM over simpler policies given only nine predefined strategies and rule-based diagnostics, and note missing runtime/cost details and underspecified main-text mechanics.

UUcPqCJLiM.one_liner: Steers frozen masked diffusion language models from pure masks using a membership-trained hidden-state corrector to extract alignment data.
UUcPqCJLiM.problem: Extracting post-training alignment data from masked diffusion language models typically requires target prefixes or costly sampling and filtering.
UUcPqCJLiM.method: D-Miner generates candidate completions from fully masked inputs, ranks them by membership signals, and trains a lightweight corrector on top candidates to shift intermediate hidden states of the frozen DLM toward alignment-data recovery.
UUcPqCJLiM.key_idea: Trains a lightweight hidden-state steering corrector on a frozen DLM's own membership-ranked generations to recover alignment data starting from pure masks.
UUcPqCJLiM.evidence: Supported by an ideal-corrector distribution theorem and experiments across 12 target DLMs (SFT and RL) plus downstream coding utility tests.
UUcPqCJLiM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find mask-only extraction from DLMs an interesting problem and note consistent recovery gains over equal-budget sampling on all 12 targets.
UUcPqCJLiM.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing non-member/held-out similarity controls (to separate true extraction from generic in-domain generation), no random-selection ablation for the corrector, and impractical white-box hidden-state access assumptions.

fJKhNhHcvB.one_liner: Learns frequency-invariant material parameters via 3D Gaussian ray tracing and Fresnel equations for cross-band RF prediction.
fJKhNhHcvB.problem: Radio-frequency digital twins tied to a single frequency band fail on unseen bands, while multi-band measurement surveys are costly.
fJKhNhHcvB.method: FresGRT models scenes with 3D Gaussian ray tracing and learns frequency-invariant material parameters grounded in Fresnel equations and frequency-selective fading, using a staged training pipeline on single-band RF measurements.
fJKhNhHcvB.key_idea: Parameterizes 3D Gaussians with physical material properties governed by Fresnel equations and staged fading optimization so single-band RF data generalizes to unseen bands.
fJKhNhHcvB.evidence: Evaluated on a real robotic RGBD + Nexmon CSI testbed (three sites, three bands) and 24 simulated ray-tracing datasets.
fJKhNhHcvB.claimed_gains: Achieves unseen-band prediction with a mean error of 4.4 dB on the testbed, a 30% improvement over the best baseline, while reducing survey time by 55%.
fJKhNhHcvB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the physics-grounded Fresnel material parameterization for cross-band transfer and the real multi-site testbed.
fJKhNhHcvB.main_concern: Reviewers note that all compared baselines are frequency-agnostic (missing Friis-corrected, empirical indoor, or physically calibrated ray-tracing baselines) and that visual/depth geometry access is not matched across baselines.

Y2xuYYfFOD.one_liner: Coordinates decentralized power-grid topology control using physics-grounded LLM agents with counterfactual offline simulation memory.
Y2xuYYfFOD.problem: Decentralized power-grid topology control lacks mechanisms combining physical state assessment, inter-regional coordination, and past intervention evidence.
Y2xuYYfFOD.method: GridRefine equips regional LLM agents with local network graphs, counterfactual reasoning over offline simulation memories, local power-flow tool feedback, and neighbor proposal coordination prior to execution.
Y2xuYYfFOD.key_idea: Combines regional LLM counterfactual reasoning over past simulation outcomes with local power-flow tool checks and neighbor proposal coordination.
Y2xuYYfFOD.evidence: Evaluations on two power-grid benchmarks of different sizes across multiple LLM backbones.
Y2xuYYfFOD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers note that decentralized power-grid topology control is a timely, safety-critical problem and appreciate the detailed physical grounding.
Y2xuYYfFOD.main_concern: The main learned baseline (MAPPO) is unconverged and performs worse than doing nothing, while the justification for using LLMs over classical distributed optimization is lacking.

xNTcxjqcoC.one_liner: Unifies code/CLI, batched accessibility-tree diffs, and GUI channels into a single interface with stale-state guards for computer-use agents.
xNTcxjqcoC.problem: Screenshot-and-mouse computer-use interfaces impose unnecessary visual round trips and underexpose semantic accessibility and programmatic tools.
xNTcxjqcoC.method: Hybrid Computer Use (HCU) exposes programmatic, semantic (AX), and visual (GUI) channels together, featuring compact batched AX actions with diff feedback, cross-channel stale-state guards, and a channel-selection skill.
xNTcxjqcoC.key_idea: Unifies CLI/code, batched accessibility-tree actions with diff feedback, and GUI controls under stale-state guards for model-directed channel selection.
xNTcxjqcoC.evidence: Evaluations across multiple models on OSWorld 2.0 and OSWorld 1.0 benchmarks measuring task scores and interaction efficiency.
xNTcxjqcoC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that HCU provides a practical unified interface that reduces tool calls and improves interaction efficiency on computer-use benchmarks.
xNTcxjqcoC.main_concern: Individual AX mechanisms (batching, diffs, guards) are not ablated separately, positioning against prior hybrid agents is incomplete, and single-run OSWorld 2.0 gains are modest.

AjJBqSxb1z.one_liner: Feeds preference-weighted Pareto decisions back into lower-level objectives to steer non-convex multi-objective bilevel optimization.
AjJBqSxb1z.problem: Open-loop multi-objective bilevel pipelines fail to guide path-dependent lower-level responses toward preference-compatible Pareto branches.
AjJBqSxb1z.method: PAOS maintains a stateful selector that accumulates preference-weighted signals from upper-level Pareto subproblems and injects them into the lower-level training objective via implicit hypergradients.
AjJBqSxb1z.key_idea: Closes the bilevel loop by feeding stateful preference-weighted Pareto signals back into the lower-level objective.
AjJBqSxb1z.evidence: An analytical double-well problem and experiments on data hyper-cleaning, few-shot bilevel learning, PINNs, and medical image segmentation.
AjJBqSxb1z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the closed-loop double-well branch selection clean and appreciate the multi-domain evaluation and low memory footprint.
AjJBqSxb1z.main_concern: Dynamic feedback yields negligible gains over static preference scalarization on benchmarks like MNIST, while writing clarity and theoretical assumptions/baseline coverage need work.

I6XtP6BpbP.one_liner: Tests whether decodable Mandarin lexical tones in speech SSL models localize into reusable TopK sparse autoencoder features.
I6XtP6BpbP.problem: High linear probe accuracy does not distinguish whether linguistic contrasts in speech SSL models reside in reusable sparse features or distributed coordinates.
I6XtP6BpbP.method: Fits label-blind TopK sparse autoencoders to HuBERT, wav2vec 2.0, and WavLM representations of Mandarin speech, evaluating transfer to unseen syllables, refit recurrence, tone inventory recovery, and downstream readout influence against decoder-span and PCA controls.
I6XtP6BpbP.key_idea: Compares TopK sparse autoencoder activations against their decoder-direction spans and norm-matched PCA controls across held-out syllables and independent refits.
I6XtP6BpbP.evidence: Experiments on Mandarin speech (AISHELL-3) across layers of HuBERT, wav2vec 2.0, and a WavLM control.
I6XtP6BpbP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the rigorous evaluation protocol and the dissociation showing tone information resides in SAE decoder spans even when TopK activations miss it.
I6XtP6BpbP.main_concern: Reviewers note limited generalizability (one corpus, one tonal language, two main checkpoints) and incomplete isolation of TopK gating vs. feature absorption.

HNyMy0d2H0.one_liner: Uses joint proper scoring rules over two or more agents to elicit minimal decision-relevant outcome sets.
HNyMy0d2H0.problem: Single-agent proper scoring rules cannot strictly incentivize an agent to report the minimal set of outcomes needed for a principal's decision.
HNyMy0d2H0.method: Evaluates two or more agents jointly by rewarding an agent when it refines the reported outcome set in a way that alters the principal's decision, and extends the mechanism to large or continuous outcome spaces.
HNyMy0d2H0.key_idea: Incentivizes minimal decision-relevant outcome reporting by scoring multiple agents jointly and rewarding outcome-set refinements that change the principal's decision.
HNyMy0d2H0.evidence: Theoretical impossibility/possibility results plus experiments on minimal MNIST pixel masks for classification and LLM-generated unit tests for weak code judges.
HNyMy0d2H0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem interesting and appreciate the clean theoretical connection between joint scoring rules and debate/second opinions.
HNyMy0d2H0.main_concern: Reviewers cite unclear practical motivation over simpler alternatives, limited experimental scope (MNIST and small code tests), and organization issues.

O8hDBz5nN0.one_liner: Calibrates weakly-paired H&E-to-IHC virtual staining via optical-density-weighted graphs and unbalanced Gromov-Wasserstein alignment.
O8hDBz5nN0.problem: Adjacent tissue sections in weakly-paired H&E-to-IHC staining suffer from misalignment and expression heterogeneity, making spatial correspondence unreliable.
O8hDBz5nN0.method: PGLStain combines PECC, which weights spatially proposed candidate pairs and graph summaries by optical-density (OD) compatibility, with MRSA, which aligns unordered OD marginals and intra-image relations via unbalanced Gromov-Wasserstein transport.
O8hDBz5nN0.key_idea: Uses continuous optical-density compatibility to weight local candidate graphs and align global stain-state relations via unbalanced Gromov-Wasserstein transport.
O8hDBz5nN0.evidence: Evaluated on MIST and ACROBAT virtual staining benchmarks with component ablations.
O8hDBz5nN0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize that using optical density to handle misaligned weakly-paired virtual staining is well motivated.
O8hDBz5nN0.main_concern: Reviewers highlight inconsistent results on ACROBAT (trailing baselines on FID and |Bias mIoD|), heavy combination of modules with unclear individual necessity, and reliance on predicted IHC OD.

YzRib0v2mm.one_liner: Simulates latency, throughput, communication, and memory of HE/MPC private LLM serving without running cryptography.
YzRib0v2mm.problem: Evaluating cryptographic and hardware configurations for private HE/MPC LLM serving is prohibitively slow because single encrypted runs take minutes to hours.
YzRib0v2mm.method: CipherScope counts homomorphic and MPC operations, models HE segment repricing, KV-state growth, preprocessing supply waiting, and batching compatibility, and simulates end-to-end serving cost in microseconds to milliseconds.
YzRib0v2mm.key_idea: Models HE/MPC operator placement, preprocessing supply queues, and growing KV state analytically to predict private LLM serving costs without executing cryptography.
YzRib0v2mm.evidence: Validated against real CPU MPC executions from BERT-tiny to LLaMA-7B dimensions and a four-user GPT-2 generation schedule replay.
YzRib0v2mm.claimed_gains: Predicts communication within 1%, BERT forward-pass latency within ~2–12%, and four-user GPT-2 generation replay within 2.1%, while all-HE and LLaMA-specific layers show 15–25% timing errors.
YzRib0v2mm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the careful engineering, honest reporting of failure cases, and practical motivation of avoiding costly cryptographic runs.
YzRib0v2mm.main_concern: Reviewers question the utility of CPU-only validation when private LLM serving targets GPUs, and ask for clearer novelty boundaries against prior cost models like CostCO, CryptOracle, and Vidur.

6h7YWJMR5U.one_liner: Provides a JIT-compiled JAX benchmark suite for multi-task LTL reinforcement learning across six algorithms and four environments.
6h7YWJMR5U.problem: Inconsistent implementations, task distributions, and slow execution hinder fair comparison and statistical reliability in LTL-based multi-task RL.
6h7YWJMR5U.method: Jaxolotl precompiles symbolic LTL task representations into static arrays to enable end-to-end JIT-compiled training and evaluation across six algorithms and four environments under a standardized protocol.
6h7YWJMR5U.key_idea: Precompiles symbolic LTL formula-progression closures into static JAX arrays to enable full JIT compilation of multi-task RL training.
6h7YWJMR5U.evidence: Benchmarked across six LTL-RL algorithms and four existing environments including ZoneEnv, with stress tests on proposition scaling.
6h7YWJMR5U.claimed_gains: Achieves end-to-end speedups of up to 220x (e.g., reducing DeepLTL training on ZoneEnv from 14 hours to 8 minutes).
6h7YWJMR5U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that Jaxolotl delivers impressive JAX speedups and useful standardized infrastructure for the LTL-RL community.
6h7YWJMR5U.main_concern: Reviewers note limited research novelty beyond engineering existing algorithms/environments in JAX, lack of challenging new domains, and minor formalism errors.

tbUUMVxz5L.one_liner: Proves that a learned linear skip connection eliminates spurious local minima in shallow ReLU networks with planar teacher features.
tbUUMVxz5L.problem: Spurious local minima can persist in shallow ReLU teacher-student networks even under arbitrary overparameterization.
tbUUMVxz5L.method: The authors analyze the Gaussian population loss of bias-free shallow ReLU networks, proving via interlacing arguments that adding a learned linear skip removes all spurious minima with nonnegative student weights for planar teachers, while constructing a 3-neuron counterexample without skips.
tbUUMVxz5L.key_idea: Uses interlacing analysis of Gaussian population loss to show a linear skip connection forces student features into the teacher subspace and removes spurious minima.
tbUUMVxz5L.evidence: Purely theoretical proofs in the two-layer bias-free ReLU teacher-student setting.
tbUUMVxz5L.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper proves a clean theoretical separation showing skip connections remove spurious minima where overparameterization alone fails.
tbUUMVxz5L.main_concern: Reviewers note restrictive assumptions (planar 2D teacher features, bias-free shallow networks, nonnegative student weights, population loss without gradient dynamics) and a complete lack of empirical validation.

qdox7Bc4hA.one_liner: Evaluates whether autonomous driving VLMs support safe decisions with grounded risk awareness via the SAR diagnostic protocol.
qdox7Bc4hA.problem: Autonomous driving benchmarks focus on final action correctness, masking models that produce safe recommendations without recognizing underlying risks.
qdox7Bc4hA.method: The authors build RADIUS-Drive via controllable scenario generation and introduce the SAR protocol (S-Pass, A-Pass, R-Pass, and cross-phase G-Pass) to score safety, risk awareness, and decision reasoning.
qdox7Bc4hA.key_idea: Decomposes driving evaluation into stage-wise safety, risk awareness, and reasoning gates (SAR) paired with a cross-phase grounding score (G-Pass).
qdox7Bc4hA.evidence: Benchmarks 15 VLMs and four VLM-based autonomous driving agents on 550 image-based scenarios.
qdox7Bc4hA.claimed_gains: Across 15 VLMs and four AD agents, G-Pass scores range from 0.21 to 0.63.
qdox7Bc4hA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating risk-aware reasoning beyond final action accuracy addresses an important gap in safety-critical driving.
qdox7Bc4hA.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the reliance on 550 static single images in a simplified 2D simulator without temporal inputs, heuristic/unclear G-Pass definitions, and evaluating A-Pass/R-Pass on different per-model collision-free subsets.

u7THv0qTCi.one_liner: Improves 1-bit LLM post-training quantization via output-alignment constrained by token similarity preservation.
u7THv0qTCi.problem: Naive output-driven 1-bit LLM quantization degrades performance due to cross-layer error accumulation and anisotropic representation distortion.
u7THv0qTCi.method: The authors formulate output alignment as a constrained optimization problem that minimizes reconstruction error while preserving token affinity, solved via conditional closed-form updates on the final layer of each block.
u7THv0qTCi.key_idea: Adds a token-affinity regularization term to output-driven 1-bit weight refinement to curb anisotropic representation distortion.
u7THv0qTCi.evidence: Evaluated on OPT, LLaMA, and Qwen families for perplexity and downstream non-generation tasks against ARB-X and ARB-RC.
u7THv0qTCi.claimed_gains: Improves all 18 perplexity comparisons and all 24 downstream task comparisons against ARB-RC, with average gains of 2.55, 2.77, and 5.06 percentage points on three LLaMA models.
u7THv0qTCi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge consistent empirical perplexity and downstream task gains over ARB-RC across multiple LLM families.
u7THv0qTCi.main_concern: Reviewers note overlap with prior work, a gap between cosine-similarity motivation and the unnormalized Frobenius affinity surrogate, restriction to the final block layer, and no generation-task evaluation.

GmF5ug8JsI.one_liner: Optimizes executable multimodal attribute and relation refinement programs using multi-agent search, paired replay, and online policy adaptation.
GmF5ug8JsI.problem: Generic data preparation pipelines use fixed quality criteria and fail to adapt both record attributes and inter-record relations to specific downstream tasks.
GmF5ug8JsI.method: MATAR uses a multi-agent framework to search executable attribute and relation programs via task-adaptive tool optimization, compares revisions under matched-training paired replay, and guides proposals with an online controller.
GmF5ug8JsI.key_idea: Searches executable attribute and graph-relation refinement programs independently using downstream paired replay evaluation and an online experiential controller.
GmF5ug8JsI.evidence: Evaluated across eight datasets spanning four downstream tasks with ablations on TATO, PRE, and EPA plus cross-dataset transfer tests.
GmF5ug8JsI.claimed_gains: Across eight datasets spanning four tasks, MATAR achieves an average relative gain of 23.9% over the strongest baseline per dataset.
GmF5ug8JsI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formulating multimodal data preparation as task-driven optimization over both features and inter-record relations is useful.
GmF5ug8JsI.main_concern: Reviewers note that gains may stem from added neighbor-graph construction capabilities unavailable to sample-filtering baselines, and question the MM cosine-similarity metric and unclear novelty over prior workflow optimization.

MneZtnwovr.one_liner: Establishes impossibility results, tight Ω(log T/√T) lower bounds, and bounded-iterate O(1/√T) rates for AdaGrad in stochastic convex optimization.
MneZtnwovr.problem: The exact convergence behavior of AdaGrad and AdaGrad-Norm in stochastic convex optimization—regarding last iterates, high-probability rates, and logarithmic factors—remains incomplete.
MneZtnwovr.method: The authors prove that neither AdaGrad nor AdaGrad-Norm admits a universal last-iterate rate under sub-Gaussian noise and bounded iterates, and that bounded variance alone cannot yield high-probability average-iterate rates or expectation convergence without bounded iterates. They construct Ω(log T/√T) lower bounds under sub-Gaussian noise and show O(1/√T) rates under an ABC bounded-iterate condition.
MneZtnwovr.key_idea: Constructing counterexamples and lower bounds characterizing when AdaGrad and AdaGrad-Norm fail last-iterate or high-probability convergence in stochastic convex optimization.
MneZtnwovr.evidence: Theoretical proofs (Theorems 3.1–3.5) and one-dimensional smooth convex lower-bound constructions.
MneZtnwovr.claimed_gains: Constructs Ω(log T/√T) lower bounds for AdaGrad and AdaGrad-Norm under sub-Gaussian noise and achieves O(1/√T) rates under bounded iterates and an ABC condition.
MneZtnwovr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the negative last-iterate and logarithmic lower-bound results fill meaningful theoretical gaps in understanding AdaGrad.
MneZtnwovr.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the disorganized presentation across shifting assumptions and note that some abstract claims overstate horizon-dependent worst-case constructions or lack matching upper bounds.

HepHYPmDSa.one_liner: Generalizes state space models with a learnable Caputo fractional derivative order approximated via FFT contour sampling and streaming tail compression.
HepHYPmDSa.problem: Standard first-order state space models encode memory through exponential decay, lacking an explicit learnable mechanism for algebraic long-time history weighting.
HepHYPmDSa.method: The authors introduce fractional-order SSMs with a learnable Caputo derivative order α ∈ (0, 1], yielding algebraic decay for α < 1. To avoid quadratic history cost, they discretize via convolution quadrature and realize parallel training via contour-sampled FFT convolution and streaming inference via a recent-state buffer plus sum-of-exponentials tail approximation.
HepHYPmDSa.key_idea: Parameterizing a learnable Caputo fractional derivative order in SSMs with contour-FFT parallel training and constant-cache sum-of-exponentials streaming inference.
HepHYPmDSa.evidence: Evaluated on Long Range Arena (LRA) and synthetic tasks alongside mathematical derivations.
HepHYPmDSa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extending S4/S4D parallel and streaming machinery to fractional-order Caputo SSMs is mathematically rigorous and well-derived.
HepHYPmDSa.main_concern: Reviewers point out insufficient baselines (missing Mamba, Mamba-2, S5, FRACTAL, LinOSS), overlap with prior fractional SSMs (LongSpike, FRACTAL), and no evaluation on language modeling tasks.

DibLRSV1nR.one_liner: Couples bidirectional recurrent scans, survival memory decay, and local routing into a normalized transport operator for generative time-series forecasters.
DibLRSV1nR.problem: Existing generative time-series forecasters rely on generic backbones for cross-horizon interaction without normalized accounting of information routing across forecast steps.
DibLRSV1nR.method: CoBiST is a generator-agnostic operator where a shared gate produces directional preferences and one-step survival probabilities to allocate a normalized budget across causal/anti-causal recurrent scans and a direct-local branch. It admits an exact row-stochastic augmented kernel, a linear-time semiseparable realization, and a horizon-independent Lipschitz bound.
DibLRSV1nR.key_idea: Coupling directional preferences and survival decay via a single gate to form a row-stochastic, linear-time bidirectional cross-horizon transport operator.
